Christos eventually created a successful fashion line called Drendie Girl. The couple used the profits from that business to buy up property.
Lazari Investments owns more than 3 million square feet of commercial real estate in London, mostly office space that it rents out.
Maritsa was a cofounder of the real estate business and serves as a director. Her three children are also involved in the company.
abouts: In 2017, the family established a charity foundation in honor of Christos, donating an initial $4.9 million with plans to invest more in the future.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Frank Fertitta III and his brother, Lorenzo, made the bulk of their fortune through mixed martial arts promoter UFC.
The brothers bought UFC for $2 million in 2001; it sold to an investment group led by WME/IMG for $4 billion in 2016.
They sold their remaining stakes in UFC in August 2017 at a $5 billion valuation.
The Fertittas took their casino business, Red Rock Resorts, public in 2016. It was founded by their father.
They each pledged $7.5 million in 2016 to NYU's Stern School of Business for a scholarship for veterans.
abouts: His daughter Kelley got married at a lavish wedding at Red Rock Resorts in September 2018 where Bruno Mars sang.
Frank and Lorenzo got hooked on martial arts after taking weekly lessons in their casino's basement. Soon after, they bought UFC.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mahima Datla is the managing director of Biological E, a privately held vaccine producer, in which she holds a controlling stake.

The Hyderabad-based company's portfolio includes Corbevax, a Covid-19 vaccine developed in partnership with Texas Children's Hospital Center for Vaccine Development and Baylor College of Medicine in Houston.
Biological E has 10 vaccines pre-qualified by the World Health Organization including those against polio, tetanus and measles. It exports vaccines to more than 130 countries.
Biological E was founded in 1953 by her paternal and maternal grandfathers.
abouts: Datla has a bachelor's degree in business management from London's Webster University. She became managing director in 2013.
In 2022, she won a nearly decade-long battle with her mother over the company's ownership that went up to India's Supreme Court.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Vince McMahon grew World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) from a regional operation into a global phenomenon.
A third-generation wrestling promoter, McMahon grew up in a trailer park in North Carolina and joined his father's small wrestling company in 1972.
He purchased the business 10 years later and turned it into a giant. He took WWE (then named WWF) public in 1999.
In 2023, McMahon agreed to merge WWE with UFC to form TKO Group Holdings.
He stepped down as executive chairman of TKO in 2024 amid sexual misconduct allegations, which he has denied.
abouts: Donald Trump picked McMahon's wife, Linda, to lead the Small Business Administration during his first term and to run the Department of Education in his second term.
McMahon's daughter Stephanie, the chief brand officer for WWE, is married to professional wrestler Paul Levesque, better known as Triple H.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liu Weiping chairs snack food maker WL Delicious.
WL is headquartered in the central Chinese city of Luohe.
Liu is a graduate of Southwest University in Chongqing, China, where he was majored in management.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jose Roberto Marinho and his two billionaire brothers, Joao Roberto and Roberto Irineu, inherited control of Globo, Brazil's largest media group.
Their grandfather started Globo in 1925 by launching a newspaper. He died 25 days after the first issue was published so his oldest son took over.
Globo Group owns Brazil's largest TV broadcaster, Rede Globo; Brazil's largest newspaper company, and Globosat, Brazil's largest pay TV provider.
In 1991, Jose Roberto founded CBN, the first Brazilian radio to broadcast 24 hours of news.
Jose Roberto leads the family's philanthropy through Roberto Marinho Foundation, which created the world's first museum to dedicated to Portuguese.
abouts: In 1992, he founded Acqua Institute, an entity that focuses on the preservation of water resources.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joao Roberto Marinho and his two billionaire brothers, Jose Roberto and Roberto Irineu, inherited control of Globo, Brazil's largest media group.
Their grandfather Irineu Marinho launched O Globo newspaper in 1925; he died 25 days after the first issue was published and his oldest son took over.
Globo Group includes Brazil's largest broadcaster, Rede Globo; Brazil's largest newspaper company and Globosat, Brazil's largest pay TV provider.
Joao Roberto worked at O Globo, one of Brazil's most influential newspapers. He held a number of positions before becoming vice president in 1982.
Joao Roberto is now the executive president of Grupo Globo and the chairman of the board of directors.
abouts: The Marinho family contributed to the establishment of museums in Brazil such as Museum of Tomorrow, The Football Museum, and Museum of the Portuguese Language.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: The son of a wealthy art collector, Nicolas Berggruen was born in Paris and moved to the U.S. to attend New York University.
He first worked in real estate for Bass Brothers Enterprises before founding Berggruen Holdings in 1985 to manage his investments.
In 1988, he cofounded Alpha Investment Management, a fund of hedge funds operation that was sold to Safra Bank in 2004 for an undisclosed amount.
His Berggruen Holdings owns office buildings and apartments in Berlin, Germany; Portland, Oregon and Albany, New York.
He is the founder and chairman of The Berggruen Institute, a think tank focused on developing ideas for the future of democracy and capitalism.
abouts: A bachelor, Berggruen has settled down in Los Angeles with his 2 children, born in 2016 through an egg donor and 2 separate surrogates.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Theodore Rachmat, known as Teddy, founded Triputra group in 1998; its business lines now include agriculture, manufacturing and mining.
Rachmat owns a minority stake in listed coal company Alamtri Resources Indonesia, formerly Adaro Energy, where he is vice president commissioner.
He started out at automotive group Astra International, founded by his uncle William Soeryadjaya, in 1968. He eventually became CEO.
His son Ariano is vice president director and deputy CEO of Alamtri Resources; son Arif Patrick, who worked for GE for seven years, is cofounder and chairman of palm oil giant Triputra Agro Persada.
Alamtri Resources plans to spin off and list its thermal coal unit Adaro Andalan Indonesia in December 2024, raising up to $291 million.
abouts: Triputra means three children.
Rachmat was awarded the Bintang Jasa Utama medal of honor from Indonesian president Joko Widodo in 2019.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Dorrance is an heir to the Campbell's Soup fortune; his grandfather invented the Campbell's formula for condensed soup.
His relatives are still the company's largest shareholders, but he sold his stake in the mid-1990's and emigrated to Ireland.
His move was presumably timed to avoid capital gains taxes when he sold his Campbell's stake.
The Irish government reportedly gave Dorrance citizenship in 1995 when he spent $1.5 million planting trees.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: David Wertheim is the son of the late Moshe Wertheim (d. 2016), founder of the Central Bottling Company, Israel's Coca Cola bottler. He owns 63% of the company.
Before he died, Moshe Wertheim gave the bottling business, as well as his shares in Mizrahi Tefahot Bank and Alony Hetz,.to David and his sister Drorit,

In 2018, he purchased his billionaire sister's Alony Hetz shares, sold them because of Israeli anti-monopoly rules, and is controlling shareholder of Mizrahi Tefahot, the country's third-largest bank.
He founded and controls Keshet Media Group, which controls TV channel Keshet 12, CH12 News, and websites Mako.co.il and N12.co.il.
He is the founder and CEO of M. Wertheim (Holdings) Ltd., whose investments include publicly traded Alony Hetz Properties & Investments.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ralph Dommermuth leads United Internet, one of Europe's leading internet specialists serving home users and businesses.
He launched United Internet's predecessor company, 1&1 AG, in 1988 with a borrowed desk and $285,000 saved from working as a computer salesman.
1&1 became the first internet company listed on Germany's stock exchange for high-tech companies, the Neuer Markt, in 1998.
United Internet, of which Dommermuth owns around 50%, has expanded its offerings to include mobile telecommunication services and data centers.
abouts: Dommermuth owns a 5% stake in Borussia Dortmund, a soccer club in the German Bundesliga.
Dommermuth is married to the fashion designer Judith Dommermuth, who sits on Borussia Dortmund's supervisory board.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Neal Blue is chairman and CEO of $3.1 billion (est. sales) General Atomics, a defense company based in San Diego.
The company is best known as the manufacturer of the Predator drone, one of the first drones to fly over Afghanistan after 9/11.
The largest private government contractor in the U.S., GA's clients include foreign nations such as Italy, Spain, and the UAE.
With his brother Linden, he bought the then nuclear energy company from Chevron for a reported $60 million in 1986.
After graduating from Yale, Blue served in the U.S. Air Force as a nuclear weapons custodian.
abouts: Linden Blue, who owns a smaller stake and is a vice president at the company, is worth $800 million.
In 1956, Neal, then 21, and Linden, 20, raised $3,000 to fly a single-propeller plan across Central and South America. Life Magazine put them on its cover.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Newmark Grubb Knight Frank (Commericial Real Estate Company)

bios: Donald Trump tapped Howard Lutnick to co-chair his transition team, then named him America's 41st secretary of commerce.
Lutnick lost both parents as a teenager, leaving him and his two siblings to take care of each other.
After graduating from Haverford College, he got a job at the Wall Street firm of Cantor Fitzgerald, where he became a favorite of founder Bernie Cantor and eventually took control of the firm.
The September 11, 2001 attack on the World Trade Center killed 658 of Cantor Fitzgerald's 960 New York employees, including Lutnick's younger brother, Gary.
Thanks to an electronic trading business and savvy dealmaking, Lutnick rebuilt his empire, which employed more than 14,000 people by the time he joined the Trump administration in 2025.
abouts: Lutnick's rise to power at Cantor Fitzgerald sparked a fight with the family of his mentor, Bernie Cantor, whose widow barred Lutnick from her husband's cemetery.
Lutnick lived in a Trump Palace penthouse before purchasing a townhouse next door to Jeffrey Epstein, with whom a Lutnick spokesperson says he had no association.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sophie Luise Fielmann is the daughter of Guenther Fielmann, the founder of Fielmann Group AG.
Together with her brother Marc, who heads the company as CEO after the death of their father in 2023, she is the majority shareholder of the company.
Fielmann is one of the biggest optician chains across Europe with revenues of more than EUR 2 billion.
Some 24,000 people work for Fielmann across more than 1,000 locations.
Her father Guenther openend the first store in Cuxhaven in 1972.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Former finance professional Abhay Soi is chairman and managing director of Max Healthcare Institute, India's second-largest listed hospital chain by revenue.
Soi started his career at the erstwhile Arthur Andersen and later worked for EY and KPMG.
Soi got his entrepreneurial break in 2010 when he took over a struggling 650-bed hospital in Delhi and set up Radiant Life Care.
Radiant was merged with Max in June 2020 and listed two months later.
He's looking to double the number of hospital beds by 2029.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sunil Vachani is the founder and chairman of India-listed Dixon Technologies.
Vachani borrowed two million rupees ($27,600) from his father to set up the company in 1993 to manufacture TV sets.
The company makes products such as smartphones, washing machines and TVs for a range of clients including Samsung, Panasonic and Xiaomi.
The Noida-based company was listed in 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: YTO Express Group Co., Class A
YTO Express Group Co., Class A

bios: Shi Yuzhu is chairman of Giant Interactive, an online game developer and operator in China.
Giant, which had traded in New York, was relisted on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016 through a reverse merger with Chongqing New Century Cruise.
Shi was a revered entrepreneur in China in the 1980s when he first made his fortune in computer hardware.
A graduate of Zhejiang University, Shi got his degree in math.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Until 2022 Andrei Bokarev runs Transmashholding (TMH), Russia's biggest producer of rolling stock for railways and subway systems.
Bokarev previously headed Krutrade AG, which ran the export operations of the Kuzbassrazrezugol coal company.
Bokarev is a partner in most of his senior partner Iskander Makhmudov's projects including TMH, Kuzbassrazrezugol and Ural Mining Metallurgical Company (UMMC).
He owns half of Ust-Luga Oil company, largest oil terminal in Europe with capacity of 30 million tons per year.
abouts: In June of 2018 Alexei Krivoruchko, Bokarev's former partner, was appointed deputy minister of defense of Russia.
UMMC spent $100 Million on constructing ice arena Shayba for the Sochi Olympics, which it gave to the government after the olympics.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Najib Mikati cofounded Beirut-based investment firm M1 Group.
Mikati currently served as the prime minister of Lebanon until February 2025, a position he previously held from 2011 to 2014 and briefly in 2005.
Mikati and his billionaire brother Taha founded Investcom in 1982, selling satellite phones at the height of Lebanon's civil war.
They expanded into Africa where they built cellphone towers in Ghana, Liberia and Benin, among other countries.
In 2005, Investcom went public on the London Stock Exchange, and in 2009, South Africa's MTN bought the Mikatis' stake for $3.6 billion.
abouts: In 2005, Investcom was the largest IPO of a Middle Eastern company in London, and the first stock to trade on the Dubai Financial Market.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Taha Mikati cofounded Beirut-based holding company M1 Group.
Its investments include stakes in South African telecom firm MTN, fashion retailer Pepe Jeans and prime real estate in New York, London and Monaco.
Mikati and his billionaire brother Najib founded Investcom in 1982, selling satellite phones at the height of Lebanon's civil war.
They expanded into Africa where they built cellphone towers in Ghana, Liberia and Benin, among other countries.
In 2005, Investcom went public on the London Stock Exchange, and in 2009, South Africa's MTN bought the Mikatis' stake for $3.6 billion.
abouts: Mikati bought a bunch of satellite phones and sold them to friends and associates in Beirut in the early 80s for $50,000 apiece.
Mikati's son Azmi is the CEO of M1 Group.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: William "Bill" Chisholm, a private equity executive, is leading a group of investors to buy the Boston Celtics NBA team for $6.1 billion.
Chisholm is the managing partner of STG Partners, a software-focused Silicon Valley private equity firm with about $12 billion in assets under management.
He cofounded Symphony Technology Group, the predecessor to STG, in 2002 with software billionaire Romesh Wadhwani.
Chisholm has worked in Silicon Valley for decades but grew up near Boston and has been a lifelong Celtics fan.
The Celtics' current CEO and governor, Wyc Grousbeck, will stay in his roles through the 2027-2028 season.
abouts: Prior to Symphony Technology Group, Chisholm worked in venture capital and as a management consultant at Bain & Co.
Chisholm was a member of the varsity soccer team at Dartmouth College that won Ivy League titles in 1988 and 1990.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mikhail Shelkov is the former head of the investment division of state-owned Rostec, which controlled military contractors in Russia.
Shelkov's former boss Sergey Chemezov, CEO of Rostec, is a member of Putin's inner circle, befriending Russia's president in Germany in the 1980s.
From 2012 to 2014, Shelkov and partners bought a controlling stake in VSMPO-AVISMA Corporation from Rostec and Gazprombank.
VSMPO-AVISMA is the world's largest titanium producer for the aerospace industry, which once counted Boeing, Airbus and Rolls-Royce as customers; In 2022 they ceased sourcing from the company.
In 2022 he bought aluminum factory in the Samara region from Arconic, a former division of Alcoa, stopped operations in Russia, for $230m.
abouts: In 2019 Shelkov launched Empathy Foundation, which supports school teachers in Russia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: America Movil S.A.B. de C.V. (Class B)
Grupo Carso S.A.B. de C.V. (Series A
Grupo Financiero Inbursa S.A.B. de C
Grupo Posadas SAB de CV Class A

bios: Fernando Chico Pardo started his first company in Mexico City at age 27, a stock brokerage called Acciones y Asesoría Bursátil.
That brokerage later became part of Grupo Financiero Inbursa, a banking and financial group controlled by Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim.
After he left Inbursa in 2003, Chico Pardo became a controlling shareholder in Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (Asur), which operates nine airports in Mexico and one in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
He also runs private equity fund Promecap, which has acquired interests in or provided funding for a variety of Mexican companies.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lee Yeow Chor inherited stakes in IOI group, a palm oil and property empire built by his father Lee Sin Cheng.
He and his brother Lee Yeow Seng run the group.
Lee Yeow Chor is group managing director and chief executive of IOI Corporation, the main listed arm.
He holds a law degree from King's College, London.
His brother Lee Yeow Seng, who also studied law, is the CEO of IOI Properties.
abouts: The late Lee grew up on a rubber plantation where his father ran a Chinese food shop.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Fabien Pinckaers created Odoo, his second company, when he was a 22-year-old student who needed a software to manage the flow of beer kegs in a student party room on campus.
Odoo operates in more than 10 countries including the U.S and Dubai, had revenue of over 240 million euros in 2022 and has more than 7 million users.
Pinckaers read his first book on Toyota's business management at 13 years old and didn't use internet until he was at university.
He developed his first business management software at 13 and sold it to the Belgian Writers' Association and to green transports.
Tech entrepreneur and fellow billionaire Xaviel Niel owns a minority stake in Odoo.
abouts: Pinckaers became Belgium's youngest billionaire in 2023.
His company owns a lab on wheels, a truck called the "LabOdoo" that travels in Belgium to visit schools and universities to teach business management to students.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chan Tan Ching-fen is the wife of the late Hong Kong property tycoon Chan Tseng-hsi. She controls the largest shareholding in Hang Lung Group.
Hang Lung was run by her eldest son, Ronnie, until his retirement in 2024. His son Adriel took over as chairman.
Ronnie's brother Gerald leads the family's Morningside Group, a private equity and venture capital investor.
abouts: Her father Tan Hui-kuk was a second cousin of Sun Yat-sen, the founding father of the Republic of China, and provided Sun with financial support.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gilles Martin is the executive chairman of Eurofins Scientific, a Luxembourg-based laboratory services company listed on the French stock exchange.
Martin, who founded the original lab in 1987, owns an estimated 22% of the company through the family's holding company Analytical Bioventures.
His brother Yves-Loic owns an estimated 10% stake. He served as CTO from 1998 until 2015 and now is a board member.
Eurofins has 900 labs in 61 countries and is prominent in food and pharmaceutical products testing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Friede Springer inherited a stake in media giant Axel Springer Verlag from her husband, Axel, following his death in 1985.
Hired as the nanny of his two sons, Springer eventually married Axel, who trained her to take over the business.
Among the largest publishing houses in Europe, Axel Springer is active in over 40 countries. Its newspapers include Bild and Die Welt.
The company acquired TV news station N24 (since rebranded as Welt) and the New York-based digital news outlet Business Insider (now renamed Insider) in 2015.
Axel Springer went public in 1985. In 2020, it went private again in a KKR-funded buyout.
abouts: To ensure continuity, in 2020 Friede Springer gave a 15% stake in Axel Springer to CEO Mathias Doepfner and sold him an additional 4.1%.
After the delisting and the gift and sale to Doepfner, she now holds 22.5% of the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Olivier Pomel is the CEO of Datadog, a cloud monitoring company he cofounded with Alexis Le-Quoc, the firm's chief technology officer, in 2010.
Datadog listed on the Nasdaq in September 2019, raising nearly $650 million and nabbing a $10.9 billion market cap on its first day of trading.
Pomel and Le-Quoc became billionaires in May 2020 after a blockbuster earnings release sent shares soaring; Pomel owns 4% of Datadog shares.
The French natives met while undergraduates at Ecole Centrale Paris, where both received Master's degrees in computer science.
Before building Datadog, the duo worked together at New York-based firm Wireless Generation, which was acquired by News Corp in 2010.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Erwin Franz Mueller owns an eponymous drugstore chain with some 880 stores across seven European countries and annual revenue of around $4.4 billion.
The business dates to 1953, when Mueller opened a hairdressing shop in his home in Ulm, Germany.
In recent years, working conditions at his drugstores have been the subject of scrutiny in media reports.
In August 2022, shortly before his 90th birthday, M?ller retook the helm after CEO G?nther Helm suddenly departed.
In 2017, he founded the Erwin-Mueller-Privatstiftung as a company foundation in Linz, Austria to deal with his eventual succession.
abouts: Mueller is believed to have pledged more $1 billion of real estate assets - including a house and a golf course in Mallorca - as collateral in a 2013 tax dispute.
He married his second wife and former secretary, Anita, in 2006. Around the same time, his son Reinhard left the company's management team.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sam Gance started his first pharmacy in 1972 with his brother Jack Gance.
He went on to acquire a stake in the Chemist Warehouse pharmacy chain that Jack cofounded with Mario Verrocchi in 1995 with five pharmacies.
Today Chemist Warehouse has annual revenue of A$3.3 billion and over 600 outlets across Australia, China, Dubai, Ireland and New Zealand.
Chemist Warehouse dropped its plan for an IPO opting for  a merger with ASX-listed Sigma Healthcare, which was completed in February 2025.
abouts: In 1976, the brothers established a successful sunglasses, perfume and suntan lotion company-Le Specs and Le Tan-which they sold in 1991.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Aspire Capital Holding for Financial Investments

bios: Emad Al Muhaidib is vice chairman of Al Muhaidib Group, a Dammam, Saudi Arabia-based family-owned conglomerate.
Al Muhaidib Group invests in companies across consumer products, infrastructure, construction, real estate and finance; Emad owns 28% of the company.
The group was founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir, who started out as a food trader before expanding into building materials and real estate.
Emad and his brothers Essam and Sulaiman took over after Abdulkadir's death in 1996; they share ownership of the group with 4 other family members.
Al Muhaidib Group owns shares in at least 16 publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia and Egypt.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Frank VanderSloot founded and runs Melaleuca, which makes more than 450 products ranging from health supplements to eco-friendly household cleaners.
Melaleuca sells them direct from the factory to more than one million consumers every month through its online store.
Born into a poor farming family, he ran the farm while his father worked a railroad job, then lived in a laundromat to pay his way through school.
He is a major landowner -- with an estimated 148,000 acres across Idaho, Utah and Montana -- and he runs a leading purebred angus cattle operation.
He is also an active political donor, giving millions to Republicans. He was a national finance co-chair for Mitt Romney's two presidential bids.
abouts: VanderSloot is an avid indoor rower and holds six world records.
In 2019, VanderSloot started what is now a $1 million fund to help Idahoans defend themselves from aggressive medical debt collection tactics.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Paper magnate Patrick Lee was born in Hainan, came to Hong Kong as an orphan and learned the art of trading from an uncle.
After early success in handbags Lee noticed that he was having trouble finding boxes for his exports, leading him to start a paper company.
Today, Lee & Man Paper is an industrial-packaging behemoth in China. Sons Raymond and Edmond run operations.
Lee also ventured into chemical production and set up Lee & Man Chemical in 2006, now headed by another son Norman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bill Stone started financial-software firm SS&C Technologies in 1986 with the $20,000 he had saved from his days as a KPMG executive.
His product became popular among asset managers, bankers and insurers who wanted to electronically manage their books.
He guided the firm to an IPO in 1996, but the dot-com crash nearly crippled the company in 2001.
Stone refocused and added services such as data centers, then took the company private in 2005.
In 2011, a resurgent SS&C went public again; Stone remains the firm's largest individual shareholder, with a 14% stake.
abouts: Between June 1999 and December 2001, SS&C went from 610 to 250 employees, as the markets crashed.
The Evansville, Indiana native was the captain of his high school football team.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cai Dongchen is the chairman and CEO of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group.
CSPC's bulk drug products include vitamin C, antibiotics and caffeine.
The company's manufacturing facilities are located mainly in the eastern Chinese city of Shijiazhuang.
Cai holds a MBA degree from Nankai University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Nandan Nilekani is the cofounder of tech giant Infosys and its non-executive chairman since 2017.
Nilekani, who left Infosys in 2009, was brought back in 2017 after a boardroom shakeup at the company and the sudden departure of its CEO.
Nilekani is credited with building Aadhaar, India's mammoth identity card scheme, during his tenure as chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India.
The tech magnate, who still has shares in Infosys, has backed Fundamentum, a venture capital fund aimed at technology companies.
In 2023, he donated $38 million to the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, his alma mater, to expand research and infrastructure.
abouts: He teamed up with Ratan Tata, former chairman of the Tata Group, to start Avanti Finance to provide microloans to the poor.
He and wife Rohini have signed the Giving Pledge. They run separate philanthropic arms, which focus on areas such as urbanization and biodiversity.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Oprah Winfrey transitioned her hit talk show, which ran for 25 years until 2011, into a media and business empire.
Reinvested, the profits from her show, plus profits from films like The Color Purple, Beloved and Selma (which her Harpo Productions coproduced) add up to an estimated more than $2.5 billion.
In 2011, Winfrey launched cable channel OWN. She sold most of her stake in the network to owner Warner Bros. Discovery in 2020 in exchange for shares in the company.
Her sprawling real estate portfolio includes homes in California and over a dozen properties including 2,100 acres of land in Hawaii.
abouts: Winfrey overcame a tough childhood, born to a teen mother in rural Mississippi and raised without indoor plumbing.
Winfrey has focused her philanthropy on education, including supporting a girls' school in South Africa.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Caroline Hagen Kjos became chairman of her family's Canica AS holding company in 2014.
The Swiss resident also received a majority stake in Canica at at that time.
Her father, Norwegian billionaire Stein Erik Hagen, founded discount supermarket Rimi with his father in the 1970s.
Rimi merged with Sweden's ICA group in 1998 and later with Dutch retailer Ahold; Hagen eventually sold his stake, forming Canica AS with the proceeds.
Canica AS now has a number of investments across Scandinavia, including consumer goods manufacturer Orkla ASA and hardware store chain Jernia.
abouts: Caroline has a bachelor's degree in business administration from the Parsons School of Design in New York.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lyu Yixiong is the CEO of Shanghai Chicmax Cosmetic, a cosmetics supplier in China.
Chicmax went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in December 2022.
Lyu completed executive management training at the Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Coates is the co-CEO of U.K. company Bet365, one of the world's largest online gambling businesses.
He joined his billionaire sister and co-CEO, Denise, in 2001 to launch Bet365 after she sold some of their father's betting shops.
Bet365 has since become a global player, with over 53 million customers across 200 countries; John owns a quarter of the firm.
In July 2015, he became the vice chairman of English Premier League's Stoke City Football Club, in which Bet365 has a majority stake.
abouts: Coates studied law at Bristol University and started his career as an attorney.
Bet365 handles more than $65 billion of bets a year.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mao Geping is chairman of his eponymous company Mao Geping Cosmetics, based in Hangzhou, China.
He took the company public in Hong Kong in 2024, raising over $300 million in the IPO.
The cosmetics brand competes with international labels in China's premium market, offering products such as $50 foundations and $30 eye shadow palettes.
Mao initially studied Chinese opera performance but later went into cosmetics. He set up his own brand in 2000.
The mogul's wife, Wang Liqun, is the company's vice chairman. His two sisters are both directors.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lam and her husband Yeung Kin-man own Hong Kong's Biel Crystal, which makes screens for smartphones.
Lam, Biel's chairman, owns 49% of the business; Yeung holds 51%.
Biel is the largest supplier of glass screens for cell phones, tablets and watches to Apple and employs 90,000 people around the world.
While weakening iPhone demand may affect shipments to Apple, they also supply to Samsung and Sony and have stated they expect stable revenue.
Since 2021 Biel has filed twice for a Hong Kong IPO but it never materialized.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Weili Dai, a former semipro Chinese basketball player, has cofounded at least four semiconductor companies.
The newest one, Singapore-based Silicon Box, is planning at $3.6 billion chip-making factory in Italy.
Her husband and cofounder Sehat Sutardja, also a billionaire, died in 2024; Forbes assumes that she inherited his fortune.
The couple cofounded and ran Marvell Technology for 21 years before being pushed out in 2016 amid an accounting investigation; they never faced any charges.
Dai is a board member and the largest shareholder of Alphawave Semi, which trades on the London Stock Exchange.
abouts: Dai played semi-professional basketball in Shanghai as a teen.
A native of Shanghai, Dai studied at UC Berkeley, and was reportedly the first woman to deliver a commencement address at the university's engineering school.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Roberto Irineu Marinho and his two billionaire brothers, Joao Roberto and Jose Roberto, inherited control of Globo, Brazil's largest media group.
Grandfather Irineu Marinho started Globo in 1925 with a newspaper. He died 25 days after the first issue was published and his son Roberto took over.
Globo Group includes Brazil's largest broadcaster, Rede Globo, Brazil's largest newspaper company and Globosat, Brazil's largest pay TV provider.
In December 2017, Roberto Irineu quit as the executive president of the group. For the first time ever, a non-family member assumed that position.
He remains vice-president of the board of directors, which is chaired by his brother Joao Roberto Marinho.
abouts: The low profile media baron also owns Sertaozinho Farm, which produces Orfeu gourmet coffee.
In the 1970s, he worked as an intern at U.S. TV network ABC.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mario Araripe founded Brazil's largest renewable energy developer Casa dos Ventos, meaning "House of the Winds," in 2007.
Araripe is the majority owner of the privately held company and currently shares its leadership roles with his son Lucas Araripe.
Before turning to renewables, he helmed companies in the real estate, textile, and car industries;  in 2006, he sold off-road vehicle manufacturer Troller to Ford.
French company TotalEnergies acquired a 34% stake in Casa dos Ventos? energy generation portfolio in January 2023, with the joint venture valued at over $2 billion.
Casa dos Ventos' developments account for one-third of all Brazilian wind farms currently in operation.
abouts: Raised in the northeastern state of Ceará, Araripe returned to the windy plateaus of his homeland to develop Casa dos Ventos' first projects.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michael Intrator is cofounder and CEO of cloud computing company CoreWeave, which sells computing power mostly to AI companies.
CoreWeave went public in March at an approximately $23 billion valuation; Intrator owns approximately 11%.
Along with Brannin McBee and Brian Venturo, he cofounded the company in 2017; it was originally a crypto firm.
Now, CoreWeave's biggest customers are Microsoft and OpenAI; it signed a $12 billion deal with the latter in March.
Before starting CoreWeave, Intrator was CEO of natural gas futures trading firm Hudson Ridge Asset Management.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Haim Saban turned his success with children's TV show "Mighty Morphin Power Rangers" into Fox Family Channel, a joint venture with News Corp.
Saban, who repurchased Power Rangers back in 2010, sold it for a second time in 2018, this time to Hasbro in a $522 million deal.
Saban and a group of private equity investors purchased Spanish language TV Network Univision Communications for $13.7 billion in 2007.
In February 2020, Univision agreed to sell a majority stake for an undisclosed price to two firms: Searchlight Capital Partners and ForgeLight LLC.
The Sabans, who have given $230 million to various organizations and initiatives, pledged $50 million to the forthcoming Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in 2017.
abouts: Born in Egypt to Jewish parents, Saban moved with his family to Tel Aviv when he was a child and lived in a one-room flat.
While serving in the Israeli army, Saban landed a booking for his band, but he didn't have a band or play an instrument, so he founded a band on the spot.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Manohar Lal Agarwal runs Delhi-based Haldiram Snacks with brother  Madhusudan Agarwal. It has now been merged with the Nagpur arm.
The company is known for its savory snacks, sweets and frozen foods.
Their grandfather started selling savory snacks from a tiny shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan in 1937.
The business was divided among his descendants into three separate companies, including Haldiram Snacks.
Haldiram Snacks has backed Venture Catalysts, an incubator, to invest in startups in packaged foods.
abouts: In April 2023 two arms of the family ? from Delhi and Nagpur- came together to create Haldiram Snacks Food Limited which is headquartered in Delhi.
There have been news reports of stake sale to global private equity groups like Blackstone and Temasek but nothing has been firmed up yet.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yuji Otsuka is the son of the late Minoru Otsuka, who founded Otsuka Corp. in 1961, a software developer and supplier of office copy machines.
Yuji, a former banker, took over as CEO when Minoru retired in 2001.
Otsuka's forecasted revenue for 2024 is $6.6 billion.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gustavo Denegri is the chairman of biotech company DiaSorin SpA; the bulk of his fortune is a 45% stake in the publicly-traded company.
In 2000, his private equity firm acquired the distressed DiaSorin from American Standard Companies and built it into a global player in diagnostics.
His first breakthrough came when his Gruppo Pro-Ind, a components firm, merged with Piaggio, owner of motor scooters Vespa and Aprilia.
He is one of few Italian businessmen to have built billion-dollar companies in more than one sector.
His firm Investimenti is run by his son Michele and has a diverse portfolio, including medical technology, real estate and TV production.
abouts: Gustavo Denegri was trained as a chemist.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Vladimir Litvinenko owned about 21% of publicly traded Russian chemical company PhosAgro. In May 2022 he transferred that stake to his wife Tatyana Litvinenko.
Since 1994, Litvinenko has been rector of Saint Petersburg Mining University.
He chaired the committee that awarded president Vladimir Putin his Ph.D in 1997.
According to Litvinenko, he was one of the creators of PhosAgro's development strategy; as a reward he became a shareholder of the company.
Other sources say Litvinenko was given his PhosAgro shares for political support and lobbying.
abouts: In the 2000s, Litvinenko served as Vladimir Putin's presidential campaign manager in Saint Petersburg three times.
Litvinenko is the author of more than 150 scientific papers and has 47 patents and inventions.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Brothers Martin and Olivier Bouygues control over 28% of their eponymous industrial conglomerate Bouygues Group through the holding company SCDM.
The Paris-headquartered giant, which boasted almost $60 billion in sales in 2023, operates in more than 80 countries in construction, energy, telecoms and media.
Martin has been chairman of the company since 2021; older brother Olivier is a board member.
Their father Frances (d.1993) started the construction firm in 1952. Their mother died in 2017 at age 93.
The brothers own a portfolio of wineries that includes Chateau Montrose, which they purchased in 2006.
abouts: Martin is a close friend of former French President Nicolas Sarkozy and is the godfather of Sarkozy's son.
Martin was awarded the highest French order of merit for military and civil merits, Legion d'Honneur, in July 2010.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Shandong Zhongji Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. Shandong Zhongji Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd.
Shandong Zhongji Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd. Shandong Zhongji Electrical Equipment Co., Ltd.

bios: Wang Weixiu's fortune derives from his stake in Zhongji Innolight, a supplier of optical communication modules and devices.
He stepped down as its chairman in 2023.
Zhongji Innolight was founded in 1987 and formerly known as Shandong Zhongji Electrical Equipment.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Howard Butt III is CEO of Texas grocery store chain H-E-B and serves on the board.
His uncle Charles Butt is the company's chairman.
His brother, Stephen Butt, is H-E-B's President of Shareholder Relations and its Central Market division, focused on specialty foods, and serves on the board.
The Butt family owns an estimated 90% of the $42.5 billion (sales) company.
H-E-B has 449 stores in Texas and Mexico and employs 160,000 people.
abouts: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity each year.
Butt's great-grandmother, Florence Butt, started the company in 1905.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stephen Butt is Texas grocery chain H-E-B's President of Shareholder Relations and its Central Market Division, a brand focused on specialty foods from around the world, and serves on the board.
His brother, Howard Butt III, is H-E-B's CEO and his uncle, Charles Butt, is chairman.
Based in San Antonio, H-E-B has 449 stores in Texas and Mexico and does $42.5 billion in annual revenue.
Butt's great-grandmother, Florence Butt, started the company in 1905.
abouts: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Qian Dongqi chairs Ecovacs, a supplier of robotic vacuum cleaners, window washers and air purifiers.
In 2018, Qian took Ecovacs public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
His son and heir-apparent, David Cheng Qian, is vice chairman of the company.
Qian previously worked for two state-owned entities: Hainan Province Foreign Trade and Economic Corporation and later the China National Electronics Import and Export Corporation in Shenzhen.
abouts: Qian holds a master's degree in Philosophy.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stephen Lansdown cofounded Hargreaves Lansdown, a British financial services firm.
The company manages over $100 billion in assets and boasts more than 1.7 million clients.
Lansdown stepped down as chairman of the firm in 2009 and left its board in 2012.
In 2010 he relocated to Guernsey, where he was a non-executive director of Ravenscroft Group, an investment services firm based on the island. He retired as chairman in 2021.
Lansdown cofounded Earth Capital, a private equity firm focused on sustainable and impact investing, in 2008. It shut down in 2024.
abouts: Lansdown owns Bristol Sport, which oversees the commercial operations of Bristol City F.C., Bristol Rugby Club, Bristol City W.F.C., Bristol Flyers and DZ Racing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xie Liangzhi chairs Beijing-based Sinocelltech Group, a supplier of biological products.
Xie holds a Ph.D. from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in chemical engineering.
He worked for Merck & Co. in the U.S. as a senior engineer from 1997 to 2002.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Arnout Schuijff is the cofounder and former chief technology officer of Adyen, an Amsterdam-based payment processing company.
He stepped down from the company's management board in 2021.
Schuijff became a billionaire when Adyen went public in 2018. He sold 15% of his stake in 2019.
Schuijff started the company in 2006 with Pieter van der Does, who is the company's CEO.
Schuijff and van der Does first worked together in 2000 at another e-commerce platform, Bibit.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Scott Shleifer cofounded Tiger Global Management's private equity investing arm in 2003, two years after Chase Coleman founded the hedge fund firm.
Tiger Global's venture funds now make up the bulk of the firm's $46 billion in net assets under management.
Shleifer made lucrative bets on several Chinese tech companies for Tiger, including JD.com, ride-hailing app Didi Chuxing and e-commerce giant Meituan.
Shleifer stepped down as Tiger Global's head of private equity at the start of 2024, transitioning to a role as senior advisor.
He bought a 21,000-square-foot Palm Beach mansion in 2021 for $123 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Jiangsu Yuyue Medical Equipment & Supply Co., Ltd.
Jiangsu Yuyue Medical Equipment & Supply Co., Ltd.

bios: Wu Guangming is founder of China's Jiangsu Yuyue Medical Equipment and Supply, which is chaired and run by his son Wu Qun.
The company supplies medical equipment such as rehabilitation machines, oxygen tanks and diagnostic equipment.
In 2008, the elder Wu took the company public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Wu was born to a fisherman's family, and cofounded the predecessor of Yuyue with his father in 1990s.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Denis O'Brien founded Digicel, a mobile phone network provider that operates in the Caribbean, Asia Pacific and Central America.
O'Brien made a fortune selling his Irish mobile outfit, Esat Telecom Group, to British Telecom Group in 2000 for $2.8 billion.
He has investments in energy companies and resorts on the Iberian Peninsula.
In 2019, O'Brien sold his stake in Independent News and Media to Mediahuis, losing hundreds of millions of Euros on his investment.
O'Brien made another media industry exit in 2021 by selling Communicorps, a radio company, to Bauer Media
abouts: O'Brien once sold horse pills.
O'Brien, whose mother was a political activist, cofounded the Front Line Defenders to protect and provide emergency support for human rights activists in danger.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ramesh Juneja and his younger brother Rajeev Juneja cofounded privately held Mankind Pharma in 1995.
The company is a low-cost generics champion generating most of its $1 billion in revenue in India.
Debuted on the Indian bourses in May 2023. The stock was listed at a 20 percent premium to its issue price.
His U.K.-educated son Arjun heads international operations.
The company also makes popular brands of condoms and pregnancy test kits.
abouts: Bollywood veteran Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.
Juneja and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart.
In September 2022 Mankind filed a draft red herring prospectus for a proposed IPO.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jurgen Wirtgen is one of two billionaire brothers who inherited the family fortune from their father, Reinhard, founder of construction equipment maker Wirtgen Group.
Wirtgen group was founded in 1961 and sold to Deere & Company in 2017 for $5.2 billion.
After the sale, the brothers created Wirtgen Invest, a family office with interests in energy, real estate, healthcare, consumer goods and finance.
The investment firm has made some 700 generally passive investments, according to its website.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stefan Wirtgen is one of two billionaire brothers who inherited the family fortune from their father, Reinhard, founder of construction equipment maker Wirtgen Group.
Wirtgen group was founded in 1961 and sold to Deere & Company in 2017 for $5.2 billion.
After the sale, the brothers created Wirtgen Invest, a family office with interests in energy, real estate, healthcare, consumer goods and finance.
The investment firm has made some 700 generally passive investments, according to its website.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: A scion of a Silicon Valley investing dynasty, Tim Draper is a founding partner of venture capital firm Draper Fisher Jurvetson.
Draper has made hundreds of VC investments in companies including Tesla and Theranos, and has made a fortune investing in cryptocurrencies.
In 2014, he bought 29,656 bitcoins confiscated by U.S. Marshals from the shuttered Silk Road black market for $18.7 million, or just $632 per coin.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Theodore 'Ted' Leonsis is founder, majority owner and CEO of Monumental Sports,  which owns several teams and arenas in Washington, D.C.
Subsidiaries include the NBA's Wizards, the NHL's Capitals, the WNBA's Washington Mystics and Capital One Arena.
The grandson of Greek immigrants, Leonsis initially built his fortune as a senior executive at AOL, where he worked for nearly 14 years.
He is a cofounder and partner at Revolution Growth, a venture capital firm helmed by AOL cofounder Steve Case.
abouts: He lives in a house in Potomac, MD that Franklin Roosevelt, and later Joe Kennedy (the father of President John F. Kennedy), used to rent out over the summer.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Aneel Bhusri cofounded the business software firm Workday together with Dave Duffield, the founder of PeopleSoft.
Bhusri stepped down from his role as co-chief executive in February 2024, taking on an advisory position.
Bhusri started his career in the early 1990s at business software firm PeopleSoft, where he rose to become vice chairman.
He's a former Intel board member and managing partner at venture capital firm Greylock Partners; he's been on the Forbes Midas List six times since 2008.
He studied electrical engineering at Brown University and has an MBA from Stanford.
abouts: Bhusri joined the Giving Pledge, a commitment by the world's wealthiest people to dedicate the majority of their wealth to philanthropy, in 2018.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Frank Blase runs the plastics manufacturer igus, which his father, Günter Blasé, founded in a garage in 1964.
Igus is the global leader in high-performance plastics for moving applications and has sales of more than 1 billion euros.
Blasé owns 97% of the business, his brother Carsten Blase, who lives in the USA, owns 3%.
Blase's Igus developed the world's first bike made from plastic in 2024.
abouts: When his father celebrated his 90th birthday in 2021, Blasé rebuilt the founding garage of 1964 with all original parts.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jian Jun is the chairwoman of biomedical supplier Imeik Technology Development, which makes products like skin fillers and facial implant threads.
Imeik listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020, in an IPO that raised more than $530 million.
Best known for its Hearty filler that treats neck wrinkles, the company has also branched into segments such as skincare products amid heightened competition.
Jian worked for the state-owned China National Cereals Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export early in her career.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yang cofounded web portal Yahoo in 1995 after dropping out of a Ph.D. program in electrical engineering at Stanford.
Yang served as Yahoo's CEO from 2007 to 2009; he left Yahoo's board in 2012.
In 2017, he and his wife, Akiko Yamazaki, pledged $25 million to San Francisco's Asian Art Museum, the largest gift in the museum's history.
In 2016, Yahoo completed the sale of its core operating business to Verizon for $5 billion in cash.
Yang founded AME Cloud Ventures, which bets on data-driven startups. Through his fund and personally, Yang has made several impact-minded investments.
Yang began a two-year term as chair of the board of trustees at Stanford, where he received his bachelor's and master's degrees, in July 2021.
abouts: Yang was born in Taiwan; his father died when he was two. He immigrated to the U.S. at age 10 with his mother and brother.
A former Chinese calligraphy student, Yang has a collection of about 250 works of ancient Chinese calligraphy from the Ming and Qing eras.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sean Parker's fortune stems from his brief tenure, at age 24, as Facebook's president. Parker is now a venture capital investor and philanthropist.
Parker was a teenage hacker and famously founded filesharing site Napster in 1999.
His interest in music led him to invest in Spotify in 2010. He served on the company's board until 2017.
He launched his Parker Foundation in 2015 with $600 million earmarked for science, global health and civic engagement.
In 2016, his foundation announced a $250 million grant to establish the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy.
Parker became chairman of image-generation startup Stability AI in June 2024.
abouts: Parker, who has asthma and allergies to certain foods, also founded the Sean N. Parker Center for Allergy & Asthma Research at Stanford in 2014.
Parker bought Brody House in Los Angeles from Ellen DeGeneres for approximately $55 million in 2014.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Theo Roussis controls Ravago, a plastics recycling and compounds producer and distributor.
Roussis is the son-in-law of Raf Van Gorp, who founded Ravago in 1961 as a recycler of plastic waste.
Under Roussis, Ravago grew into an empire with revenue 13 billion euros and 9.000 employees.
Together with his wife, Gunhilde Van Gorp, Roussis controls Ravago through Luxembourg-based holding company, Plastiche.
abouts: Roussis is of Greek descent and has never given an interview.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yu Zhuyun is the chairman and CEO of Central New Energy Holding Group, a business whose diverse interests span new energy, real estate and wellness.
Central New Energy went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Yu holds an MBA from Hong Kong Baptist University and an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joe Lonsdale is the managing partner of venture capital firm 8VC, which he cofounded in 2015 and relocated to Texas in 2020.
8VC, with $6 billion in assets, has made several big bets on startups in defense tech and life sciences.
A serial entrepreneur, Lonsdale has also cofounded data mining firm Palantir, which went public in 2020, and government software firm OpenGov.
After studying computer science at Stanford, Lonsdale started his career working for billionaire investor Peter Thiel's hedge fund.
In 2018 he founded the Cicero Institute, a conservative think tank that advocates for entrepreneur-friendly public policy in healthcare, housing and other causes.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yuri Kovalchuk is friends with Russia's president Vladimir Putin; they met when Putin was deputy mayor of St. Petersburg.
They both had country houses in the Ozero dacha cooperative, and when Putin became president, many of the cooperative's members' careers improved.
Kovalchuck is now the largest shareholder of Rossiya Bank and has a large stake in Sogaz insurance company.
He controls National Media Group, an investment firm with controlling stakes in popular Russian media assets.
He was sanctioned by the U.S. and the EU in 2014, along with a group of close Putin friends.
In December 2021 Sogaz bought 45% of MF Technologies, that controls VK, one of the largest internet companies in Russia.
abouts: After US sanctions hit Kovalchuk's Rossiya Bank, Vladimir Putin moved his payroll account to the bank.
Kovalchuk's son Boris is a former CEO of InterRAO, a large state-owned energy company in Russia. Now he is a chairman of the Accounts Chamber of Russia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Isaad Rebrab founded Cevital and served as its CEO for more than 50 years; He named his son, Malik, CEO in July 2022.
Cevital, Algeria's biggest privately-held company, owns one of the largest sugar refineries in the world, with the capacity to produce 2 million tons a year.
Cevital owns European companies, including French home appliances maker Groupe Brandt and Spanish aluminum firm Alas Iberia.
After serving 8 months in jail on charges of corruption, Rebrab was released on January 1, 2020. He denies any wrongdoing.
In May 2023, an Algerian court barred Rebrab from exercising any commercial or management duties at Cevital.
abouts: Rebrab is the son of militants who fought for Algeria's independence from France.
Cevital helped finance a biopic on Algerian resistance hero Larbi Ben M'hidi, who was executed by the French in 1957.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lucio Tan is the founder and chairman of LT Group, which has interests in tobacco, spirits, banking and property development.
In 1982, Tan established Asia Brewery. Now a subsidiary of LT, the brewery was the only one then to compete with the market leader San Miguel.
Tan's grandson and heir apparent Lucio Tan III was appointed president of LT Group and PAL Holdings in 2023.
In 2023 the airline ordered nine long-haul A350-1000 jets from Airbus, worth more than $3 billion, to tap into the post-pandemic rebound in travel demand.
abouts: Lucio Tan enjoys riding helicopters.
Tan studied chemical engineering at Far Eastern University.
PAL Holdings, the parent company of Philippine Airlines, completed its debt restructuring and turned profitable in 2021 after four years of losses.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cardiac surgeon Devi Shetty founded and runs Bangalore-based hospital chain Narayana Health.
It has 47 healthcare facilities including a hospital in the Cayman Islands.
U.K.-trained Shetty founded Narayana Health as Narayana Hrudayalaya in the year 2000.
Shetty took the company public in 2015. Biopharma billionaire Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw has a small stake in the company.
An ardent advocate of affordable healthcare, Shetty helped design the Yeshasvini scheme, a micro-insurance program in his home state of Karnataka.
abouts: He's often seen in his trademark blue surgeon's outfit.
Shetty was Mother Teresa's personal physician.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lin Ming-Hsiung is the chairman of PX Mart, one of Taiwan's largest supermarket chains.
He took over PX Mart from the government in 1998 when it had 66 outlets. Today it boasts over 1,000 stores as well as minimarkets that serve Taiwan's remote villages.
In 2022, the company completed a $377 million deal to purchase a 96% stake in hypermarket chain RT-Mart's Taiwan business.
Lin also controls real estate developer Yuanlih Construction and Hwatai Bank.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Originally from Chandigarh, India, Harindarpal Banga, known as Harry, has lived in Hong Kong since the 1970s.
The former vice-chairman of Noble Group made his fortune over a 21-year career with one of Asia's largest commodity traders.
He cashed in the last of his Noble shares in 2012, and started Hong Kong-based Caravel Group with sons Guneet and Angad in 2013.
Caravel Group trades and ships commodities.
Banga was an early investor and still holds a stake in India's online beauty retailer Nykaa, which went public in Mumbai in 2021.
abouts: In 2018 the National Maritime Day Celebrations Committee and the Directorate General of Shipping, India, honored him with the NMD Award of Excellence.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: A native of New Zealand, Richard Chandler relocated to Singapore in 2006 where he now runs Clermont Group, his personal investment outfit.
Clermont's portfolio includes interests in healthcare, financial services and aerospace.
Clermont has stakes in SBFC, an Indian provider of small business loans, and Hoan My, a healthcare group in Vietnam.
His Clermont Aerospace aviation engineering firm MagniX. It also owns a controlling stake in Eviation, an Israeli maker of light electric aircraft, which has orders worth $5 billion.
abouts: Chandler previously cofounded investment firm Sovereign Global with his brother, Christopher, who now runs his own Legatum Group in Dubai.
In 2021, MagniX won a $74 million, five-year contract from NASA to support its research in electrified aircraft propulsion.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xue Hua is cofounder and chairman of Guangdong Haid Group, a supplier of animal feed products.
Haid employs 20,000 people.
Xue graduated from Huazhong Agricultural University with a major in aquaculture in 1992.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhao Yan is the chairman and CEO of Shanghai-listed Bloomage Biotechnology, a biotech company best known for making hyaluronic acid, an ingredient widely used in beauty products.
Not content with just being a supplier, Zhao has established her own skincare brands that include the Biohyalux line for facial creams, gels and masks.
To expand the use of hyaluronic acid, Bloomage also sells products such as candies and bottled water infused with the compound.
Besides Bloomage, Zhao has interests in finance, property and sports as well.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rajeev Juneja and his older brother Ramesh Juneja cofounded privately held Mankind Pharma  in 1995.
The company is a low-cost generics champion generating most of its $1.05 Billion in revenue in India.
Private equity firms Capital International and ChrysCapital are key investors in Mankind.
Juneja's U.K.-educated nephew Arjun heads international operations.
The company also makes popular brands of condoms and pregnancy test kits.
abouts: Juneja and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart.
Bollywood veteran Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.
In September 2022 Mankind filed a draft red herring prospectus for a proposed IPO.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lin Jianhua is the chairman of Hangzhou First Applied Material, a supplier of packaging films, backplane and other products to the solar power industry.
Lin worked at a state-owned fertilizer factory in Zhejiang Province from 1982 to 1994, then set up Hangzhou First in 2003 with his wife Zhang Hong.
Zhang Hong is a vice president at Hangzhou First.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sergei Popov has cashed out of all his major investments in recent years.
He and his former partner Andrei Melnichenko made a fortune managing finance and industrial group MDM.
They later created TMK, one of the world's largest oil and gas pipe manufacturers, with fellow billionaire Dmitry Pumpyansky.
They sold out to Pumpyansky in 2006. That same year the partners started to divide up their assets, a process completed in 2012.
In 2015 he sold MDM Bank to Russia's Binbank. Two years later it went bankrupt and came under the control of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation.
abouts: Popov is a founder of a private fund called Agat, which has a mentoring program that offers young businesspeople startup capital.
Popov hired a special public relations agency to help him stay out of the press.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Brothers Martin and Olivier Bouygues control over 28% of their eponymous industrial conglomerate Bouygues Group through the holding company SCDM.
The Paris-headquartered giant, which boasted almost $60 billion in sales in 2023, operates in more than 80 countries in construction, energy, telecoms and media.
Olivier has been on the board of Bouygues since 1984, while his younger brother Martin is chairman of the company.
Their father Frances (d.1993) started the construction firm in 1952. Their mother died in 2017 at age 93.
The brothers own a portfolio of wineries that includes Chateau Montrose, which they purchased in 2006.
abouts: Olivier studied at the same French engineering school as fellow billionaire Carrie Perrodo's son Francois.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Augusto Perfetti and his brother Giorgio Perfetti own candy and gum giant Perfetti Van Melle, a company with more than $2.9 billion in revenues in 2022.
Their father Ambrogio and uncle Egidio started the company in 1946 as a chewing gum business in a small town near Milan.
In 2022, the company announced it would acquire Mondelez International's developed market gum business, adding brands such as Trident, Dentyne and Bubbalicious.
Augusto Perfetti named his yacht and his private jet after Mentos mints and Airheads taffy, the company's top-selling brands.
Perfetti once sold a 90-metre yacht under construction to fellow billionaire Suleiman Kerimov.
abouts: Perfetti's father and uncle were inspired to start the company after seeing American soldiers bring gum to Europe during World War II.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Fisher is the youngest of Gap founders Doris and Donald Fisher's three sons.
He stepped down from Gap's board of directors in May 2022. His brothers Robert and William still sit on the board.
John is a founding partner of investment firm Sansome Partners and sits on the board of the Silicon Schools Fund.
He is a majority owner of the Oakland A's baseball team and has smaller stakes in MLS' San Jose Earthquakes and the Scottish Glasgow Celtic F.C.
abouts: The three Fisher brothers attended Princeton University and went on to study at Stanford University's School of Business.
John is a chairman of the Knowledge Is Power Program Foundation (KIPP), a non-profit network of public charter schools.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Benjamin Otto inherited a 15.1% stake in Otto Group, which his grandfather, Werner, started as a mail-order business in 1949.
His father, Michael Otto, he ran the business for 26 years until 2007. He is now chairman of its supervisory board.
With revenues exceeding $15 billion, Otto Group has more than 40 companies in retail (including Crate and Barrel), real estate and financial services.
Benjamin joined the family company as an executive director in 2012.
abouts: Benjamin Otto and his wife are active in philanthropic organizations focused on healing through alternative treatment methods.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Jiangsu Wujiang China Eastern Silk Market
Jiangsu Wujiang China Eastern Silk Market

bios: Miao Hangen chairs Eastern Shenghong, a Shenzhen-listed petrochemical and new material firm.
Its parent Shenghong Group, which also has interests in textile and new energy, was founded in 1992.
The group broke ground on a $4.2 billion plant for energy storage system batteries in Zhangjiagang, Jiangsu in July 2023.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shigenobu Nagamori is the founder and chairman of motor manufacturer Nidec.
Nidec bills itself as the world's largest manufacturer of motors for hard-disk drives and optical drives, by units sold.
Nagamori has said publicly that his goal is to hit ¥10 trillion ($91 billion) in revenue by 2030, partly by focusing on drivetrains for electric vehicles.
In 2024, Mitsuya Kishida, one of five executive vice presidents, became the new president and CEO.
Nidec made an unsolicited $1.7 billion takeover bid for Tokyo -based machine-tool maker Makino Milling Machine in 2024 but was unsuccessful.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Aspire Capital Holding for Financial Investments

bios: Essam Al Muhaidib is the CEO of Al Muhaidib Group, a Dammam, Saudi Arabia-based family-owned conglomerate.
Al Muhaidib Group invests in companies across consumer products, infrastructure, construction, real estate and finance; Essam owns 28% of the company.
The group was founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir, who started out as a food trader before expanding into building materials and real estate.
Essam and his brothers Emad and Sulaiman took over after Abdulkadir's death in 1996; they share ownership with 4 other family members.
Al Muhaidib Group owns shares in at least 16 publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia and Egypt.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Aspire Capital Holding for Financial Investments

bios: Sulaiman Al Muhaidib is the chairman of Al Muhaidib Group, a Dammam, Saudi Arabia-based family-owned conglomerate.
Al Muhaidib Group invests in companies across consumer products, infrastructure, construction, real estate and finance; Sulaiman owns 28% of the company.
The group was founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir, who started out as a food trader before expanding into building materials and real estate.
Sulaiman and his brothers Essam and Emad took over after Abdulkadir's death in 1996; they share ownership of the group with 4 other family members.
Al Muhaidib Group owns shares in at least 16 publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia and Egypt.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jeffrey Talpins runs Element Capital Management, a hedge fund firm that specializes in macro trading and has a reported $12 billion under management.
Element has been one of the best performing hedge funds since it was founded in 2005, posting annualized returns in excess of 20%.
A former Citigroup and Goldman Sachs trader, Talpins invests across bonds, currencies and stocks.
Even by hedge fund standards, Talpins is exceptionally secretive and is careful to avoid any publicity.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Smith raised more than $15 billion in debt to build three giant plants at Freeport, Texas to chill and export 15 million tons per year of liquefied natural gas -- equivalent to 2 billion cubic feet per day.
He made his first fortune with oil and gas company Basin Exploration, which he sold in 2001 for $428 million.
Enjoys homes in Miami Beach, Malibu and the Hamptons.
Freeport LNG was originally envisioned as an LNG import terminal; when the shale gas boom arrived, Smith turned his strategy 180 degrees.
abouts: He majored in chemistry at Colorado State University but dropped out just 6 credits shy of a degree to focus on skiing. Later donated $13 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhang Jian chairs AIMA Technology, a maker of electric bikes and scooters.
AIMA was founded in 1999.
AIMA listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: The grandson of John T. Dorrance, the inventor of condensed soup, Bennett Dorrance owns a 15% stake in Campbell Soup.
Dorrance retired from the Campbell's Soup board in 2022, ending a 33 year stint.
Dorrance is a founding partner of DMB Associates, a real estate development firm with projects in Arizona, California and Hawaii.
A licensed pilot, Dorrance owns a private hangar in Scottsdale, Arizona that sometimes houses his vintage car collection.
The Dorrance Scholarship, established by Bennett and Jacquelynn Dorrance in 1999, has supported 150-plus first-generation college students in Arizona.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Yun'an is the chairman and CEO of Chinese bubble tea maker Guming Holdings.
Founded in 2010, Guming sells bubble tea products under the Good Me brand.
It operates a network of almost 10,000 stores across China, where each cup of tea is priced at no more than $3.
Wang launched the first Good Me store in his hometown of Daxi in Zhejiang Province.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yang Huiyan chairs property developer Country Garden. She became the only one at the helm after her father Yeung Kwok Keung stepped down as co-chair in February 2023.
Yang has long been groomed for succession. Yeung transferred a 57% Country Garden stake to her back in 2007, which once made her the world's youngest female billionaire.
Her sister Yang Ziying also sits on the board; husband Chen Chong is a non-executive director.
In August 2023, Country Garden triggered fresh turmoil in China's beleaguered real estate market after it missed interest payments of $22.5 million on two offshore bonds.
Yang donated in the same year $826 million worth of shares in property management arm Country Garden Services to a Hong Kong charity set up by sister Ziying.
abouts: Yang obtained a bachelor's degree from Ohio State University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems Co Ltd

bios: Zhou Bajin and his daughter Zhou Xiaoping control Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems.
The duo cofounded the company in 1993; Xiaoping serves as its chairman and CEO.
Its customers include Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Geely and Nio.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Huang Shan chairs Shenzhen Fortune Trend Technology, a supplier of financial-market software.
Fortune Trend went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020.
Huang holds undergraduate and graduate degrees from Wuhan University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Erman Ilicak's Ronesans Holding, founded in 1993, operates as construction contractor and real estate developer in 28 countries.
In July 2016, he sold 5% of Ronesans to IFC, a World Bank institution, in a deal that valued the company at $4.3 billion.
Construction firm acquisitions include the Swiss Hergiswill and German Heitcamp in 2013, and the Netherlands' Ballast Nedam in 2015.

In a public-private partnership with the Turkish government, Ronesans has so far built 
healthcare complexes with a contract value of $3.4 billion.
Ronesans is partnering with the Port of Rotterdam to develop the Ceyhan Mega Petrochemical Industrial Zone in the south of Turkey.
abouts: A basketball player during his years at TED high school, Ilicak served as president of the TED Ankara Sports Club from 2014 to 2016.
Ilicak started Ronesans in St. Petersburg, Russia, where he worked as an engineer for billionaire Sinan Tara's construction firm, Enka Insaat ve Sanayi AS.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Anu Aga derives her wealth from a majority stake in listed engineering firm Thermax.
Aga started working at Thermax in 1985 when it was run by her husband and took the helm in 1996 after he died of a heart attack.
She stepped down as chairman in 2004, ceding the spot to her daughter Meher, a U.K.-trained chemical engineer, who lets hired executives manage the firm.
Consumer goods billionaire Harsh Mariwala has a board seat in the company.
Thermax has partnered with Australian billionaire Andrew Forrest's Fortescue Future Industries to set up a green hydrogen venture in India.
abouts: Aga cofounded Teach for India in 2008, a non-profit that recruits young people to teach for two years in schools for low-income kids.
Aga was a nominated member of parliament for six years.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Serge Godin founded Canadian tech firm CGI Group in 1976 at age 26.
One of nine children, Godin started working for his father (who had just a fifth-grade education) at the family's sawmill at age 12.
He studied computer science and got an MBA from Quebec's Université Laval, then worked in consulting before using $5,000 in savings to start CGI.
Godin serves as co-chair of the $10 billion (revenue) company; he was president and CEO until 2006. His daughter, Julie, was appointed executive chair in January 2025.
He has overseen more than 100 acquisitions, including the 1998 purchase of Bell Sygma, which nearly doubled the size of the company at the time.
abouts: When his father's uninsured mill burned down, a young Godin worked at a convenience store after school and at a dry cleaner's on Saturdays to help pay the bills.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhang Lei is the founder and CEO of Hillhouse Capital Management, a global investment firm based in Singapore.
Zhang obtained an MBA and M.A. in international relations from Yale University.
Zhang holds a B.A. from Renmin University in Beijing, where he is vice chairman of the board of trustees; and earned an MBA and M.A. from Yale University.
During his time at Yale, he worked for the Yale Investment Office which manages the university's endowment funds.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cheng is the cofounder of Kuaishou, a short video platform headquartered in Beijing.
The company went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in February 2021.
Pre-IPO strategic investors included funds managed by Fidelity and BlackRock.
Kuaishou cofounder Su Hua is also a billionaire.
Cheng, the CEO, succeeded Su and added the role of chairman in October 2023.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Eva Maria Bucher-Haefner's fortune mostly stems from her former stake in IT management software maker CA Technologies, acquired by Broadcom in 2020.
She inherited half of her father Walter's stake in the business when he died in June 2012, then the world's oldest billionaire at 101.
She and her brother, Martin Haefner, also inherited equal stakes in car dealer AMAG.
Bucher-Haefner sold her stake in AMAG to Martin, who is also a billionaire, in late 2018.
She runs Moyglare, a 500-acre horse farm in Ireland that was purchased by her father in 1962, home to around 100 horses today.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Son of a Fujian farmer, Sam Goi owns Tee Yih Jia Food Manufacturing, one of the world's largest makers of popiah skins, which are used for spring rolls.
Goi dropped out of school to work in his father's grocery store then got into frozen foods when he bought a struggling food unit.
He also has real estate interests through his stakes in listed firms GSH and KOP.
In 2021, he became chairman of Singapore-based consumer goods firm Hanwell Industries after a boardroom tussle. Hanwell is now PSC Corp.
Goi is Singapore's non-resident ambassador to Brazil.
abouts: Goi sold a 28-story office tower in Singapore for $512 million to a Chinese buyer in 2017.
He collects both local and Chinese artworks and antiques.
Goi built a new factory in Singapore for S$450 mill, which opened in 2023.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: China Tourism Group Duty Free Corporation

bios: Chen Fashu chairs New Huadu Group, a holding company which he founded in 1998 after several business ventures including timber trading and retail.
Through New Huadu Group, Chen holds stakes in Yunnan Baiyao (a pharmaceutical company) and Longi Green Energy.
Chen became an avid investor after reaping a large return with stakes in Zijin Minging Group, a gold miner.
Chen is also on the board of Shanghai Pharmaceuticals Holding.
He is a native of China's Fujian Province, northeast of Hong Kong.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dmitry Pumpyansky got his start as a trader, then oversaw several metals plants in the Ural in the 1990s before taking over the Sinarsky Pipe Factory.
Pumpyansky teamed up with fellow billionaires Sergei Popov and Andrei Melnichenko to acquire pipe conglomerate TMK, and then bought them out in 2006.
Making pipes became the source of Pumpyansky's wealth. His TMK, a supplier to Gazprom since 1998, is No.1 in Russia.
In 2011 Pumpyansky's JV with Siemens won a $2.7 billion contract from Russian Railways to deliver modern trains called Lastochka (swallow bird).
In March 2021, Pumpyansky's TMK acquired an 86.5% stake in its rival, Russia-based steel producer ChelPipe Group, for 1.1 billion.
His companies also gave a face lift to a stadium that hosted the 2018 World Cup in Ekaterinburg.
Pumpyansky was sanctioned by the EU and U.K. in March 2022. He exited as TMK's beneficiary and resigned as a member of the board. Son Alexander also resigned as a member of TMK's board of directors.
In 2022 his 236ft yacht Axioma was seized by Gibraltar authorities and then sold at the auction for $37.5m.
