personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: G.V.Prasad is  the co-chairman and managing director of pharma company Dr Reddy's Laboratories.
The company was founded by his late father-in-law K.Anji Reddy in 1984.
Prasad runs the company with Satish Reddy, the late founder's son, who is also a billionaire.
In December 2023 Dr. Reddy's launched Nerivio, a wearable therapy device to treat migraines.
abouts: Prasad sits on the boards of the Indian School of Business and Ashoka University.
His father-in-law was the son of a turmeric farmer and founded the company with seed money of $45,000 to make pharma ingredients and generics.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: David Mindus is the founder and CEO of Swedish commercial real estate company Sagax AB.
Mindus and two partners began buying warehouses and light industrial properties around Stockholm in 2000 after identifying the sector as undervalued.
Mindus owns more than 17 percent of Sagax, which listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange in 2004.
Its portfolio consists of more than 37 million square feet across 673 properties.
Before Sagax, Mindus worked at GE Capital, where he helped found the company's Swedish real estate investment business.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chang Jianming chairs Shanghai Moons, a maker of industrial equipment for the automotive industry.
Moons went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
The company was founded in Shanghai in 1994 and employs more than 3,000 people.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shao Qinxiang chairs Zhejiang Garden Bio-chemical High-tech, a supplier of pharmaceuticals and animal nutrition products.
Shao is the controlling shareholder of parent Garden Group, which was founded in 2000.
Garden Group was founded as a candle factory and then a garment manufacturer. It has since diversified into pharmaceuticals, energy and other fields.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jerry Moyes and his father founded Swift Transportation in 1966 with one truck, moving cotton and imported steel between Arizona and California
Swift grew to nearly 20,000 trucks and some $4 billion in annual revenue before it merged with Knight Transportation in 2017.
Moyes owns nearly a quarter of the merged company, called Knight-Swift Transportation.
He stepped down as chairman of Swift in 2016, after 50 years in the business.
Moyes owned the Phoenix Coyotes hockey team, with minority partner Wayne Gretzky, until the team filed for bankruptcy in 2009 and was sold to the NHL.
abouts: Moyes resigned as Swift CEO in 2005 after an insider-trading case (he did not admit to wrongdoing). Two years later, he took Swift private in a leveraged buyout.
Moyes took Swift public once again in 2010, listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yasuhide Uno runs U-Next Holdings, a company that's become a streaming services giant in Japan.It also provides payment and point-of-sales services to restaurants and stores, broadband services and energy to companies.
His father Mototada started the Osaka-based company providing background music via cable to retailers and restaurants.
Yasuhide joined the firm in 1998, just before his father died.
In 2001, it listed on the Osaka Stock Exchange's bourse for startups and moved to the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2013.
The Tokyo-based company posted nearly $2.1 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through August 2024.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani is the chairman of Al Faisal Holding, one of Qatar's biggest conglomerates, which he founded in 1964.
It owns more than 20 hotels around the world, including the St. Regis in Washington, D.C. and Miami, and the W Hotel in London.
Al Faisal Holding also has a majority stake in publicly-traded Aamal, which owns real estate in Qatar and sells medical supplies and pharmaceuticals.
Al Thani started selling car parts in Doha at age 16. He became the sole distributor of Bridgestone tires in the 1960s.
abouts: Al Thani is a distant relative of the Qatari royal family.
A museum in Doha houses his collection of more than 15,000 artifacts, including antique cars, ancient coins and Islamic art.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Satish Reddy is the chairman of listed pharma company Dr Reddy's Laboratories, in which he has a minority stake.
The company was founded by his late father K.Anji Reddy in 1984.
Reddy's brother-in-law G.V.Prasad, who is also a billionaire, is the co-chairman and managing director of the company.
In December 2023 it rolled out Nerivio, a wearable therapy device to treat migraines.
abouts: He is a member of the board of governors at the Indian Institute of Management in  Visakhapatnam.
His father was the son of a turmeric farmer and founded the company with seed money of $45,000 to make pharma ingredients and generics.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Walter Kortschak is an investor who joined growth equity firm Summit Partners in 1989. He spent 26 years there as an active partner.
At Summit, some of his biggest tech bets and buyouts were E-Tek Dynamics (a 40x return) and networking company Xylan (127x).
Kortschak now invests solo, with early bets on such outfits as The Trade Desk and Robinhood.
At first, Kortschak wanted to be a software engineer, but got into venture investing after business school at UCLA.
He also owns 2,800 acres in Kauai, Hawaii, including a ranch where Jurassic Park was filmed.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ulrike Baro is one of the three daughters of Horst Sartorius, who passed on a 50% stake in biopharmaceutical firm Sartorius AG after his death in 1998.
Her great-grandfather Florenz Sartorius founded the firm in 1870 to make analytical balances to measure small mass in laboratories.
Sartorius AG, which went public in 1990, makes pharmaceutical and laboratory equipment.
Today, the company has around 10,600 employees and annual revenue exceeding $2.5 billion.
abouts: Ulrike shares in the legacy with sisters Karin Herbst-Sartorius, Christine Franken and Christine's sons, Andreas and Kai Christian.
An executor oversees their inheritance until 2028.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sefik Yilmaz Dizdar is a partner in LC Waikiki, a producer and retailer of ready-to-wear fashions and home items.
Designer Georges Amouyal and a partner founded LC Waikiki in France in 1985. Dizdar and partners including Mustafa Kucuk acquired it in 1997.
LC Waikiki's first international store opened in Romania in 2009. In 2016, it expanded into home textile products under the brand name LCW Home.
The company prides itself on promoting women into its management ranks.
Today, LC Waikiki has over 1,000 locations in 47 countries; roughly half are outside of Turkey. Its motto: "Everyone deserves to dress well."
abouts: LC Waikiki, with annual revenue of around $2.5 billion, is managed by Kucuk, also a billionaire, and his family.
The brand combines the name of the famous Hawaiian beach with "LC," as in "Les Copains" ("friends" in French).

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shen Xiqiang is vice chairman of Jiangsu Yoke Technology, a supplier of electronics, insulation and plastics materials.
Shen cofounded Yoke in 1997 in the Yixing county of Jiangsu province.
His elder son Shen Qi is Yoke's chairman; younger son Shen Fu is deputy general manager.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Evangelos Mytilineos is the chairman and CEO of Athens-based, publicly traded metals and energy firm METLEN Energy & Metals.
METLEN's assets include aluminum plants, bauxite mines and solar energy projects, and the firm is Greece's largest independent electricity supplier.
METLEN grew out of a metallurgy business founded by Mytilineos' grandfather, also named Evangelos, in 1908.
Mytilineos founded the modern company, then named Mytilineos Energy & Metals, in 1990 and took it public on the Athens stock exchange in 1995.
He renamed the company METLEN in 2024, ahead of a planned dual listing on the London stock exchange in 2025.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: George Christ cofounded software company Altair Engineering with fellow billionaire James Scapa in 1985.
Christ retired before Altair went public in 2017 but remains the company's second largest individual shareholder with a 12% stake.
Scapa, who has served as CEO since Altair's founding, owns 21% of the Troy, Michigan-based company.
In January 2025, Altair agreed to be acquired by German tech giant Siemens for $10.6 billion in cash. The deal is expected to close during the second half of 2025.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sergei Katsiev, partner of billionaire Igor Kesaev, made his fortune in tobacco after the fall of the Soviet Union.
From 1991 to 1993, he worked in the government trade mission to the Netherlands.
When he returned to Russia, he headed Mercury Tobacco Corporation, an importer of tobacco products owned by Kesaev.
In 1998 Katsiev founded his own company, Megapolis, which also sold tobacco products.
In 2006 Katsiev and Kesaev merged their companies. Megapolis is now Russia's largest seller of tobacco products.
Philip Morris and Japan Tobacco International bought 40% of Megapolis for $1.5 billion in 2013.
abouts: Katsiev is now the owner of Nizhny Karmadon, a mineral water producer sourced from the Caucasus.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Richard Chang is vice chairman of ASE Technology Holding.
ASE is a world-leading provider of semiconductor assembly and testing services.
He and his brother Jason are the main investors in real estate developer Sino Horizon.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Elizabeth Sy is an advisor of SM Investments, a post she's held since 2012.
She is the second child of the late SM founder, Henry Sy.
She is president and chairman of SM Hotels and Conventions Corp., which oversees nine hotels including a slew of Radisson properties.
She started out as an assistant at her father's first hotel business, the Manila Royal Hotel.
She has a degree in business administration from Maryknoll College, now known as Miriam College.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sun Huaqing chairs Guangdong Marubi Biotechnology, a supplier of cosmetics and skin care products.
Sun worked for an electric machinery factory in Chongqing more than 20 years ago.
He founded the "Marubi" brand in Guangzhou in 2000.
Marubi investors include L Capital, an affiliate of LVMH.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Christine Brigitte Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
abouts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Igor Tulchinsky is founder and CEO of WorldQuant, a quantitative investment firm with $17 billion in assets under management.
WorldQuant specializes in stastical arbitrage and other quantitative-driven trading techniques.
Born in Belarus, Tulchinsky immigrated to the U.S. as a child and began his career at AT&T Bell Laboratories.
He spent two years at Interactive Brokers before moving to Millennium, the hedge fund run by billionaire investor Izzy Englander.
He founded WorldQuant in 2007 as a subadvisor of Millennium, and it still manages $7 billion on behalf of the larger hedge fund.
abouts: His nonprofit WorldQuant University provides free online masters-level courses in financial engineering.
He has written three books about investing and financial markets.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ivan Zhao is the CEO and original founder of productivity software company Notion, which was last valued at $10 billion.
Notion's software is a minimalistic competitor to Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
The software is popular among both business users and consumers. Zhao expects it to hit 100 million users in 2024.
Word-of-mouth growth has helped Zhao to keep Notion lean in employee count and profitable.
In turn, he has raised about $330 million at low dilution. He owns 30% of the company, Forbes estimates.
abouts: Zhao is particular about the design and aesthetics of a space. Notion's first three offices had a no-shoes policy.
He also hand-selected every piece of furniture in Notion's San Francisco headquarters.
His favorite is the Artek Aalto Stool, designed in 1933, which retails for about $400.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Chaobin chairs the Zhonglu Group,  one of the largest non-government real estate owners in the central Chinese city of Zhengzhou.
Son George is heir apparent.
The Wang Chaobin Charitable Foundation in Zhengzhou provides financial support for disaster relief, cultural exchanges, education and other fields.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Karl Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips traces its roots to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
abouts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ni Zugen is chairman of home appliance maker Kingclean Electronic, which sells wares under the Lexy brand.
Ni worked for  a Suzhou-base vacuum cleaner factory before founding his own business in 1994.
Kingclean Electronic listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2015.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ivan Chrenko is Slovakia's first billionaire, who began building his real estate fortune in the early 1990s.
His company, HB Reavis, developed the first business centers in Bratislava and the top shopping mall, later sold.
In one of the earliest big post-Brexit real estate deals in London in 2016,  HB Reavis sold 33 Central to Wells Fargo for a reported $400 million.
In Warsaw, it is constructing one of the tallest buildings in Europe.
He invested more than $10 million in e-commerce cloud startup Exponea, which was sold in 2022.
Chrenko served as CEO of the HB Reavis Group from 1994 to October 2013. He is now the board chairman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Matthew Pritzker and his sister Liesel Pritzker Simmons sued their family for a chunk of its Hyatt Hotels fortune and received around $500 million apiece in 2005.
Their uncle Jay Pritzker (d. 1999) founded the hotel chain and their uncle Donald Pritzker (d. 1972) managed and developed it.
Their father Robert Pritzker (d. 2011) ran the family's industrial conglomerate Marmon Group, which was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in a series of transactions beginning in 2008.
Three of Matthew and Liesel's step-siblings, seven cousins and their father's cousin Nick Pritzker are also billionaires.
Matthew invests his fortune through the Chicago-based Matthew Pritzker Company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Aier Eye Hospital Group Co Ltd
Aier Eye Hospital Group Co Ltd

bios: Li Li is the vice chairman of Shenzhen-listed Aier Eye Hospital Group.
Aier Eye Hospital Group was founded in 2002 and is headquartered in the central Chinese city of Changsha.
The company's chairman, Chen Bang, is also a billionaire.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hajime Satomi is the chairman of Sega Sammy, a Japanese pachinko machine and gaming software firm.
He founded pachinko machine maker Sammy, which got into the videogame business when it acquired Sega in 2004.
His son, Haruki, is CEO and chairman.
Sega Sammy has a 45% stake in South Korean gambling-and-entertainment resort Paradise City.
Satomi is also a top-ranked owner of thoroughbred horses.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xu Chuanhua founded a small family workshop to produce liquid soap and detergent in 1986 when he was 52 years old.
Today, his Transfar Group generates most of its business from logistics and chemicals. It also operates in agribusiness and investment industries.
Xu has retired from daily operations, handing reins to sons Guanju and Guanbao, who are chairman and vice chairman of Transfar Group respectively.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rubén Coppel Luken and his four brothers own the Coppel department stores, one of Mexico's largest retailers.
Coppel is chairman of BanCoppel and Afore Coppel, the group's banking and pension fund businesses
BanCoppel, founded in 2007, stemmed from the retailer's historical practice of financing items to their clients.
Because customers were low on cash after World War II, founder Enrique Coppel Tamayo started selling furniture on credit using weekly payments.
In mid-2023, Afore Coppel reported over $24 billion in assets under management.
abouts: BanCoppel has over 1,000 offices across Mexico.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Vladimir Yevtushenkov is a cofounder of AFK Sistema, which has investments in Russia's largest cellular operator MTS, online retailer Ozon and healthcare chain Medsi.
Yevtushenkov was hit by sanctions in April 2022 and transferred 10% of his stake in AFK Sistema to his son; Forbes still credits him with his remaining 49% stake in the company.
In 2014, AFK Sistema was accused of illegally acquiring a controlling stake in oil firm Bashneft. The shares were returned and sold to state-owned Rosneft.
In 2023 the company, through its Cosmos Hotel Group, acquired ten Radisson and Park Inn hotels for just 200 million euros from Norway's Wenaas Hotel Russia, which left the Russian market.
AFK Sistema was founded in 1993.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Xicheng's fortune rose following the July 2016 IPO of his tire manufacturer, Shandong Linglong Tire, on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Its predecessor was a state-owned tire factory founded in 1975 in Shandong Province.
The company was on the verge of collapse in 1987 when Wang was named leader and shifted its focus to pricier tires.
The company is now a supplier to GM, Ford, Tata, Fiat and Hyundai.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Asok Kumar Hiranandani is a cofounder of the erstwhile Royal Brothers property group.
He separated from his older brother Raj Kumar in 2011 after dividing their property empire.
His Royal Group Investments, run by his son Bobby, owns the 215-room Sofitel Singapore Sentosa Resort.
Hiranandani opened Singapore's second Raffles hotel in Sentosa, consisting of 62 villas, in August 2024.

In 2022 after selling his 134-room SO/Singapore hotel in the city's central business district for a record S$240 million, he paid a record price of S$172 million for the Ming Arcade near Orchard Road.
abouts: In 2018, he bought the Darby Park Executive Suites, a serviced apartments complex close to Orchard Road, for $70 million but has sold it since.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Eugene Kaspersky graduated from the Higher School of KGB and began creating his first antiviral programs in the early 1990s.
Kaspersky became interested in computer security in 1989 when his computer was infected with the 'Cascade' virus.
The young engineer founded Kaspersky Lab in 1997, with Eugene heading the company's antivirus research.
Over 400 million users now use Kaspersky Lab products to protect their computers.
Kaspersky is a Forbes contributor.
In 2019-2024 Kaspersky Lab bought about 70% of New Cloud Technologies, developer of office software suite MyOffice.
abouts: Kaspersky Lab is the official sponsor of Scuderia Ferrari, one of the most successful Formula One racing team.
President Trump signed a law that banned the use of Kaspersky Lab products within the U.S. government  due to concerns that it was vulnerable to Kremlin influence.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pavan Jain is the chairman of Delhi-based INOX Group.
His son Siddharth Jain  runs INOX Air Products, which supplies medical oxygen, and INOXCVA, which manufactures cryogenic tanks.
His brother Vivek Jain is chairman of the Inox GFL group, which includes listed Gujarat Fluorochemicals and Inox Wind.
In 2023, his INOX Leisure multiplex chain merged with PVR to form India's largest multiplex operator PVR-INOX.
He listed cyrogenics cylinder maker Inox India in 2023 at a 44% premium to the IPO price.
abouts: Patriarch Devendra Jain divided the family's assets in INOX Group in 2021 between Pavan and Vivek.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Li Haiyan is a co-founder of  hot-pot chain Haidilao International Holdings; she has been a company supervisor since 2009.
Li is the wife of billionaire Shi Yonghong, a director at Haidilao and chairman of  hotpot seasonings supplier Yihai International.
Haidilao co-founders Li, Zhang Yong, Shu Ping and Shi Yonghong funded their first restaurant with personal savings in 1994.
Haidilao today is one of the most popular restaurant chains in China and has about 1,300 locations worldwide.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Christopher Kwok is the younger son of property mogul Raymond Kwok, chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
He's served as an executive director at Sun Hung Kai since 2016, taking charge of sales, project management and the leasing of major projects.
He's also a member of the Beijing Municipal Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.
In 2012, his father and his uncle Thomas became involved in a bribery investigation. Raymond was acquitted but Thomas was found guilty and sentenced to five years in prison in 2014.
abouts: Christopher's brother, Edward, and three of his cousins are also billionaires.
Christopher and his wife, Rachel Zhao, a former news anchor for China's Phoenix TV, met while they studied at Stanford University in 2013.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kishin RK is among Singapore's leading developers with his Royal Holdings/RB Capital property empire, which he owns and runs together with his father Raj Kumar.
He's been on a dealmaking spree after a 2011 family settlement between his father and uncle Asok Kumar Hiranandani, who's also a billionaire.
Prize holdings include the 442-room Holiday Inn Express at Clarke Quay, Holiday Inn Little India  and the hotel Intercontinental Singapore Robertson Quay.
He bought the Porcelain Hotel in Singapore's Chinatown, which was refurbished and reopened in 2023 as the 134-room Hotel 1900.
abouts: Kishin's RB Food Group owns a portfolio of brands, such as members' club 1880, cocktail bar Employees Only, Roia restaurant and cloud kitchen company TiffinLabs.
The name RB is derived from the erstwhile Royal Brothers, a 77-year-old property group with roots in textile trading.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Raj Kumar is among Singapore's leading landlords with his Royal Holdings/RB Capital property empire, owned and run together with his son Kishin RK.
After a 2011 family settlement between him and his younger sibling Asok Kumar Hiranandani, also a billionaire, he has been on a deal-making spree.
Prize holdings include the 442-room Holiday Inn Express at Clarke Quay, Holiday Inn Little India and the hotel Intercontinental Singapore Robertson Quay.
He bought the Porcelain Hotel in Singapore's Chinatown, which was refurbished and reopened in 2023 as the 134-room Hotel 1900.
abouts: The name RB is derived from the erstwhile Royal Brothers, a 77-year-old property group with roots in textile trading.
Son Kishin's RB Food Group owns a portfolio of brands, such as members' club 1880, cocktail bar Employees Only, Roia restaurant and cloud kitchen company TiffinLabs.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Deng Weiming chairs CNGR Advanced Material, which makes components of lithium batteries, some of which are used in cars.
Customers include battery production firm Contemporary Amperex Technology, Korea-based LG Chem and U.S.-based Tesla.
Deng started his own business in 1995 age 27; he founded CNGR in 2004.
His wife Wu Xiaoge is a CNGR director and vice president.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liquor baron Lalit Khaitan is chairman of the $494 million (revenue) publicly traded spirits maker Radico Khaitan.
The Delhi-based company started off as a bottler before expanding into making bulk alcohol and eventually branded spirits.
Radico Khaitan has a range of brands including 8 M whisky, Contessa rum and Magic Moments vodka.
Khaitan inherited the liquor business from his later father G.N.Khaitan in 1995 after a family division.
abouts: Khaitan's son Abhishek runs Radico Khaitan as managing director.
The company used to be called Rampur Distillery and Chemical Company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mitchell Jacobson began working for MSC Direct, an office and industrial equipment distributor founded by his father Sidney, in 1976.
In 1995, Jacobson took over as CEO of the Melville, N.Y.-based firm, which now distributes hundreds of products, from staplers to air conditioners.
Jacobson held the CEO position through 2005 and, since 2013, has been non-executive chairman.
abouts: Jacobson's parents, who married six weeks after they met, poisoned themselves in 2005 after his father was diagnosed with cancer. They had been married 59 years.
Mitchell has one sister, Marjorie Gershwind Fiverson, whose son Erik is currently the president and CEO of MSC Direct.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Saroj Rani Gupta cofounded APL Apollo Tubes in 1986 with her late husband S.K. Gupta. It was initially called Bihar Tubes.
Delhi-based APL Apollo Tubes is a leading producer of a range of widely used, branded steel products.
Her son, Sanjay Gupta, runs the company as managing director.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Edward Kwok is the older son of property mogul Raymond Kwok, chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
He's served as an alternate company director to his father since 2012, when Raymond and his uncle Thomas became involved in a bribery investigation.
His father was acquitted but Thomas was found guilty of bribing a government official and sentenced to five years in prison in 2014.
He joined Sun Hung Kai in 2010 and is a sales and project manager, responsible for planning and marketing the group's Hong Kong residential projects.
A certified accountant, he worked for international audit firm Deloitte before joining the family business.
abouts: Edward's brother, Christopher, and three of his cousins are also billionaires.
Edward is often seen carrying a white cane because he's visually impaired.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lu Di was an early investor in Chinese drone maker DJI when it was founded in 2006.
Today the Shenzhen-headquartered business is one of the world's largest drone makers.
Lu has been called a "penny pincher" by DJI's CEO Frank Wang.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Peter Sperling stepped down as the chairman of the Apollo Education Group when it was taken private in a $1.1 billion deal in February 2017.
Sperling joined the company in 1983, about a decade after his father founded it.
The for-profit education company became well-known for its online University of Phoenix network.
His father John Sperling, former San Jose State University professor, founded the University of Phoenix in 1973.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ron Corio is the founder and former CEO of Array Technologies, which makes solar tracking systems.
Within half-a-year of the Albuquerque, New Mexico-based company's October 2020 IPO, Corio unloaded his 38% stake for an estimated $1.2 billion before-tax.
Corio founded Array Technologies in 1989; he stepped down as CEO before the IPO and resigned from its board in 2022.
Corio is New Mexico's first billionaire.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hou Juncheng chairs Shanghai-listed Proya Cosmetics,  a supplier of moisturizing and whitening skincare products.
Most of the company's sales come from its "Proya" brand, which are popular among Chinese women between the age of 18 to 24 who reside in small and medium cities.
Hou founded Proya in 2006 as a distributor of local brands such as "Yue Sai" before starting his own product lines.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ruan Shuilong is the largest shareholder in Zhejiang Longsheng Group, a supplier of specialty chemicals and a variety of dyes.
Longsheng's predecessor organization was an insecticide factory founded in a commune set up in the eastern city of Shangyu in 1970.
Longsheng listed at Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2003.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Nicholas (Nick) Pritzker is a cousin of the late Jay Pritzker and his brothers Donald and Robert, who built the Hyatt hotel chain.
Pritzker spent many years leading Hyatt's hotel development efforts, but he has since sold most of his Hyatt stock.
He has shifted his attention and investment dollars to causes like clean energy, marijuana legalization and criminal justice reform.
His venture capital and impact investing firm Tao Capital Partners has invested in Tesla, Uber and Joby Aviation
Pritzker was also an early investor in e-cigarette maker Juul and the synthetic DNA company Twist Biosciences via Tao Capital Partners.
abouts: In the 2016 election, Pritzker donated to Proposition 64, a ballot initiative in California which successfully legalized marijuana in the Golden State.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sam Pollock is the CEO of Brookfield Infrastructure, a spinoff of Toronto-based Brookfield which invests in industries like utilities and data storage.
Pollock has worked for Brookfield since 1994 in several senior roles, including leading its private equity business.
Brookfield raised $30 billion for its fifth flagship infrastructure fund in 2023, the largest such fund ever raised by an investment firm.
Brookfield Infrastructure Partners' publicly-traded stock has generated a 14% annualized return since inception in 2008.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Avram Glazer and his five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.
The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.
The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $4 billion (net of debt).
Avram co-chairs Man U with brother Joel. Joel co-chairs the Bucs with brothers Bryan and Edward. Another brother, Kevin, runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties.
Sister Darcie Glazer Kassewitz is president of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and the Glazer Vision Foundation, which provides eyecare to underserved children.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bryan Glazer and his five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.
The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.
The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $4 billion (net of debt).
Bryan co-chairs the Bucs with brothers Joel and Edward. Joel co-chairs Man U with brother Avram. Another brother, Kevin, runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties.
Sister Darcie Glazer Kassewitz is president of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and the Glazer Vision Foundation, which provides eyecare to underserved children.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Darcie Glazer Kassewitz and her five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.
The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.
The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $4 billion (net of debt).
Darcie is president of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and the Glazer Vision Foundation, which provides eyecare to underserved children.
Brother Kevin runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties. Brothers Joel and Avram co-chair Man U. Joel also co-chairs the Bucs with brothers Bryan and Edward.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Edward Glazer and his five siblings own a controlling stake in English Premier League club Manchester United, which Forbes values at $5.9 billion (net of debt).
The Glazer siblings also own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers, which Forbes values at $5.2 billion net of debt.
Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought Man U for $1.4 billion in 2005 and the Bucs for for $192 million in 1995.
Edward Glazer is co-chairman of the Bucs and oversees real estate acquisitions for the family's First Allied Corporation.
Edward is also founder and CEO of US Property Trust and US Auto Trust, which own and operate retail centers and auto dealerships, respectively.
Through their Edward and Shari Glazer Charitable Trust, Edward and his wife support a variety of organizations, including his mater Ithaca College, where a track and field arena bears their names.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joe Rogers Jr. is the longtime chairman of Waffle House and the son of one of the 24-hour breakfast chain's cofounders.
There are now 2,100 locations in 25 states and estimated annual revenue of over $1 billion.
He was 26 in 1973 when he took the helm of the chain, which had two family ownership groups, mounting debt and control of only 30% of the locations.
Rogers consolidated ownership within his family, which now has a controlling share, while ending the company's reliance on debt.
Rogers also created an employee ownership plan that now provides 3,500 workers (mostly hourly) with a piece of the business.
abouts: Rogers made a point of keeping his diners defiantly open in the face of calamity and showed up in Charleston in 1989 to pour coffee after Hurricane Hugo hit.
In March 2020, the Waffle House index flashed red as sales dropped 70%, 20% of locations closed and thousands of workers were furloughed.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joel Glazer and his five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.
The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.
The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $4 billion (net of debt).
Joel Glazer co-chairs Man U with his brother Avram and the Bucs with his brothers Bryan and Edward. Another brother, Kevin, runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties.
Sister Darcie Glazer Kassewitz is president of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and the Glazer Vision Foundation, which provides eyecare to underserved children.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kevin Glazer and his five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.

Kevin runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties. Brothers Joel and Avram co-chair Man U. Joel also co-chairs the Bucs with brothers Bryan and Edward.
Sister Darcie Glazer Kassewitz is president of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and the Glazer Vision Foundation, which provides eyecare to underserved children.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bill Gross cofounded PIMCO, an investment management firm, in 1971 and became known as a superstar bond fund manager.
He decamped in 2014, and joined Janus Henderson to manage a global macro bond fund; he retired in 2019.
Gross sued PIMCO for wrongful dismissal in 2015. The case was settled in March 2017 for $81 million, which went to the Sue and Bill Gross Foundation.
In 2016, Gross' wife of 31 years, Sue, filed for divorce. She eventually walked away with over $1 billion.
Gross is a 1966 graduate in psychology from Duke University. He has donated millions to his alma mater for financial aid.
abouts: Named after him, the William H. Gross Stamp Gallery at the Smithsonian National Postal is the world's largest gallery dedicated to philately.
Gross, who has Asperger's Syndrome, was prompted to seek diagnosis after reading Michael Lewis's "The Big Short," which features a protagonist with the condition.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Peter Jackson is best known for his "Lord of the Rings" and "The Hobbit" trilogies, which have grossed $6 billion worldwide.
The film director became a billionaire in 2021, after selling a chunk of his Weta digital film effects shop to Unity Software for $1.6 billion in cash and stock.
He made $10 million up front for each of the three "Lord of the Rings" films (2001-2003), with at least another 10% of profits earned from each film's box office receipts.
For the "Hobbit" movies, he likely made $20 million per film with 20% backend.
Jackson's Weta Digital used motion capture of the actor Andy Serkis to create the now-iconic on-screen visualization of the character Gollum.
abouts: Sean Parker, the tech investor known for founding Napster and serving as Facebook's first president, had a 25% stake in Jackson's Weta Digital at the time of sale.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alexander Sixt, together with his brother, Konstantin, owns 56% of Sixt SE, one of the world's largest car rental companies. They are the co-CEOs.
Their grandfather Martin Sixt founded the firm in 1912. Their father, Erich, took over in 1969 when it was a local operation with just 200 vehicles.
Together with his wife, Regine, Erich turned the company into a global player. He stepped down as CEO in 2021; he is chair of the supervisory board.
Sixt SE, which went public in 1986, had 2021 revenues of around $2.5 billion, 7,000 employees and some 2,000 locations in over 100 countries.
Alexander joined Sixt in 2009; he and his brother Konstantin were appointed co-CEOs in 2021 after their father stepped down.
abouts: In 2015, Alexander and his brother Konstantin joined Sixt's executive board.
His mom is still active in the company, in her role as Senior Executive Vice President of Marketing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Konstantin Sixt, together with his brother, Alexander, owns 56% of Sixt SE, one of the world's largest car rental companies. They are the co-CEOs.
Their grandfather Martin Sixt founded the firm in 1912. Their father, Erich, took over in 1969 when it was a local operation with just 200 vehicles.

Sixt SE, which went public in 1986, had 2021 revenues of around $2.5 billion, with 7,000 employees and some 2000 locations in over 100 countries.
Konstantin and Alexander were appointed co-CEOs of Sixt in 2021 after their father stepped down; the brothers had been board members since 2015.
abouts: In 2005, after receiving an MSc in International Accounting and Finance from Cass Business School in London, he assumed responsibility for Sixt's online operations.
His mom is still active in the company, in her role as Senior Executive Vice President of Marketing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Ningbo Shuanglin Auto Parts Co Ltd
Ningbo Shuanglin Auto Parts Co Ltd

bios: Wu Jianbin is chairman of Ningbo Shuanglin Auto Parts, which manufactures auto parts, including automobile accessories, bearings and electronic control modules.
His father Wu Yonglin founded the company in 1987 and stepped down from management in 2006 due to health reasons.
Wu Jianbin's sister Wu Weijing is a director of the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liu Ko-chen, also known as K.C. Liu, is the chairman of Advantech, a supplier of industrial computing devices and software.
Liu cofounded Advantech in 1983 at age 29 with two colleagues from HP Taiwan.
Advantech is the world's largest industrial PC maker with a 41% market share in 2024.
Liu's sons, Wesley and Tony, sit on the board.
abouts: An avid reader of management books, Liu enjoys sharing books with staff, including Built to Last and Blue Ocean Strategy.
Before Advantech he was an R&D engineer and later a sales engineer for HP Taiwan in the Instrument Department.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Christoffel Wiese built his Pepkor retail empire by offering bargain prices in South Africa, and expanded into other African countries.
In 2015, South Africa-based furniture retailer Steinhoff International spent $5.7 billion in cash and stock to acquire Pepkor.
He stepped down as Steinhoff chairman in December 2017 after the company disclosed accounting irregularities. Its share price plummeted and Wiese lost his billionaire status.
Wiese regained his 9-figure fortune 2022 when he settled his dispute with Steinhoff for cash and stock, including a 5% stake in Pepkor.
His most valuable asset is Shoprite, but he also holds stakes in real estate firm Collins Property Group, investment holding company Brait and industrial products distributor Invicta Holdings.
In March 2023, Brait spun off food manufacturer Premier Group in an IPO on the Johannesburg stock exchange; Wiese owns about 47% of the shares.
abouts: Wiese's father owned a sheep and cattle farm and a car dealership.
Wiese studied law at Stellenbosch University but switched gears to go into business.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: George Raymond Zage III is the founder and CEO of Singapore-based investment firm Tiga Investments.
The bulk of his wealth comes from a stake in LGBTQ social networking app Grindr, where he sits on the board.
Grindr went public on the New York Stock Exchange through a SPAC merger in 2022.
Zage worked with U.S. hedge fund Farallon Capital Management for 18 years before setting up Tiga Investments in 2017.
He also has interests in Indonesia's property developer Lippo Karawaci and Australia's mining company Whitehaven Coal.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Malaysian investor Kie Chie Wong, who has lived in Australia since the 1980s, gets the bulk of his wealth from a minority stake in Fortescue Metals Group.
A longtime backer of billionaire Andrew Forrest, Wong once held a 26.5% stake in Fortescue, for which he paid about $1 million in 2003.
Wong was part of a Malaysian consortium, which bought an Australian realtor in 1988.
He reportedly hails from a Sarawak timber family in Malaysia.
Wong and his wife, Ann Pin Lim, also own a farm south of Sydney.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: After cashing out of palm oil giant Wilmar more than a decade ago, former stockbroker Peter Lim focused on healthcare, property and sports.
Lim has consolidated his healthcare businesses in Singapore and Malaysia with his Singapore-listed Thomson Medical Group.
Son Kiat serves as executive vice chairman of Thomson Medical Group. In 2022, he launched the world's first professional football decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) dubbed CO92 DAO.
In 2023, Thomson Medical Group acquired hospital operator Far East Medical Vietnam for $353 million.
Peter ventured into education in 2022, partnering with top British boarding school Wellington College to set up international schools across Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore in the next few years.
abouts: Lim also owns Hotel Football in Manchester, located close to Old Trafford, a stadium that's the home of Manchester United.
Lim, who once made a failed bid to buy English football club Liverpool, owns a controlling stake in Spanish football club Valencia.
The son of a fishmonger, Lim held part-time jobs as a waiter and taxi driver to pay for his college tuition.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Thomas Bruch's retail fortune derives from Globus, with roots dating back to 1828.
Globus operates hypermarkets and DIY stores in Germany, Luxembourg, Russia and Czech Republic. It employs almost 47,000 worldwide.
Bruch owns about 38% of the holding company; the rest is distributed among other family members, a family foundation and a charitable foundation.
The charitable Globus Stiftung -- of which Bruch's wife, Graciela, is CEO -- holds about 26% and will receive Bruch's stake after his death.
In 2020, his son Matthias took over as managing director of Globus, representing the sixth generation of the family to run the firm. He also holds 10% of the company.
abouts: Globus Stiftung has supported more than 400 social projects with $10.5 million. It focuses on supporting youth in their transition from school to work.
Globus offers its 18,500 employees the chance to invest in and profit from the performance of the company though silent partnerships.
Globus offers its employees the chance to invest in and profit from the performance of the company though silent partnerships.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ivan Savvidis, a Greek-Russian businessman, is the founder of Agrocom Group, whose assets included Russian tobacco firm Donskoy Tabak.
Savvidis sold Donskoy Tabak for $1.6 billion to Japan Tabacco in March 2018.
Seen as a Putin ally, Savvidis is a former member of the Russian parliament.
Through his Greek company Dimera, he owns a stake in soccer team FC PAOK in Thessaloniki, Greece, where he also operates a port.
He got his start as a worker at the Don State Tobacco Factory (now Donskoy Tabak) and was elected general director in 1993.
abouts: In 2022 Savvidis bid for the port of Alexandroupoli in northeastern Greece but in the long run the Greek government decided not to sell it.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Yung-tai got his start selling office clocks in 1965. He later expanded into office equipment, furniture and electronics.
Today his listed Aurora Corp., chaired by wife Yuan Hui-Hua since 2018, sells electronics in over 1,500 locations in Taiwan and mainland China.
Aurora also owns real estate, including a 38-story tower, in Shanghai's Lujiazui financial district.
Chen studied economics in college. That department is now part of National Taipei University.
abouts: Chen was born into a well-off family but worked as a small trader and street merchant after his father died in his youth.
Chen founded the Aurora Museum in Shanghai, known for its Buddhist sculptures and jade.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ulrike Meister is among a community of four family heirs who inherited 63% of kitchen appliance manufacturer Rational AG.
Siegfried Meister founded the company in 1973 and died in 2017, at age 78. Its products include ovens, steamers and grills.
Rational has more than a 50% share of the global market for multifunctional food preparation appliances used in large-scale and commercial kitchens.
The company, which went public in 2000, has grown consistently without acquisitions, and prides itself on innovative, energy-efficient technology.
abouts: Siegfried Meister had the idea to cook using steam after disliking how food was prepared at restaurant chain Wienerwald, where he worked previously.
Rational employs over 250 professional chefs, and its products are used in the White House and Buckingham Palace.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jim McKelvey cofounded payments firm Square with Jack Dorsey in 2009 after he had trouble selling a $2,000 art piece from his studio; the company was renamed Block in 2021.
McKelvey remains on Block's board He started a new company, Invisibly, which powers micropayments for journalism and publishing.
He owns nearly 5% of Block stock and has netted at least $270 million from selling Block shares over the years.
A serial entrepreneur, he has started at least seven companies, ranging from a CD cabinet maker to a glass-blowing studio.
He also sits on the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis and started a nonprofit, LaunchCode, to teach people how to program.
In March 2020, he released "The Innovation Stack," a book detailing Square's battle with Amazon to create a better payments system.
abouts: McKelvey is the author of two textbooks on computer science and one textbook called "The Art Of Fire: Beginning Glassblowing."
He hired Jack Dorsey as a teenager to be an engineering intern for his first tech company, Mira.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pascal Vanhalst's fortune stems from Thermote & Vanhalst, also known as TVH Parts, a supplier of spare parts for industrial and agricultural equipment.
He inherited part of the company from his father, Paul Vanhalst, who started TVH with his friend Paul Thermote to repair and resell forklift trucks.
He's reinvested a significant part of his wealth by acquiring European companies through his investment vehicle Quva Invest.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Barbara Benetton is one of two daughters of Gilberto Benetton, who founded the Benetton Group in 1965 with siblings Carlo, Gilberto and Giuliana.
In 2018, with the death of their father, Barbara and her sister Sabrina each inherited part of his fortune; Barbara is not involved in the business.
The Benetton family started knitting and selling colorful sweaters from their home in Treviso, Italy and opened their first store abroad in 1969.
The four siblings later diversified their portfolio, and now own investments in infrastructure, catering, and financial firms.
Each of their families owns a quarter of the main holding, Edizione. Currently, the second generation has taken over its board of directors.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gao Jifan is founder, chairman and CEO of Trina Solar, a Changzhou-based company specializing in solar panels.
Trina Solar, which supplies PV modules and smart energy solutions, listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 2006 before privatizing in 2017.
The company has manufacturing sites across China as well as in Vietnam and Thailand.
abouts: Gao holds bachelor degree in chemistry from Nanjing University and a master degree from Jilin University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Co Ltd
Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology Co Ltd

bios: Hu Yangzhou is the general manager of Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology, one of the world's largest suppliers of surveillance products.
Hu graduated from the Huazhong University of Science and Technology.
Fellow billionaire Gong Hongjia was an early Hikvision investor and is its current vice chairman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Huang Dawen derives his fortune from a stake in Shanghai-listed Hoshine Silicon Industry.
Huang is also the vice chairman of Ningbo Hoshine Apparel.
Hoshine Silicon Industry makes silicon and silicon-related products in China.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Vadim Yakunin founded Protek Center of Implementation in 1990.
Protek, which went public in 2010, is one of the biggest drug distributors in Russia.
Yakunin, who got his start importing computers and writing software, also worked in the tourist business in Hungary.
While in Hungary, he met reps from a large pharmaceutical firm and decided to start importing drugs.
Later he founded the Rigla chain of drug stores, and built a pharmaceutical factory and logistics center near Moscow.
abouts: Sister Yuliya Yakunina is economic director of Protek and a member of Protek's board since 2002.
Yakunin graduated from the Moscow Physical and Technical Institute (MIPT) as engineer-physicist. He holds a degree as a Doctor of Technical Sciences.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kenny Troutt founded long-distance phone company Excel Communications in 1988 and took the company public in 1996.
In 1998, Troutt sold Excel Communications to Teleglobe in a $3.5 billion deal and reinvested the profits in stocks, bonds and horses.
An avid horse racing fan, Troutt owns WinStar Farm in Versailles, Kentucky, breeder of Thoroughbreds including a Kentucky Derby winner.
The son of a single mother who worked as a bartender, Troutt grew up in public housing in Mount Vernon, IL.
abouts: For years, Troutt sponsored his sons' nationally competitive basketball teams, providing jerseys, equipment and even rides on his private jet to tournaments.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Roy Mann cofounded monday.com, a cloud-based platform that allows companies to create their own work management tools, in 2012.
Mann, an Israeli, is co-CEO of the Tel Aviv-based company, which went public on the NASDAQ in 2021.
Mann served as a senior tech leader at Wix.com, an Israeli provider of cloud-based web development tools, from 2010 to 2012. Wix IPO'd in 2013.
A serial entrepreneur, Mann cofounded two other companies before joining Wix: Facebook app Save An Alien and digital marketing firm ntt.co.il.
abouts: Originally called dapulse, monday.com adopted its current name in 2017, as a nod to its international audience (work weeks start on Sundays in Israel).
Zoom and Salesforce both invested in monday.com in a private placement as part of the company's IPO in 2021.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Giammaria Giuliani is a healthcare investor who owns a 5% stake in Royalty Pharma, the world's largest acquirer of pharmaceutical royalties.
Royalty Pharma went public in 2020 and has collected revenue slices of blockbuster drugs like Humira, Imbruvica, Lyrica and Xtandi.
Giammaria and his brother Mario also own stakes in Swiss investment company HBM Healthcare Investments and a number of biotech firms in the U.S.
The brothers share ownership of their family's pharmaceutical company, Giuliani, founded by their great-grandfather Germano in Milan, Italy in 1889.
They also own real estate investments in Europe and the U.S., including a planned commercial and residential project on a maritime platform in Monaco.
abouts: The family company's best-known product is Amaro Giuliani, a herbal digestive remedy invented by Germano, a chemist, when he bought a pharmacy in Milan in 1889.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xu Shugen is the founder and chairman of Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Dingli Machinery.
Founded in 2005, Dingli manufactures industrial lifts.
Xu's brother, Xu Zhilong, is a board member.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Artem Khachatryan cofounded Russian discount retailer Fix Price in 2007 together with Sergei Lomakin.
The chain has opened more than 4,000 stores across Russia, Kazakhstan, Georgia, Belarus, Latvia, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.
Khachatryan was previously the executive director of the company, which went public in 2021.
In December 2023 Khachatryan sold his entire stake in FixPrice and resigned as a member of the board, citing family matters.
His cofounder, Lomakin, is also a billionaire.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ron Sim is the founder of OSIM International, maker of high-end massage chairs.
He took the company private in 2016 when its shares had dropped steeply from their 2014 high.
In both 2018 and 2022, V3 Brands Asia, part of his V3 Group, filed for an IPO in Hong Kong but shelved it due to market volatility.
He owns a majority stake in the popular Bacha Coffee, a more than century-old Moroccan cafe chain, in Singapore.
Sim also has a sizable property portfolio that includes a stake in Perennial Holdings, which was taken private in 2020.
abouts: At age 20, he started a company that sold knife sharpeners and other household goods.
Sim has founded R3 Asset Management to back fast-growing companies.
His Futuristic brand supplies wooden and metal store fixtures to a range of retailers from Levi's to Gap to Bath & Body Works.
His fortune also includes stakes in listed companies such as GHY Media (a film production and distribution company) and Jumbo (a seafood restaurant chain).

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Franziska Wuerbser is the daughter of Gabriella Meister, who is one of four family heirs who inherited 63% of kitchen appliance manufacturer Rational AG.
Rational has more than a 50% share of the global market for food preparation appliances used in large-scale and commercial kitchens.
The company, which went public in 2000, has grown without acquisitions, and prides itself on innovative, energy-efficient technology.
More than 2,200 employees work for Rational AG, which is headquartered just outside Munich, Germany.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gabriella Meister and her daughter Franziska Wuerbser, who is also a billionaire, are among four family heirs who inherited 63% of kitchen appliance manufacturer Rational AG.
Gabriella's late husband, Siegfried Meister, founded the company in 1973 and died in 2017, at age 78.
Rational has more than a 50% share of the global market for multifunctional food preparation appliances used in large-scale and commercial kitchens.
The company's products include ovens, steamers and grills.
Rational, which went public in 2000, has grown consistently without acquisitions, and prides itself on innovative, energy-efficient technology.
abouts: Siegfried Meister had the idea to cook using steam after disliking how food was prepared at restaurant chain Wienerwald, where he worked previously.
Rational employs over 250 professional chefs, and its products are used in the White House and Buckingham Palace.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kwek Leng Keow inherited a stake in Hong Leong Group from his father, Kwek Hong Leong, whose brother, Kwek Hong Png, founded the group in 1941.
Kwek Leng Keow is the brother of Kwek Leng Peck, who is the executive chairman of Singapore-listed Hong Leong Asia, which makes, trades and distributes cement and steel products.
He's the managing director of Hong Realty, a unit of Hong Leong Investment Holdings.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kwek Leng Peck is the executive chairman of Singapore-listed Hong Leong Asia, which makes, trades and distributes cement and steel products.
Singapore billionaires Kwek Leng Beng and Kwek Leng Kee are his cousins.
Kwek has a board seat in the family's Hong Leong Finance.
He inherited a stake in Hong Leong Group from his father, Kwek Hong Leong, who cofounded it with the fathers of Kwek Leng Beng and Kwek Leng Kee.
In 2020, Kwek caused a stir by resigning from the board of flagship City Developments, citing differences with the management, such as the company's investments in China.
abouts: Kwek is a trained accountant.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jeffrey Gundlach is the cofounder of mutual fund company, DoubleLine Capital, which manages $91 billion in assets.
The bond-trader extraordinaire is known for his bold calls and correctly predicted the housing crash in 2007.
He previously helped build the fixed-income business at TCW, before he was fired in 2009.
He is an avid modern art collector and owns works by artists including Warhol, Mondrian and de Kooning.
abouts: Gundlach used to be the drummer in a punk rock band.
He became interested in the investments business after learning of the earnings potential in an episode of "Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous."

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pawan Munjal is the chairman and managing director of Hero MotoCorp,the world's largest producer of two-wheelers by volume having sold more than 120 million units to date.
He inherited a stake in the Hero group after his father Brijmohan Lall Munjal, who cofounded the enterprise with his brothers, died in 2015 at age 92.
A former partner of Honda, Hero MotoCorp parted ways with the Japanese company in 2011. Since then Pawan has led a global expansion with factories in Colombia and Bangladesh.
The group's renewable energy arm, Hero Future Energies, along with U.S. private equity firm KKR, is investing $450 million in expanding capacity.
abouts: In 2022, Hero launched Vida, its first electric scooter.
In 2023, the Delhi High Court stayed a federal investigation into allegations that he took money out of the country illegally. He's denied any wrongdoing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Christine Franken is one of the three daughters of Horst Sartorius, who passed on a 50% stake in biopharmaceutical firm Sartorius AG after his death in 1998.
er great-grandfather Florenz Sartorius founded the firm in 1870 to make analytical balances to measure small mass in laboratories.
Sartorius AG, which went public in 1990, makes pharmaceutical and laboratory equipment.
Today, the company has around 10,600 employees and annual revenue exceeding $2.5 billion.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mike Repole cofounded sports drink BodyArmor in 2011 and serves as the company's chairman.
Coca-Cola bought 15% of BodyArmor in 2018, then purchased the rest in 2021 for $5.6 billion, the company's largest acquisition of a brand.
BodyArmor's investors included tennis star Naomi Osaka and the late Kobe Bryant, who discovered the brand while rehabbing from a torn Achilles tendon.
The son of a waiter and a seamstress, Repole studied sports management at St. John's before working in sales for a small company, Mistic Beverage.
Repole also cofounded Glaceau, maker of the popular brands Vitaminwater and Smartwater, which he also sold to Coca-Cola, in 2007.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bernd Freier opened his first clothing store in Wuerzburg, Germany in 1969. He named it Sir Oliver after the hero of Dickens' novel Oliver Twist.
The company, whose name was later shortened to s.Oliver, initially focused on standard mix-and-match casual fare.
It has diversified into underwear, beachwear and nightwear, as well as licensing and sub-labels for evening clothes and trend-focused collections.
With annual sales of around $1.5 billion, s.Oliver now has more than 700 stores and partner stores in over 20 countries.
Freier stepped down as CEO in 2014 but took over again in 2018. He stepped down once more in  2019.
abouts: Freier's son Christian has taken his place on s.Oliver's advisory council.
s.Oliver has been a big sponsor of German sports including soccer and basketball.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sue Gross is the ex-wife of PIMCO cofounder and billionaire Bill Gross. The two divorced in 2017 after 32 years of marriage.
Gross walked away with roughly $1.3 billion, including a $36 million house in Laguna Beach and half of the couple's art collection.
After the divorce, she sold a Picasso painting for $35 million and purchased a number of properties in Orange County.
In 2017, Sue Gross started her own charitable vehicle, Sue J. Gross Foundation.
Previously the couple had run the William and Sue Gross Family Foundation, which supported Doctors Without Borders, Columbia U. and Duke U.
abouts: Gross apparently got custody of two of she and her ex-husband's three cats in their divorce settlement.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lin Fanlian is chairman of Order Group, whose interests include energy, real estate and finance.
Order is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Linyi in Shandong Province.
Lin Fanlian was reportedly born into a farming family in a small village of Shandong Province; he dropped out of school and worked as construction worker as a teen.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Torsten Toeller encountered pet supply superstores during a visit to the U.S. in the late 1980s and decided the concept deserved a try in his native Germany.
When he opened his first Fressnapf store in 1990, in Erkelenz, customers were initially unimpressed with his selection and prices.
Toeller doubled down by selling his car to raise cash, invested in more inventory and went for broke with aggressive discounts.
The gamble paid off, and in 1992 Fressnapf Tiernahrungs GmbH began opening franchise stores, paving the way for rapid growth.
Today, with over 20,000 people working in approximately 2,600 stores in 15 countries, it is Europe's largest pet-focused chain.
abouts: Toeller has invested in an office building project called Mercator One in Duisburg, close to the company's headquarters in Krefeld.
He is a car fanatic and former sailor.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Wolong Real Estate Group Co Ltd
Wolong Real Estate Group Co Ltd

bios: Chen controls Wolong Real Estate, a property developer, and Wolong Electric, a supplier of motors, power transmission equipment and batteries.
Wolong Electric acquired the parent of ATB Group of Austria in 2011; it's one of the largest suppliers of industrial electric drive systems in Europe.
Chen's daughter Yanni chairs Wolong Real Estate.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Eduard Kučera is the cofounder of Prague-based internet security company Avast Software.
In 1988, he and Pavel Baudis, with whom he'd worked at Research Institute of Mathematical Machines, cofounded ALWIL to sell an antivirus software.
Following the fall of Communism in 1989, the pair broke off to establish what would become Avast.
Now run by an outside CEO, Avast, which secures online activities for more than 435 million users, went public in 2018.
In 2021, Avast, which Kučera chaired Avast from 2006 to 2014, agreed to merge with cybersecurity firm NortonLifeLock.
abouts: Kučera is one of the biggest watch collectors in Czechia; he also owns a significant vintage car collection with his son.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jung-min and her younger sister, Jung-youn, each own a stake in NXC, which is the largest shareholder in online gaming giant Nexon.
The sisters inherited the bulk of their stakes from their father Kim Jung-ju, who founded Nexon in 1994; he died in 2022 at age 54.
Neither Jung-min nor her sister has been involved in Nexon's operation. Little is known about them.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jung-youn and her older sister, Jung-min, each own a stake in NXC, which is the largest shareholder in online gaming giant Nexon.
The sisters inherited the bulk of their stakes from their father Kim Jung-ju, who founded Nexon in 1994; he died in 2022 at age 54.
Neither Jung-youn nor her sister has been involved in Nexon's operation. Little is known about them.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Guodong draws his wealth from a stake in Chinese jewelry maker Laopu Gold.
Dubbed by consumers as "Hermes of gold jewelry," the luxury brand features traditional Chinese design and craftsmanship.
It went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2024.
An individual investor, Chen also made investments in real estate, IT and biotech. He worked for over two decades at China's IT conglomerate Legend Holdings until 2016.
He held a teaching post for four years at Renmin University of China after graduating there with a master's degree in economics and management.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Paolo Bulgari, a great-grandson of the founder of luxury jeweler Bulgari, joined the company when he was 18.
A law student at the time, he was asked by his father to design necklaces, rings and bracelets.
Paolo became chairman of Bulgari in 1984, while his brother Nicola became vice chairman.
In 2011, the Bulgari family sold its controlling stake to French luxury conglomerate LVMH for $5.2 billion in cash and stock.
abouts: Paolo has designed jewelry for generations of Hollywood actresses, from Elizabeth Taylor to Nicole Kidman.
Bulgari financed a year-long restoration project of the Spanish Steps in Rome for a reported $1.6 million and wants restricted access to the monument to protect it.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Benoit Dageville is president of products at Snowflake, the cloud-based database company he cofounded with Thierry Cruanes in 2012.
The French-born computer science PhD got his start at Bull Information Systems before spending 16 years at Oracle in California's Bay Area.
Dageville and Cruanes, both architects at Oracle, teamed up on a startup to store a company's data in the cloud to make it more easily usable.
Snowflake went public in 2020 with a $3.9 billion offering, making it the largest software IPO in history.
The company has been registered in Bozeman, Montana since 2021, but has no official headquarters.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jared Isaacman is the founder and CEO of Allentown, Pennsylvania-based payment processing firm Shift4 Payments.
Shift4 handles payments for a third of America's restaurants and hotels; Isaacman took it public in 2020.
He started the firm at age 16 in his parents' basement in Far Hills, New Jersey in 1999.
In 2011, he founded Draken International, a defense firm that trains Air Force pilots and owns the world's largest private fleet of military aircraft.
He sold a majority stake in Draken to Wall Street firm Blackstone in 2019 for a nine-figure sum.
Isaacman was nominated by Donald Trump in January 2025 to serve as the administrator of NASA.
abouts: Isaacman is a fighter jet pilot and his call sign is "Rook."
In 2019, he bought a Soviet-era Mikoyan MiG-29 fighter jet from the estate of Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen (d. 2018).

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hisako Yamamoto is the daughter of Seven & I Holding's late honorary chairman Masatoshi Ito and gets her  wealth from her stake in the global retailing giant.
Her  two siblings are also billionaires based on their stakes.
Masatoshi Ito, who helped build 7-Eleven into a global giant, died in March 2023 at age 98.
Seven & i Holdings has close to 80,000 stores in 19 countries and nearly $80 billion in annual revenue.
The company is best known for its thousands of 7-Eleven convenience stores in Japan, the U.S. and China.
abouts: The company also runs Denny's restaurants in Japan and owns department stores, supermarkets, and financial services firms.
The family was considering a $58 billion management buyout of the company but backed out in February 2025 citing financial issues.
In 2024, Canada's Alimentation Couche-Tard made a $47 billion takeover bid for the Japanese company.
In March 2025, the company announced a massive share buyback plan in a bid to bolster the share price - in light of the takeover offer.
In March 2025, Seven & I agreed to sell its York Holdings unit, which includes major supermarket chains and specialty retailers, to Bain Capital for $5.4 billion.

Masatoshi Ito, who helped build 7-Eleven into a global giant, died in March 2023 at age 98.

bios: Yasuhisa Ito, the son of Seven & I Holding's late honorary chairman Masatoshi Ito, gets his wealth from his stake in the global retailing giant.
His two siblings are also billionaires based on their stakes.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: JB Straubel is the founder and CEO of Redwood Materials and the former chief technology officer of Tesla.
A Stanford-educated engineer, Straubel was working on battery-powered planes in 2003 when he met Elon Musk at a campus lecture.
He joined Tesla as employee No. 5 in 2004, and drove the development of its battery packs and electric motors as CTO. He left the C-suite in 2019 but remains on the board.
He now runs Redwood Materials, a Nevada-based electric vehicle battery recycling startup  he founded in 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Suh Kyung-bae is the chairman of Amorepacific, South Korea's largest cosmetic and skincare maker by revenue.
He's capitalized on the Hallyu wave, a keen interest in Korean pop culture that has swept Asia and the U.S.
The only one out of six children interested in the business, Suh joined the company in the 1980s and became CEO in 1997.
abouts: Amorepacific traces its roots to Suh's grandmother, who sold camellia oil as a hair treatment across the Korean peninsula.
In the 1960s Amorepacific hired women who went from door to door selling products on commission; some of them had lost their husbands in the Korean War.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Aziz Akhannouch is the majority owner of Akwa Group, a multibillion-dollar conglomerate founded by his father and a partner, Ahmed Wakrim, in 1932.
It has interests in petroleum, gas and chemicals through publicly-traded Afriquia Gaz and Maghreb Oxygene.
Akhannouch was appointed prime minister of Morocco in Sept 2021.
abouts: His wife Salwa Idrissi runs her own company, which has franchises for Gap, Gucci and Ralph Lauren in Morocco.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Van Lieshout founded and made his fortune from the Super A-Mart furniture chain. He sold it in 2006 but retained the freehold to some stores.
His wealth is now underpinned by a large property portfolio that includes shopping malls and offices.
He also owns Unison Projects, which has property interests in residential, industrial and commercial assets.
He arrived in Australia in 1960 with his parents and 12 siblings, emigrating from the Netherlands.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hitesh Doshi is chairman and managing director of Waaree Energies, India's largest manufacturer of solar panels by capacity.
Mumbai-based Waaree Energies was listed on the Indian bourses in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price.
The company has five solar module manufacturing plants in India.
He founded the business in 1990 as a manufacturer of thermal and pressure gauges used in industrial boilers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pharma tycoon Habil Khorakiwala chairs Wockhardt, one of India's top makers of generic drugs.
He founded Wockhardt in 1967 after breaking away from his family's storied retailing empire.
His son Murtaza runs the Mumbai company which counts the U.K. as one of its top markets.
abouts: His daughter Zahabiya oversees the hospital arm while another son heads the charitable foundation.
Khorakiwala has served as the honorary consul general of Sweden in India.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joseph Steinberg is the chairman of Jefferies Financial Group, a New York-based financial services firm best known for investment banking.
He served as president of Leucadia National Corporation, an investment firm which was often compared to a mini-Berkshire Hathaway, from 1979 to 2013.
During his time at the helm, Leucadia purchased companies like National Beef and helped finance Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management.
In 2013, the firm merged with Jefferies and Steinberg became chairman. The combined company changed its name to Jefferies Financial Group in 2018.
Steinberg also serves as a director of Crimson Wine Group, which owns vineyards in California, Oregon and Washington.
abouts: Since 2015, Joseph and wife Diane have donated over $15 million through their charitable trust to museums, colleges and community centers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Haluk Bayraktar owns 47.5% of Turkish unmanned military drone manufacturer Baykar. He co-owns it with his brother Selçuk and serves as the CEO.
The company was founded by his father Özdemir in 1984 to make parts for the Turkish auto industry and began making unmanned aerial vehicles in the 2000s.
Baykar recorded sales of $1.9 billion in 2023 and its exports rose to $1.8 billion in 2024, thanks to contracts with militaries in Europe, Africa and the Middle East.
Baykar's most famous export, the Bayraktar drone, has been used so successfully by Ukrainian troops that it inspired a popular folk song.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pharma distributor's son Satish Mehta founded and runs generics maker Emcure Pharmaceuticals, headquartered in Pune city.
He started Emcure as a contract manufacturer for multinationals in 1981 then went on to sell his own branded generics.
After getting investors such as Bain Capital, he listed the company at a 31% premium in July 2024.
Daughter Namita, an MBA graduate from the Fuqua School of Business and a trained chartered accountant, has a board seat. She's a judge on the Indian version of Shark Tank.
Son Samit, who has an MBA from Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania, is also a director on Emcure's board.
abouts: Mehta's son-in-law and nephew work with him.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Akshay Arora is the chairman of Mumbai-based pharma company Blue Jet Healthcare.
The 56-year-old company makes chemical agents that are used to enhance the visibility of body tissues in medical imaging, such as X rays, CT scans and MRI scans.
It also manufactures artificial sweeteners and pharma ingredients.
The company was listed on the Indian bourses in 2023 at a 10% premium to the issue price.
His son, Shiven, who studied business at Australia's Bond University, is the company's managing director.
abouts: The company was established as Jet Chemicals in 1968 by his later father B.L.Arora.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alberto Coppel Luken and his four brothers own the family's retailing and banking giant, Grupo Coppel.
Their father and grandfather started the company in 1941 as a small shop in Sinaloa called "El Regalo."
Coppel is the CEO and chairman of GC1 Holding; owner of sake producer Nami and software company ClickBalance.
GC1 Holding's venture capital arm had investments in Spotify, Uber and Pinterest before they went public.
Coppel, who was previously director of stores in the Coppel Group, is a civil engineer with a degree from the Monterrey Institute of Technology.
abouts: He is the vice president of Pronatura Noroeste, a conservation organization in Northwest Mexico.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: José Coppel and his four brothers own Grupo Coppel, a Mexican conglomerate with over 1,700 department stores.
Their father and grandfather founded the first shop in 1941 selling radios and watches. Today, the stores sell everything from clothing to electronics.
The stores are known for providing credit to customers, allowing them to finance their purchases over multiple payments.
The group expanded into the banking sector with BanCoppel in 2007.
abouts: The brothers also have two sisters who don't have active roles in the business.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Fumio Kaneko is the president of waste management company Daiei Kankyo, which he founded with three others in 1979.
