The company has expanded into waste recycling, power generation using waste and soil remediation.
Daiei Kankyo was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2022.
The company reported $560 million in revenue in the fiscal year through March 2025.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Robert "Bob" Fisher is one of three sons of Gap founders Donald (d. 2009) and Doris Fisher.
He is managing director of the Fisher family's investment firm, Pisces, and chaired Gap's board until 2020.
Like his two billionaire brothers, he attended Princeton, where he played tennis and majored in English, before heading to Stanford's business school.
A philanthropist, Fisher cofounded the California Water Foundation, which focuses on improving California's water supply, in 2010.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hamdi Akin is the founder of Akfen Holding, a conglomerate with investments in energy, real estate development and infrastructure.
During college, he produced heating boilers and water and fuel tanks in his father's workshop. After graduating, he started Akfen as a contractor.
Winning tenders for operating the Istanbul Ataturk Airport and Ankara Esenboga Airport led him to establish TAV Airports Holding.
In 2012, he sold 38% of TAV to Aeroports de Paris Group for $874 million. In 2017, he sold his remaining 8% to Aeroports de Paris for $160 million.
Today, Afken is mainly focused on renewable energy, building hospitals and developing and renting apartments to students.
abouts: Akin has transferred ownership of Akfen to daughter Pelin and son Selim. They both serve on its board.
In December 2015, he donated six flats he owned in a compound in Istanbul Beylikduzu to Syrian refugees.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pankaj Doshi draws his wealth from a minority stake in Waaree Energies, India's largest manufacturer of solar panels by capacity.
Mumbai-based Waaree Energies listed on the Indian bourses in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price.
The stock market debut of the company made him and his three brothers billionaires.
It has five solar module manufacturing plants in India.
The company was originally founded in 1990 as a manufacturer of thermal and pressure gauges used in industrial boilers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Taiwan Shin Kong Security Co. Ltd.

bios: Eugene Wu is the founder of Shin Kong Financial Holding, one of Taiwan's largest financial companies.
Wu stepped down as the firm's chairman in 2020, after 18 years at the helm. His daughter, Olivia, was named president upon his departure.
His brother, Thomas, runs his own financial services firm, Taishin Holdings, and is also a billionaire.
Shin Kong and Taishin are planning a merger in July 2025 to create Taiwan's fourth-largest financial holding company with nearly $260 billion in total assets.
Eugene's late father, Wu Ho-Su, built a fortune in trading and textiles starting in the 1940s.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hans Thomann is managing director of Thomann, one of Europe's largest music retailers with locations in Germany, France and Denmark, among others.
Thomann took over the business from his father, who started the company in 1954, and expanded it during the dot-com-era of the 1990s and 2000s.
Today Thommann employs more than 1,800 people who come from 55 countries.
The company is still headquartered in the small German town of Treppendorf.
The sole owner of the company, Thomann became involved in the business when he was 12 years of age.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gerald Schwartz is the founder and chairman of Onex, one of Canada's largest private equity firms, which he ran for 39 years before stepping down in May 2023.
He got his start working with buyout legends Jerome Kohlberg, Henry Kravis and George Roberts at Bear Stearns in the 1970s.
The Americans left to start KKR in 1976; Schwartz went home to Canada and cofounded the media company CanWest in 1977.
In 1984 he started Onex, which now has $50 billion in assets under management and offices in London, Toronto and the U.S.
abouts: Schwartz also serves as a director of bookstore chain Indigo Books & Music, which his wife, Heather Reisman, founded and runs.
The couple's HESEG Foundation provides full academic scholarships and living expenses to lone soldiers who travel to Israel to serve in the Israel Defense Forces.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Nelson Peltz, an activist investor, is a founder of investment firm Trian Fund Management.
Trian now has $8.5 billion in assets under management.
The firm has a highly concentrated portfolio that includes stakes in Bank of New York Mellon, DuPont and food conglomerate Mondelez International.
In early 2017, Peltz battled with Proctor & Gamble over a board seat the company didn't want to grant him. He ultimately won the seat.
Peltz's daughter, Nicola, married Brooklyn Beckham, son of soccer player David Beckham, in April 2022 at the family's mansion in Palm Beach, Florida.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Real estate developer Charles Cohen bought out his father and uncle and quadrupled the family real estate empire to 12 million square feet.
Most of his fortune is in high end office buildings in New York City and design centers in several cities.
WeWork leases office space from Cohen Brothers Realty's 750 Lexington Avenue in Manhattan and the Pacific Design Center in Los Angeles.
Cohen owns high end luxury brands such as Harrys of London, Savile Row tailor Richard James and luggage company T. Anthony.
In 2018, he bought movie theater chain Landmark Theatres from Mark Cuban and picked up Manhattan society magazine Avenue.
He owns or has the rights to some 1,000 classic films.
abouts: Cohen wrote the 1985 movie quiz book "Trivia Mania."
Cohen is buying and renovating historic movie theaters like Paris cinema La Pagode, the Larchmont Playhouse and the reopened Quad Cinema in Manhattan.
Cohen produced the 2008 Oscar-nominated "Frozen River" and distributed five foreign films nominated by the Academy Awards. He won for "The Salesman."

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jennifer Steinbrenner Swindal is a general partner of the New York Yankees, the most valuable in baseball.
Her father, George, led a 12-person group of investors that bought the team from CBS for $10 million in 1973.
The Steinbrenner family also collectively owns more than 25% of YES Network, 20% of MLS's New York City FC, a stake in Legends Hospitality and 10% of Italian soccer club AC Milan.
George died in 2010, leaving an estimated one-fourth of his estate to each of Jennifer and her three siblings.
abouts: George Steinbrenner died during a one-year repeal of the federal estate tax, saving his kids an estimated $600 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jessica Steinbrenner is a general partner of the New York Yankees, the most valuable in baseball.
Her father, George, led a 12-person group of investors that bought the team from CBS for $10 million in 1973.
The Steinbrenner family also collectively owns more than 25% of YES Network, 20% of MLS's New York City FC, a stake in Legends Hospitality and 10% of Italian soccer club AC Milan.
George died in 2010, leaving an estimated one-fourth of his estate to each of Jessica and her three siblings.
abouts: George Steinbrenner died during a one-year repeal of the federal estate tax, saving his kids an estimated $600 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yoshiaki Yoshida is the founder of Japanese beauty brand DHC. He started the company in 1972 to provide translation services.
In 1980, he started the cosmetics business using organic olives. In 1983, he got into the mail order segment. It also sells nutritional supplements and health foods.
The privately held company sells both through retail stores and online.
In 2023, Yoshida sold his company to Japanese leasing giant Orix, which valued it at ¥300 billion.
abouts: DHC stands for Daigaku Honyaku Center.
Yoshida is a supporter of conservative political causes and has his own TV production company providing online and broadcast content.
DHC sources its olive oil from organic olive groves in Spain.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Oyler is the CEO and cofounder of biotech outfit BeiGene. He owns about 5% of the publicly traded company.
BeiGene, which was founded in 2010 as a research and development firm, went public on the Nasdaq in 2016 and listed in Hong Kong two years later.
Before he cofounded BeiGene, Oyler helped start and then sell two companies in the U.S. and China.
He sold Telephia, a consumer telecom research firm he founded in 1997, to The Nielsen Co. for $449 million in 2007.
Oyler's next success came with drug discovery outsourcing company BioDuro, which he founded in 2005 and sold to PPD Inc. for $77 million in 2010.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Christina Flügel is a fifth-generation member of the Mast-Jägermeister family fortune, best known for its green-bottled herbal liquor.
Her brother, Florian Rehm, a fellow German billionaire, chairs the company and serves as its spokesperson.
Mast-Jägermeister was founded in 1878 as a maker of vinegar; it shifted to producing wine and spirits in 1922 before creating the now-famous recipe for Jägermeister.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stewart Butterfield is the cofounder and CEO of team-based messaging software Slack.
In July 2021, cloud software giant Salesforce acquired Slack for $27.7 billion in cash and stock.
Butterfield departed Salesforce in December 2022, amid an exodus of executives at the software giant.
Butterfield and wife Jen Rubio, the founder of luggage startup Away, sold their San Francisco home in 2021 and moved to Aspen.
Though he leads a tech company, Butterfield proudly majored in philosophy as an undergraduate at Canada's University of Victoria.
abouts: Butterfield cofounded image hosting site Flickr in 2003; it was purchased by Yahoo for $35 million in 2005.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Eusebio Tanco is chairman of STI Education Systems Holdings, an educational institution with 63 schools across the Philippines, about 40% of which are franchised.
He also chairs digital entertainment company DigiPlus Interactive that runs online gaming platform BingoPlus.
Tanco is president of Philippine First Insurance and Asian Terminals, a shipping and logistics company.
His Tanco Group has other interests in property, energy and financial servies.
Son Joseph Augustin L. and daughter Maria Vanessa Rose L. are directors of STI; cousin Martin K. serves as non-executive director.
abouts: Tanco started his career in the insurance and property industries in the mid 1970s after graduation.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Antti Aarnio-Wihuri heads Wihuri Group, a Finnish conglomerate that has been in his family for over 100 years.
The group has interests in the packaging, technical trade, food wholesale and aviation and operates Caterpillar construction equipment dealerships.
Wihuri Group, which employs 5,000 people, also runs Metro daily goods wholesale stores and a private jet charter and ambulance service.
He is the largest shareholder of Winpak, a Canadian company that specializes in producing packaging materials.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhang Shilong chairs SG Micro, a supplier of integrated circuits for automotive and industrial markets.
Zhang worked as an engineer under China's Ministry of Railways and at Texas Instruments earlier in his career.
SG Micro went public and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Karl-Johan Persson, the third generation of his family to head up H&M, was appointed to chairman of the fast fashion favorite in 2020.
He served as CEO from 2009 when he took the reins from his father, billionaire Stefan Persson.
Karl-Johan's grandfather, Erling Persson, founded H&M in 1947.
The company has since grown into a global retail power house with more than 4,400 stores in 66 countries.
Persson's sister Charlotte S'derstr?m, brother Tom Persson, and aunt Lottie Tham, are also billionaires.
abouts: Crown princess Victoria is the godmother to one of his children.
Karl-Johan is an active investor in unlisted Nordic tech companies, including online food grocer MatHem.se.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dean Solon founded Shoals Technologies in 1996; it makes electrical gear for some of the biggest U.S. solar installations.
Solon, who stepped down as CEO to join the board, owns 40% of Shoals Technologies Group, which had its IPO in January 2021.
Solon got his start at age 8 carrying his dad's toolbox to repair air conditioners; by 16 he had his own customers.
He dropped out of Purdue University and was soon designing and manufacturing automotive parts.
He is the author of two dozen patents pertaining to solar gear.
abouts: Since the 1970s Solon has visited Disney World at least twice a year. His favorite movie is Beauty And The Beast.
Shoals makes all its solar gear at four factories in Tennessee and Alabama; the company charges more than most competitors, but its products are seen as safer, more reliable and easier to install.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: St?phane Bonvin founded Investis, a Swiss residential real estate firm, in 1994.
Investis' portfolio consists of more than 3,000 apartments in the Lake Geneva region.
He took Investis public in 2016 on Swiss stock exchange SIX.
In 2006, Bonvin cofounded a private equity group called Patrimonium, where he was managing director until 2015.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hal Steinbrenner is the managing general partner of the New York Yankees, the most valuable in baseball.
His father, George, led a 12-person group of investors that bought the team from CBS for $10 million in 1973.
The Steinbrenner family also collectively owns more than 25% of YES Network, 20% of MLS's New York City FC, a stake in Legends Hospitality and 10% of Italian soccer club AC Milan.
George died in 2010, leaving an estimated one-fourth of his estate to each of Hal and his three siblings.
abouts: George Steinbrenner died during a one-year repeal of the federal estate tax, saving his kids an estimated $600 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chu Mang Yee is a former government official who controls Hong Kong-listed real estate developer Hopson Development.
Chu's daughter, Chu Kut Yung, is the company's chairman.
Over his business career, Chu has built experience in trading and construction as well as real estate development.
Founded in 1992, Hopson focused on mid- and high-end residential projects.
Over his business career, Chu has build experience in trading and construction as well as real estate development.
Kut Yung is a graduate of Renmin University with a finance degree.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lee Su-jin is the founder and chairman of South Korean travel superapp Yanolja.
SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 invested $1.7 billion in the company in 2021.
Orphaned as a child, Lee worked as a janitor at love hotels before starting Yanolja in 2005.
abouts: Yanolja means "Hey, let's play" in Korean.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Laurans (Larry) Mendelson has been the CEO of Heico Corporation, an aerospace and electronics company, since 1990.
He and his sons, Victor and Eric, first purchased Heico stock after Victor identified a buyout opportunity in the late 1980s.
Larry was working in real estate before he put in an original $5 million stake into Heico with his sons.
His first job out of graduate school was at Arthur Anderson & Company where he worked for around six years.
Columbia University's Mendelson Center for Undergraduate Business Initiatives was established in 2016 with a gift from the Mendelson family.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ronald Perelman is a dealmaker who built a fortune with a diverse array of holdings, from candy to cosmetics.
Perelman sold assets worth billions of dollars to pay off debt in late 2020 after the Covid-19 pandemic ravaged his businesses.
He was a longtime shareholder of cosmetics giant Revlon but lost his holdings during its 2023 bankruptcy proceedings. His daughter Debra was the firm's CEO from 2018 to 2023.
Perelman learned about business from his father. He attended board meetings with him while in elementary school.
He is a prolific art collector who has sold off much of his collection in recent years.
abouts: Perelman's foundation pledged $65 million to Princeton in 2018 but did not follow through, prompting the school to remove his name in 2021 from a new dorm.
Perelman has eight children from five wives.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gan is cofounder and chairman of Shanghai-listed Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals.
Founded in 1998, the company produces insulin and injection pens and is publicly traded.
Gan graduated from Peking University and later became a teacher in the biology department.
Gan holds a PhD from Michigan State University and worked for Merck before starting Gan & Lee.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: In 2019, Karen Beckmann Legorreta inherited a nearly 36% stake in Becle S.A.B., maker of Jose Cuervo tequila, from her father, Juan Francisco Beckmann Vidal.
She serves on the board of Becle; her brother Juan Domingo Beckmann Legorreta is the CEO.
The company has been controlled by the family for more than 250 years and has distilleries and bottling facilities across Mexico, the United States and Northern Ireland.
abouts: In 2023, Becle sold more than 27 million nine-liter cases of alcohol, bringing in more than $21 billion in sales.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cho Hyun-joon is the chairman of Hyosung Group, whose interests include textiles, chemicals and construction.
He is the eldest son of the late former chairman Cho Seok-rae, who stepped down in 2016 and passed away in 2024.
Cho worked at Mitsubishi International and Morgan Stanley before joining Hyosung.
He was sentenced to prison in 2016 for embezzlement; he appealed the conviction. Cho's sentencing was suspended for three years, allowing him to continue running Hyosung.
abouts: Cho's uncle is Hankook Tire honorary chairman Cho Yang-Rai.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sidney Kimmel founded apparel company Jones Group more than four decades ago; it owned brands including Stuart Weitzman and Nine West.
In 2014, he sold the company for $2.2 billion to private equity firm Sycamore Partners.
He owns production company Sidney Kimmel Entertainment, which produced the films 'Hell or High Water' and 'The Kite Runner.'
Kimmel donated $110 million to Thomas Jefferson University in 2014.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Jianfeng chairs Ningbo Joyson, a manufacturer of automotive accessories.
Wang is an avid photographer whose work has been exhibited in the Ningbo Museum of Art.
Joyson is headquartered in the coastal Chinese city of Ningbo.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shivratan Agarwal is the founder and chairman of Bikaji Foods International, a maker of Indian snacks and sweets.
It was started as Shivdeep Products in 1986, combining his name and that of his son Deepak. He launched the Bikaji brand in 1993.
Bikaji Foods got listed in November 2022 at an 8% premium to its IPO price.
His grandfather Gangabishan Agarwal founded the famous Haldiram brand of Indian snacks.
abouts: The name Bikaji is derived from Bika Rao, the founder of Bikaner city in the state of Rajasthan.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: A dual U.K. and Canadian citizen, Terence (Terry) Matthews made his fortune with telecom firms Mitel and Newbridge Networks.
In 2018, he left his chairman role at Mitel, the company he co-founded with Michael Cowpland, after it was acquired for $2 billion.
In 1986, Matthews founded data networking business Newbridge Networks before selling it to Alcatel in 2000 for $7.1 billion.
He claims to have funded or founded more than 100 companies, many through his Ottawa-based investment firm Wesley Clover.
A resident of Canada, his U.K. property portfolio includes Celtic Manor Resort, which hosted the 2010 Ryder Cup and 2014 NATO Summit.
abouts: Matthews was knighted by Queen Elizabeth in 2001; the honor created a diplomatic incident in Canada, which does not allow its citizens to accept foreign titles.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Said Gutseriev's father, billionaire Mikhail Gutseriev, gave him stakes in retail and financial businesses of Safmar Group.
Said, who studied at the Harrow School, then Oxford and Plymouth, currently lives in London, where he runs Larnabel Ventures, the venture capital firm he founded.
He previously worked as an analyst in the London office of the commodities giant Glencore, which is a shareholder in oil company Russneft, founded by his father.
He served as CEO of Russian oil refinery ForteInvest, part of his father's Safmar Group, until stepping down in 2021.
In 2019, Said became one of the first investors in cryptocurrency exchange Currency.com based in Belarus.
He is under U.K. sanctions since June 2022.
abouts: Said Gutseriev holds U.K. citizenship as well as Russian citizenship.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Clark Hunt is chairman and CEO of the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs, which he owns with his three siblings.
Their father Lamar Hunt (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar is credited with naming the Super Bowl.
Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.
The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while brother Dan is president.
Lamar was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dan Hunt owns the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs with his three siblings. His brother Clark is chairman and CEO.
Their father Lamar Hunt (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar is credited with naming the Super Bowl.
Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.
The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while Dan is president.
Lamar was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lamar Hunt, Jr. owns the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs with his three siblings. His brother Clark is chairman and CEO.
Their father Lamar Hunt, Sr. (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar, Sr. is credited with naming the Super Bowl.
Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.
The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while brother Dan is president.
Lamar, Sr. was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sharron Hunt owns the NFL's Kansas City Chiefs with her three siblings. Her brother Clark is chairman and CEO.
Their father Lamar Hunt (d. 2006) founded the team and passed control to his kids in 2005. Lamar is credited with naming the Super Bowl.
Forbes estimates the Chiefs are now worth more than $4.7 billion (net of debt). Each Hunt Sibling owns an estimated 25% stake.
The Hunt siblings also own MLS team FC Dallas and a minority stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls. Clark is chairman and CEO of the family's soccer club, while brother Dan is president.
Lamar was one of 11 heirs of oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt (d. 1974) who appeared on the first ever Forbes 400 list of the richest Americans in 1982.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xiang Guangming chairs Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Weiming Environment Protection.
Weiming's main business is solid waste incineration disposal.
Xiang's wife, Wang Suqin, also holds shares in the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Laurie Tisch's late father Bob (d. 2005) started Loews Corporation with his brother Laurence (d. 2003) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Today, Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines, and hotels.
Laurie's mother Joan Tisch (d. 2017) was the largest individual Loews shareholder with a 6% stake. Laurie and her two siblings inherited her mother's stake.
In 1991, her father Bob bought a 50% stake in the New York Giants for $75 million.
Laurie's brother Steve Tisch is chairman and executive vice president of the NFL team, which FORBES values at $6.3 billion (net of debt).
abouts: An avid art collector, Laurie Tisch is a trustee at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York City.
In 2008, Tisch worked with then-New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg to launch NYC Green Carts, which provides fresh produce to "food deserts" throughout the city.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Steven Tisch is chairman and executive vice president of NFL's NY Giants. His late father Bob paid $75 million in 1991 for a 50% stake in the team.
Bob Tisch (d. 2005) cofounded Loews Corp. with his brother Laurence (d. 2003) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Today, Loews Corp., a publicly traded company, is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
Steven's mother Joan (d. 2017) was the largest individual shareholder of Loews with a 6% stake. His brother Jonathan is co-chairman.
Steven, Jonathan and sister Laurie Tisch, inherited their mother's fortune.
abouts: Steven is the only known person to have won both an Academy Award and a Super Bowl ring: he won an Oscar for producing Forrest Gump, and the Giants won two Super Bowls.
Steven has been a movie producer for decades, working on hit films including Risky Business, American History X, and The Pursuit of Happyness.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Fernando Espinosa Abdalá and his brother Leopoldo derive much of their fortune from the sale of their drug manufacturer Rimsa, which it sold to Tel Aviv-based Teva Pharmaceuticals for $2.3 billion.
Fernando was the operational president of the company before the sale in 2016.
Their father founded the business in 1970 as a pharmaceutical distributor before expanding into manufacturing.
Following the sale, Teva sued Fernando and Leopoldo claiming fraud and a breach of contract.
Most of the charges were dismissed; as for breach of contract, the parties eventually settled for less than $200 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Leopoldo Espinosa Abdalá and his brother Fernando gets the bulk of their wealth from the 2016 sale of their drug manufacturer Rimsa, which it sold to Tel Aviv-based Teva Pharmaceuticals for $2.3 billion.
Leopoldo was the executive president of the privately-held Mexican company before the sale.
Their father founded the business in 1970 as a pharmaceutical distributor before expanding into manufacturing.
At the time of the sale Risma was known for a slew of patented products, most notably its fixed-dose drug combinations.
Following the sale, Teva sued Leopoldo and Fernando claiming fraud and a breach of contract. 	The charges were mostly dismissed; the parties eventually settled for less than $200 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Naresh Jain is the former chairman of listed auto component companies, Endurance Group and Varroc Engineering, in which he holds stakes.
His twin sons, Anurang and Tarang, run Endurance and Varroc respectively.
Anurang Jain is a billionaire based on his holding in Endurance
Jain stepped down as chairman of both companies in 2020.
His wife Suman is the younger sister of late two-wheeler billionaire Rahul Bajaj.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Suman Munjal is the son of late Brijmohan Lall Munjal, founder of Hero Group, who died in 2015 at age 92.
He is a non-executive director on the board of two-wheeler behemoth Hero MotoCorp, which is run by his younger brother Pawan Munjal and is the family's most valuable asset.
Suman is the chairman of Rockman Industries, which supplies aluminium die castings to Hero MotoCorp.
He set up the auto components division off Rockman in 1995 and started manufacturing motorcycle chains

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Evgeny Shvidler, who became an American citizen in 1994, is the best friend and a partner of Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.
His core asset is stake in Russian steelmaker Evraz.
Former Executive chairman of Highland Gold Mining, Shvidler sold his 12% stake in this company in 2020.
Shvidler was born in Moscow, Russia. He got an MBA from Fordham University in 1992 and worked for Deloitte & Touche in New York.

Shvidler, a dual British-American citizen, was sanctioned by the U.K. in March 2022. His two jets were detained by British authorities. He filed the claim in 2023 in London to challenge the sanctions.
abouts: His 370-foot yacht, Le Grand Bleu, was a gift from Abramovich.
Shvidler was the primary funder for the rebuilding of a Jewish school in England that is now called Beit Shvidler Primary School.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: San Francisco Bay Area real estate broker George Marcus has been in the business for over 40 years.
Most of his fortune lies in a 35% stake in Marcus & Millichap, the publicly-traded real estate brokerage he founded in 1971.
Marcus & Millichap specializes in commercial real estate in the U.S. and Canada, closing nearly 9,000 transactions valued at $42.3 billion in 2016.
Marcus also controls a 3% stake in Essex Property Trust, a REIT he founded that owns more than 60,000 apartments along the West Coast.
Marcus also has a stake in several private real-estate and investment companies, including SummerHill Housing Group and Pacific Urban Residential.
abouts: He graduated with a B.A. in economics from San Francisco State University and served on the Board of Regents of the University of California from 2000 to 2012.
Marcus was born on a Greek island, northeast of Athens, and immigrated to the United States when he was four with his poor parents.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gretel Packer is the elder sister of fellow billionaire James Packer.
She became a billionaire after James split their family estate 10 years after the 2005 death of their father, media mogul Kerry Packer.
Famously low-profile, she was the driving force behind the establishment of the $160 million National Philanthropic Fund in 2014.
The fund is supported by the Packer Family Foundation, which she chairs.
She is also an arts patron, who sits on the boards of the Art Gallery of New South Wales and the Sydney Theatre Company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ben Ashkenazy bought his first building at age 17, after he went to a Bronx  shopping center to check out a site to open a fast food restaurant.
Then a recent high school grad, Ashkenazy realized the lease offered was below market value and decided to find a lender and buy the property instead.
Since then he's built a portfolio of stakes in more than 100 buildings via real estate firm Ashkenazy Acquisitions, which he founded and runs as CEO.
The company owns historical landmarks like Washington D.C.'s Union Station and Boston's Faneuil Hall.
Ashkenazy, who primarily invests in retail properties, is also a minority owner in New York's famed Plaza Hotel.
abouts: In between his real estate ventures, Ashkenazy took night classes at Adelphi University but ended up six credits shy of graduating.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Tian Ming chairs Hefei Meiya Optoelectronic Technology, a supplier of detection equipment.
Tian made his fortune initially from optical sorters for grains and tea leaves, profiting from China's agricultural boom.
Hefei Meiya went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Tibet Cheezheng Tibetan Medicine Co Ltd
Tibet Cheezheng Tibetan Medicine Co Ltd

bios: Lei Jufang chairs Tibet Cheezheng Tibetan Medicine,  best known for its pain-relief patches and cream.
Lei discovered the business that made her a billionaire on a leisure trip to Tibet seeking peace of mind.
Lei holds an undergraduate degree from Xian Jiaotong University in vacuum physics.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Farkhad Akhmedov got his start selling Russian sables at the London commodity exchange.
In 1987 he founded Tansley Trading, which supplied equipment to Russian gas producers.
Six years later, he became a minority shareholder in Nortgas, an oil and gas company in Siberia.
In 1998, he bought out the 44% stake of another investor, Bechtel Energy, and became chairman of Nortgas.
He sold that stake in 2012 for $1.4 billion.
In 2016, a U.K. High Court judge ordered Akhmedov to pay his ex-wife 454 million British pounds, but he refused. In 2021 Tatiana accepted cash and art and the divorce dispute was settled.
He is under EU and U.K. sanctions since April 2022. In June 2022 his yacht Luna, valued at about $500 million, was frozen in Germany; In September 2023 the EU removed its sanctions against Akhmedov.
abouts: Akhmedov invested $55 million in a pomegranate juice factory in his native Azerbaijan, where his father worked during the Soviet era.
Akhmedov's helicopter was seized and sold for around $5.7 million on behalf of his ex-wife in December 2018 after the London court granted his assets be frozen.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liang Yunchao chairs Guandong By-health, one of China's largest producers of vitamins and health supplements.
Every few years he invites young leaders to join a "wildlife training" boot camp to test their stamina, he told Forbes Asia in an interview.
His favorite boot camp spots include Teklimakan Qumluqi in Xinjiang, the world's second largest desert, and Antarctica.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Peter Kelly founded IT infrastructure provider Softcat in 1993, spending a reported $44,400 and working out of his garden shed.
Kelly, a college dropout, started out in sales at Xerox Corp.
He took Softcat public in 2015 on the London Stock Exchange and owns just over 30% of the company.
Kelly is known to offer his staff free breakfast and a weekly shirt-ironing service.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Taylor Swift became a billionaire in October 2023, thanks to the earnings from her Eras Tour and the value of her music catalog.
Swift is the first musician to make the billionaire ranking primarily based on her songs and performances.
Her fortune includes nearly $800 million amassed from royalties and touring, plus a music catalog worth an estimated $600 million and some $110 million in real estate.
In 2021, Swift began releasing re-records of her first six albums so she could regain the ownership rights to them.
Demand for tickets to the U.S. leg of her Eras Tour overwhelmed Ticketmaster, prompting members of Congress to question the company's hold on concert sales.
abouts: Swift has won 14 Grammys.
After releasing her album "Midnights" in 2022, Swift became the first artist in history to claim the top ten spots on the Billboard Hot 100 song list.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Diona Teh Li Shian is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades.
Her father founded the bank in 1966. Teh died in December 2022 at age 92.
Her father had a substantial minority stake in both Public Bank and insurance firm LPI Capital.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lilian Teh Li Ming is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
In addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
Teh had a substantial minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lillian Teh Li Hua is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired the Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades.
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
In addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
Teh had a significant minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: William Teh Lee Pang is the son of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who founded Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank and chaired it for several decades.
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
n addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
The late Teh owned a substantial minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Renu Munjal is the daughter-in-law of late Brijmohan Lall Munjal, founder of India's Hero Group, who died in 2015 at age 92. Her late husband Raman Kant Munjal, was one of three sons of the patriarch.
The group's flagship company is Hero MotoCorp, one of the largest producers of two-wheelers in the world.
She is the managing director of Hero Fincop, the financial services unit of the group. Her son Abhimanyu is joint managing director and CEO.
Renu chairs the Raman Kant Munjal Foundation, which supports education, skill development and community development.
She's also a founding member of Gurgaon-based BML Munjal University which offers undergrad courses as well as MBA programs.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Larry Culp is chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace (formerly known as General Electric).

He took over GE in 2018 and has broken up the bloated conglomerate into three separate public companies after spinning off its healthcare business as GE HealthCare in 2023 and its energy business as GE Vernova in 2024.
Culp also serves as chairman of GE Healthcare.
Culp started his career at Danaher, the industrial conglomerate founded by billionaire brothers Mitchell and Steven Rales.
He joined Danaher in 1990 and served as president and CEO from 2001 to 2015.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Deepinder Goyal cofounded food delivery service Zomato in 2008. He still runs the company as CEO.
Zomato's IPO in 2021 was oversubscribed 35 times and it listed at a valuation of $12 billion.
In 2022, Zomato acquired quick commerce platform Blinkit. It competes with rival Swiggy's Instamart.
Zomato also runs a B2B platform called HyperPure, which sells spices, fruits, vegetables and dairy products to hotels, restaurants and caterers.
abouts: Goyal has a math and computing degree from the premier Indian Institute of Technology in Delhi.
Goyal was working with Bain & Company as a management consultant before he struck out on his own.
Four independent directors on Zomato's seven-member board are women.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Leonid Simanovsky holds just under 2% of the gas company Novatek.
He met fellow billionaire Leonid Mikhelson, his partner in Novatek, in the late 1980s, when he worked at Mikhelson's construction company.
Since 2003 Simanovsky has been a State Duma deputy and a deputy chairman of the Duma's budget and tax committee.
Simanovsky was among the 336 members of Russia's parliament sanctioned by the EU on February 23.
abouts: Simanovsky began his career as a fitter in a factory producing space rocket technology.
Simanovsky worked for Mikhail Khodorkovsky's Yukos many years ago.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Bloor is one of the largest builders in the UK through his Bloor Homes and also owns Triumph Motorcycles, the iconic bike manufacturer.
He reportedly left school at age 15 and began an apprenticeship as a plasterer, then built his first house before turning 20.
Now the privately-held Bloor Homes puts up more than 3,500 homes every year.
In 1983 he bought the manufacturing rights for Triumph motorcycles.
He and son Nick have revamped the brand, which was made famous by riders like Marlon Brando, James Dean and Steve McQueen.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stephen Jarislowsky made the bulk of his fortune at the helm of Jarislowsky Fraser, the investment management firm he founded in 1955.
He stepped down as CEO in 2012 but remains chairman emeritus of the company and president of the Jarislowsky Foundation.
Canadian bank Scotiabank bought Jarislowsky Fraser for about $750 million in stock and cash in April 2018.
He owns a sizable art collection that is largely comprised of Canadian art, but also includes Chinese jade and French impressionism.
abouts: Jarislowsky owns the 2,000-acre Marina Island in the Strait of Georgia near Vancouver.
A longtime supporter of business ethics and shareholder rights, Jarislowsky cofounded the Canadian Coalition for Good Governance in 2002 and is an honorary director.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ibrahim Erdemoglu and his brother, Ali, together own over 75% of a top producer of materials used in carpet, SASA Polyester.
They initially acquired 51% of SASA in 2015 for $102 million, then added to their stake in the publicly traded company and watched it soar in value.
The brothers' Erdemoglu Holding also includes the two privately held companies, Merinos Carpet and Dinarsu Carpet.
In 1970, their father, Mehmet Erdemoglu, along with family members, started Merinos with two rug-weaving looms.
Today, Erdemoglu Holding is one of the world's largest carpet manufacturers, with production facilities in eight locations in Turkey and Russia.
abouts: SASA has a $935 million licensing and technical service agreement with Invista, a subsidiary of Koch Industries that makes chemicals, polymers, fabrics and fibers.
While studying physics at university, Ibrahim Erdemoglu carried carpets on his back and sold them directly to customers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rubens Ometto Silveira Mello became the world's first ethanol billionaire in 2007. Cosan, his sugar giant, is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company's origins date to 1936, when Ometto's grandparents established a sugarcane mill in Sao Paulo.
After several takeovers, Cosan became one of the world's largest growers and processors of sugarcane and one of the largest producers of ethanol.
Besides his Cosan shares, Ometto also holds a portfolio of real estate investments.
abouts: His combativeness earned him the moniker "the tractor," in part because of the long legal fights in order to gain control of Cosan.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Oran Holtzman and his sister Shiran Holtzman-Erel founded Oddity Tech in 2018, a data-driven company that develops and sells beauty products online.
Holtzman is the chairman and CEO of the more than half-billion-dollar (2024 revenue) company; Shiran is the Chief Product Officer.
Oddity brands virtually match consumers to a makeup or skincare product using AI and software technology.
The company's two brands, Il Makiage and SpoiledChild, sell directly to Oddity's more than 50 million customers solely online.
Oddity debuted on the Nasdaq in 2023 at a $2.7 billion market cap.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Carlos Sanchez owns and runs privately-held generic drug firm EMS S.A., which was founded by his late father.
EMS S.A. sells prescription, generic, branded generic and over-the-counter products.
In recent years, the company has benefited from adding drugs including generic versions of Viagra and Lipitor to its sales arsenal.
EMS was founded by Sanchez' father, Emiliano, in 1950 as a small pharmacy. Sanchez inherited EMS at age 26 when his father died.
Sanchez owns 75% of EMS; the rest is owned by the sons of his sister, who passed away in 2009.
abouts: Sanchez reportedly bid $85 million for Edvard Munch painting The Scream at a Sotheby's auction but was outbid by billionaire Leon Black at $119.9 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Heikki Herlin, born 1990, is an heir to the Kone fortune in Finland.
He is the great-great-grandson of Harald Herlin, who invested in Kone Elevators in 1924.
Heikki Herlin inherited shares in several Scandinavian companies from his father Niklas, who died in 2016.
His most valuable holdings are stakes in Kone and Cargotec, a producer of machinery for heavy duty cargo ships.
His two uncles and aunt, Ilkka, Antti and Iona Herlin, are all billionaires.
abouts: Like his father, Herlin is a journalist and writer. In 2020, he published a memoir about his father's life.
He is the second largest shareholder of Finnish publishing company Alma Media.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Johan Johannson and his family own nearly 75% of NorgesGruppen, the Norwegian grocery store chain he inherited from his father and uncle.
His father still oversees the company as chairman of the board; Jahon has no role in running the business.
The company has been family run since it was founded in 1866.
Norgesgruppen has more than 1,850 grocery stores and 650 convenience stores and nearly 40% market share in Norway.
abouts: In 2012 the company vowed to reduce sugar sales by 10% by promoting more healthy alternatives. Between 2012 and 2017, sales of fruits and vegetables were up 28%.
Johan Johannson is one of four competing Norwegian grocery billionaires; the others are Odd Reitan, Stein Erik Hagen and his daughter Caroline Hagen Kjos.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lebanon-born Sasson Dayan founded Brazil's Banco Daycoval in 1968 with his brother Ibrahim Dayan.
Daycoval has become one of Brazil's biggest lenders to small and mid-sized businesses, and also provides personal banking services.
Dayan transferred almost all his shares in Daycoval to his three sons in 2015, whose stakes are included in the family fortune.
Dayan remains president of the bank's board, while daily operations are headed by his sons and nephew.
abouts: Dayan got his start working at a banking firm in Lebanon founded by his father.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: James Tisch's father Laurence (d. 2003) started Loews Corporation with his brother Bob (d. 2005) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
James is CEO of Loews. His brother Andrew and cousin Jonathan are co-chairmen.
Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
James' mother Wilma is also a billionaire, as are his cousins Laurie and Steven.
The Tisch family donated funds to support NYU's Tisch School of the Arts and its Tisch Hospital at Langone Medical Center.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bharat Desai founded IT consulting and outsourcing company Syntel with his wife Neerja Sethi from their apartment in Troy, Michigan in 1980.
In 2018 French IT firm Atos SE acquired Syntel for $3.4 billion in cash.
Atos sued Desai, accusing him of hiding liabilities ahead of the merger; the case was dismissed in 2023.
In its first year, Syntel generated just $30,000 in sales; before it was acquired, annual revenue grew to more than $900 million.
Desai, who was Syntel's chairman, was born in Kenya, raised in India and came to the U.S. in 1976 as a programmer for Tata.
abouts: Desai and Sethi started the company with just $2,000.
The couple met in the U.S. while working for pioneering IT firm, Tata Consultancy Services, the company they went on to emulate.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Li Liangbin chairs Jiangxi Ganfeng Lithium, a manufacturer of lithium battery products that are used in electric vehicles, energy storage, chemicals and pharmaceuticals.
Ganfeng is headquartered in China's Jiangxi Province.
In 2000, Li bought the factory which became the predecessor business of Ganfeng.
Li received a Bauhinia Cup Technology Innovation Award from Hong Kong Polytechnic University in 2013.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Artur Grynbaum is the brother-in-law of Miguel Krigsner, who founded Brazil's second-largest cosmetics company Grupo Boticario.
Grynbaum joined as a financial assistant and worked his way up to president of the group by 2008. He owns about 20% of the company.
Grupo Boticario operates in more than 50 countries; Krigsner individually owns approximately 80% of the business.
Today, Krigsner and Grynbaum serve as president and vice president, respectively, of the Grupo Boticario advisory board.
In 1990 Krigsner created the Boticario Group Foundation dedicated to environmental protection, which receives about 1% of Grupo Boticario's net income annually.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Julia Oetker is an heir to the fortune of the Oetker Group, a now-divided German conglomerate with diverse holdings that included a popular range of food products.
In September of 2024, she gave up her ownership stake in Geschwister Oetker, a German holding company with brands spanning wine and spirits, chemicals and luxury hotels.
Geschwister Oetker was formed in 2021 after the eight Oetker siblings agreed to divide their $8 billion (sales) conglomerate into two separate groups.
The original business, Dr. August Oetker, began in 1891 when her great-grandfather started selling non-perishable baking powder.
Julia's brothers, Alfred and Carl Ferdinand, are co-CEOs and owners of Geschwister Oetker.
abouts: When her father, Rudolf August, passed away in 2007, ownership of Dr. August Oetker was divided between his eight children from three marriages.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Weng is the majority shareholder of Shenzhen New Industries Biomedical Engineering, a supplier of clinical instruments.
Weng was the first person to be appointed as representative of China's securities watchdog in the city of Shenzhen back in 1992.
The company was founded in 1995 and is based in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: David Fattal founded Fattal Hotels, Israel's largest hotel organization.
Fattal got his start as a waiter and bellboy and rose through management ranks before starting Fattal Hotels in 1998 at age 41.
He took the chain's parent company, Fattal Holdings 1998, public on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in 2018.
The company owns 47 hotels in Israel with 9,000 rooms, and manages 255 hotels with a total of more than 50,000 rooms across Israel, Europe and the Mediterranean region.
Fattal owns about 51% of Fattal Holdings and nearly 9% of Mediterranean Towers, which is also listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: David C. Paul is the founder and executive chairman of spine implant manufacturer Globus Medical.
A mechanical engineer by training, Paul moved to the U.S. from India to get his master's degree at Temple University.
Paul worked as an engineer for medical device giant Synthes before leaving in 2003 to start Globus.
Paul took Globus public in 2012.
In 2017 Paul stepped down as CEO due to a "health condition," according to a company press release.
abouts: Globus makes the Excelsius GPS, one of the only spinal surgery robots on the market today.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Onkar Kanwar is chairman of Apollo Tyres which makes tires for cars, trucks, farm vehicles and two-wheelers.
It sells under the Apollo and Vredestein brands in India, Europe and Asia.
He took control of the company in 2002 after a public battle with his father, the late Raunaq Singh, who started the company in 1976.
Neeraj Kanwar, the younger of his two sons, is vice-chairman and managing director.
abouts: The company's Vredestein brand supplies tires for luxury cars.
He enjoys learning about modern management practices and applying them to his business

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: The eldest of five siblings, Girdhari Jaisinghani owns a minority stake in listed Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables.
The company was started in 1986 by his younger brother Inder as a trading firm.
Today, Polycab gets the bulk of its revenues from wires and cables.
It supplies everything from power cables to solar cables to optical fiber cables. Its customers are largely in the oil and gas, power and renewable energy industries.
In the past decade, Polycab has expanded into making products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear.
abouts: He has no executive role in the company.
Polycab India went public in 2019.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alberto Cortina derives his wealth largely from shares in construction company ACS, led by billionaire Florentino Pérez.
He and his billionaire cousin Alberto Cortina ran their wives' Construcciones y Contratas firm from the early 1970s until 1989, when both marriages fell apart.
Alcocer and Cortina then moved into banking, running Banco Zaragozano. They sold their combined 40% stake to Barclays in 2004
The cousins were married to sisters Esther and Alicia Koplowitz, who were previously significant shareholders of the FCC construction group.
abouts: Alcocer owns several ranches in Cadiz and Toledo, Spain, along with houses in Paris and Madrid.
The Panama Papers revealed that Alcocer and his cousin Cortina had offshore accounts in the Central American tax haven country.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yeh Kuo-I is the founder and group president of Inventec, which started as a maker of electronic notebooks in 1975.
Inventec has since expanded into other consumer electronic products such as computers and servers, and today employs more than 30,000 people.
Apart from Inventec, Yeh also has stakes in Taiwan-based Win Semiconductors.
His wealth includes stakes held by his wife, his two sons and his two daughters-in-law. His younger son Sam is Inventec's chairman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Anas Sefrioui is the founder and CEO of listed homebuilder Groupe Addoha, which has prospered thanks to government contracts.
He made his fortune developing low-cost housing in Morocco.
His daughter Kenza is the company's deputy chairman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Robert Mouawad inherited the family's eponymous high-end jewelry business that his grandfather founded in Beirut in 1890.
He turned over management of the business to his sons Fred, Alain and Pascal in 2010.
Mouawad boasts one of the world's most dazzling gem collections, including Dynasty, a 51.12 carat Russian diamond estimated at nearly $10 million.
Robert Mouawad also owns real estate, including hotels in Beirut. He developed luxury residences on Reef Island, a man-made island in Bahrain.
abouts: Mouawad has a private museum in a 110 year-old Beirut palace displaying his collection of Roman and Phoenician antiquities.
In 2024, Mouawad announced a partnership with Dubai-based developer Dar Global to build a luxury residential development in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Luis von Ahn is the cofounder and CEO of popular language-learning app Duolingo.
More than 100 million people take language, math and music lessons on Duolingo each month.
Von Ahn grew up in Guatemala City with his single mom and grandmother. He immigrated to the U.S. in 1996 to attend Duke, then got a computer science Ph.D. at Carnegie Mellon in 2005.
While at Carnegie Mellon, he cofounded the CAPTCHA verification system that distinguishes humans from robots online. He sold reCAPTCHA to Google for an undisclosed sum in 2009.
Two years later, he started Duolingo, along with cofounder Hacker, a Swiss computer scientist he tapped as the company's CTO.
He and Hacker took Duolingo public in 2021. It did nearly $750 million in revenue in 2024.
abouts: Von Ahn has dual Guatemalan and U.S. citizenship.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Fang Hongbo is the chairman of China's Midea, one of the world's largest makers of home appliances.
Fang was born in a 10-family village in impoverished Anhui Province in central China.
He was hired by Midea in 1992 to edit the company newsletter.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Min-Liang Tan gave up a law career in Singapore to start gaming devices company Razer in 2005.

Its early backers include IDG-Accel, Temasek Holdings, Intel and Li Ka-shing's Horizon Ventures. The company has acquired a huge global following and sold millions of gaming laptops, mice, fitness bands and tablets.
Tan listed the firm in Hong Kong in 2017, raising $529 million.
Tan expanded Razer in Asia with the acquisition of Malaysian virtual currency firm MOL Global, and tie-ups with SingTel, Lazada and China's JD.com.
In 2022, Tan and Lim Kaling, who is a founding investor and director at Razer, took the company private in a deal that valued it at $3.2 billion.
abouts: Diehard Razer fans sport tattoos of the brand's logo.
Razer acquired THX, the audio company founded by Star Wars director George Lucas, in 2016 and Android smartphone maker Nextbit in 2017.
Tan is a key investor in Lucence, a Singapore- and Palo Alto-headquartered biotech company that provides cancer blood tests, founded by his older Min-Han in 2016.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhang Liguo is the founder and chairman of Harbin Fuerjia Technology, a maker of skincare products best known for its beauty masks.
He took Fuerjia public in Shenzhen in August 2023, raising $306 million.
Zhang worked as a pharmacist in a local hospital before striking out on his own.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Oleg Boyko's private equity firm Finstar Financial currently manages and consults portfolio companies operating in 30+ countries.
After Russia invaded Ukraine, his mother who held all of his shares in fintech 4Finance gave 9.9% each to Ukrainian relatives and a nonprofit in Switzerland.
She sold the rest of the family's 4Finance stake to four new, non-Russian minority shareholders.
Boyko opened Moscow's first stores with credit card readers in the 1990s.
In 2002 Boyko invested in a Moscow chain of gambling venues and founded Ritzio Entertainment Group, which invested in casinos and gambling.
When gambling was banned, Boyko sold his Russian gambling assets and moved into gambling in the European Union.
abouts: Boyko, who was injured in an accident in 1996 and often appears in a scooter-style wheelchair, is the main private sponsor of Russian Paralympics team.
He invests in movie-making. His projects include Roberto Rodriguez's Sin City II and Scarlett Johansson's Summer Crossing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Olivia Holding is one of four sisters of Frank Holding, Chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a commercial banking chain, since 2008.
Her grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to her father, Lewis Holding.
Today Olivia Holding, her three sisters, and her brother Frank collectively own about 20% of the bank.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Keiko Erikawa cofounded videogame developer Koei in 1978 with her husband Yoichi Erikawa.
The company, now called Koei Tecmo Holdings, trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The founders are stepping away from executive roles. Starting April, Yoichi, who is now CEO, will become chairman; and Keiko, who is now chairman, will become chairman emeritus.
The company is known for its Samurai Warrior games.
In 2021, Keiko Erikawa was appointed as an independent director of SoftBank Group. She's the only woman to sit on the company's board.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Eduard Schleicher is a fifth-generation member of the Schwenk family fortune, best known for its cement business.
Founded in 1847 as a cement supplier, today the business includes three other main divisions: concrete, sand and gravel and pumps.
Schleicher manages the growth of the company and focuses on international expansion.
Today the group has subsidiaries in Austria, Hungary and Czech Republic, among other countries, and employs 4,500 people.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ursula Hutter-Schleicher derives her fortune from Schwenk cement, one of Germany's oldest family-owned businesses founded in 1847.
Today the company, which employs 4,500 people, supplies the construction industry with cement, concrete, sand and gravel.
Her brother Eduard Schleicher manages the company and is also a billionaire.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yoichi Erikawa cofounded videogame developer Koei more than four decades ago with his wife Keiko Erikawa.
The company, now called Koei Tecmo Holdings, trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The founders are stepping away from executive roles. Starting April, Yoichi, who is now CEO, will become chairman; and Keiko, who is now chairman, will become chairman emeritus.
The company is known for its Samurai Warrior games.
Hisashi Koinuma, currently executive vice president, is set to become president and CEO in June.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Peter Guber, a longtime movie executive, owns stakes in several pro sports teams, most notably the NBA's Golden State Warriors.
Guber was part of a group led by Joe Lacob in 2010 that bought the Warriors for $450 million; Forbes now values the team at $8.8 billion.
Guber owns an estimated 15% of the Warriors and is co-executive chairman alongside Lacob.
He also owns an estimated 3% of the LA Dodgers baseball team and is executive chair and co-owner of the Major League Soccer team Los Angeles FC.
At Columbia Pictures and Polygram Entertainment, Guber oversaw production of hit movies including Rain Man, The Color Purple, Batman and more.
abouts: Guber is also an author whose book Shootout: Surviving Fame and (Mis)Fortune In Hollywood became a TV series on AMC.
Guber was recruited by Columbia Pictures while pursuing an MBA at New York University in the late 1960s.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Nikolay Fartushnyak, along with his older brother Vladimir and Alexander Mikhalskiy, cofounded Russia's largest sports and fashion retailer Sportmaster.
The Fartushnyak brothers and Mikhalskiy are also cofounders of Ostin, a Russian fast-fashion retailer.
In 2014 Fartushnyak and Igor Khudokormov, known as the "Russian sugar king," bought Swedish company Agrokultura, which owns about 200,000 hectares of agricultural land in Russia.
Fartushnyak and his partners started out with distribution business in the early 1990s and supplied French consumer goods to their home market.
His Sportmaster also has its own brands, such as Demix, which makes sports goods, apparel and shoes.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wu Zhigang is the founder of Shanghai-listed bakery chain Shenyang Toly Bread.
Wu was a teacher at an industrial school before founding the chain with his son Wu Xuequn in 1995; Xuequn is the company's general manager.
Wu Zhigang's wife, Sheng Yali, and sons Wu Xuedong, Wu Xuequn and Wu Xueliang hold shares in Toly.
Xuedong, Xuequn and Xueliang are board members.
Wu Zhigang retired as chairman in 2019 and was succeeded by Wu Xueliang.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: William Fisher is one of the heirs to the Gap retail fortune. He sits on Gap's board alongside his brother Robert.
Known as "Bill," he was founder and president of the International Division for Gap Inc. and expanded the company into Canada, Japan and Europe.
He is CEO of Manzanita Capital, a London-based private equity firm he founded in 2001.
Bill's parents Doris and Don (d. 2009) founded retailer Gap in San Francisco in 1969.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Arvind Lal is executive chairman of diagnostics chain, Dr Lal PathLabs, in which he owns a majority stake.
The company is located in Gurgaon, a thriving township close to Delhi, and has clinical labs and collection centres across India.
The company offers a range of pathology, radiology and cardiology tests.
The business was founded  by his father S.K. Lal, also a doctor, in 1949 in Delhi. Arvind Lal joined the business after studying medicine, at age 28.
His wife, Vandana Lal, who is a pathologist, is the technical director and heads clinical research services and the test development department.
abouts: Lal is a published author whose book, 'Corporate Yogi: My Journey as a Spiritual Seeker and an Accidental Entrepreneur' was published in 2018.
Lal has an honorary brigadier's rank in the Armed Forces Medical Services.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Doris Fisher cofounded clothing retailer Gap in 1969 with her husband, Don (d. 2009), after the couple struggled to find jeans that fit him.
The couple raised $63,000 to open their first store, which sold jeans and music, in San Francisco.
Doris Fisher served as the company's merchandiser from the day it opened until 2003 and sat on Gap's board until 2009.
The 1953 Stanford economics graduate cofounded the KIPP Foundation, which supports public charter schools, donating $15 million.
abouts: Gap is short for "generation gap." The Fishers agreed on the name after Doris nixed her husband's original idea, "Pants and Discs."
The Fishers amassed a $1 billion art collection, including works by Andy Warhol and Gerhard Richter, now on display in San Francisco's Museum of Modern Art.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joe Lau cofounded Alchemy, whose software powers thousands of blockchain-based Web3 companies.
Alchemy, founded in 2020, was valued by private investors at $10.2 billion in February; Lau owns an estimated 26% stake.
Forbes estimates that Alchemy is now worth around $6 billion as the valuations of private tech companies have generally fallen from their peaks in early 2022.
In December 2021, the company announced the launch of Alchemy Ventures, which invests in current clients with the goal of bootstrapping the industry.
Lau and cofounder Nikil Viswanathan, both Stanford grads, found initial success with meetup app Down to Lunch, briefly topping the Apple Store charts.
abouts: Alchemy's team consists of engineers from Google, Facebook, Microsoft, LinkedIn and Pinterest, some of them college friends of Viswanathan and Lau.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Nikil Viswanathan cofounded Alchemy, whose software powers thousands of blockchain-based Web3 companies.
Alchemy, founded in 2020, was valued by private investors at $10.2 billion in February 2022; Viswanathan owns an estimated 26% stake.
Forbes estimates that Alchemy is now worth around $6 billion as the valuations of private tech companies have generally fallen from their peaks in early 2022.
In December 2021, the company announced the launch of Alchemy Ventures, which invests in current clients with the goal of bootstrapping the industry.
Viswanathan and cofounder Joe Lau, both Stanford grads, found initial success with meetup app Down to Lunch, briefly topping the Apple Store charts.
abouts: Alchemy's team consists of engineers from Google, Facebook, Microsoft, LinkedIn and Pinterest, some of them college friends of Viswanathan and Lau.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lin Dingqiang is the chairman and founder of real estate developer Radiance Group.
Founded in Fujian Province in 1996, Radiance is now headquartered in Beijing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Miguel Tomás Arrufat Pujol founded Spanish online education group Proeduca Altus, which provides accredited university courses online across Spain, Latin America, and the U.S.
Arrufat Pujol, who has led Proeduca Altus since its creation in 2007, owns more than 75% of the company, which went public in 2019.
Arrufat Pujol will sell around a third of his stake in Proeduca Altus for more than $300 million as part of a take private deal that is expected to close in the second quarter of 2025.
Arrufat Pujol was previously the CEO of a Spanish publishing house that focused on educational textbooks before founding Proeduca Altus.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yi Dasheng chairs Hunan Fortune Group, whose business interests include property development, auto-related services and trade.
Yi worked in a government office in the southern Chinese city of Yueyang before taking the plunge as an entrepreneur.
He made his early fortune in auto repair.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liesel Pritzker Simmons and her brother Matthew Pritzker sued their family for a chunk of its Hyatt Hotels fortune and received around $500 million apiece in 2005.
Their uncle Jay Pritzker (d. 1999) founded the hotel chain and their uncle Donald Pritzker (d. 1972) managed and developed it.
Their father Robert Pritzker (d. 2011) ran the family's industrial conglomerate Marmon Group, which was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in a series of transactions beginning in 2008.
Three of Matthew and Liesel's step-siblings, seven cousins and their father's cousin Nick Pritzker are also billionaires.
Liesel cofounded and runs impact investing firm Blue Haven Initiative with her husband Ian Simmons.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ronald Clarke is the CEO and chairman of Corpay, a $3.9 billion (sales) digital payments company.
The Atlanta-based company offers businesses credit cards geared to travel expenses like gas, tolls and lodging.
Clarke joined the company in 2000. Ten years later, he took it public on the New York Stock Exchange under its previous name, FleetCor.
Corpay has some 800,000 customers and operates in more than 100 countries worldwide.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bernard Lewis founded UK-based clothing retailer River Island Fashion in 1948; it now sells online and has stores in several European countries.
The business had revenues in 2022 of over $900 million.
His nephew Ben Lewis, who started as a store manager in 1990, served as CEO from 2010 to 2019 and is currently a board director of River Island.
Lewis and his family also own a hotel in Palm Beach, Florida and are investors in property development and private equity.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mike Speiser is a managing partner at venture capital firm Sutter Hill Ventures, which he joined in 2008.
Speiser was an initial investor in software firm Snowflake and served as its founding CEO from 2012 to 2014.
He became a billionaire after the company went public in September 2020 in what was the largest ever software IPO at the time.
He owns less than 1% of Snowflake's stock.
His other investments include startups Augment Computing, Reve AI, Sigma Computing, Sila Nano and Observe, Inc.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Media baron Krit Ratanarak controls Bangkok Broadcasting & TV, which operates Thailand's market leader, Channel 7.
He also owns a minority stake in Bank of Ayudhya, the country's fifth-largest bank in terms of loans and deposits.
In 2020, Bank of Ayudhya acquired a 50% stake in the Philippines-based SB Finance, a lender to small businesses.
Other assets include a stake in Siam City Cement, which his late father Chuan founded in 1969.
His U.K.-educated son and only child, Chachchon, oversees the Tonson Group and Tonson Property, the family's investment and property arms.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Severin Hacker is the cofounder and chief technology officer of popular language-learning app Duolingo.
More than 100 million people take language, math and music lessons on Duolingo each month.
Hacker, who grew up in Switzerland, started the company in 2011 with Luis von Ahn, who was his computer science Ph.D. thesis advisor.
He and von Ahn took Duolingo public in 2021. It did nearly $750 million in revenue in 2024.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alex Beard retired as head of worldwide oil operations at commodities trader and mining giant Glencore in 2019.
Beard, who had worked at Glencore since 1995, is based in London and was the highest-ranking Glencore executive in the UK.
Before he left, Beard owned a 2.5% stake in the firm, which has assets in oil, gas, agriculture and mining globally.
Prior to joining Glencore, Beard spent five years as an oil trader at BP.
His new investment fund, Adaptogen Capital, is focused on renewable energy opportunities.
abouts: Beard serves on the board of trustees of Shakespeare's Globe, which operates the iconic Globe Theatre in London.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Although Ahmet Calik built his fortune on denim, selling to Diesel, Levi's, Gap and other Western brands, textiles are now ancillary.
With a footprint stretching from Turkey and the Middle East to Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Calik is active in construction, banking, telecom and mining.
Calik Holding has a partnership with Mitsubishi Corp. dating back to 1990s, when the companies began collaborating on plant construction in Central Asia.
In 2015, Mitsubishi acquired 4.5% of Calik Energy, which serves five cities in Turkey and has projects in such places as Turkmenistan, Libya, Georgia and Yemen.
Besides providing services to energy plants, the company has electricity and gas distribution businesses and a portfolio of power generation assets.
abouts: In terms of contract value, Calik Holding's pipeline of construction and energy projects amounts to around $7 billion.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: A former advertising executive, Yan Zhi chairs Hong Kong-listed Zall Smart Commerce Group, previously called Zall Group.
The firm started with shopping mall development and then got into e-commerce as well as wholesale trading, logistics and warehousing.
Yan holds an EMBA from the Cheung Kong Graduate School.
Yan holds 30% of Z-Bank, a Wuhan-based bank that specializes in lending to small businesses involved in supply chain transactions.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yu Lili is the vice chair of electronic products maker Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics.
Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016.
Yu's husband Zeng Wanhui chairs Jingjia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cai Wensheng is the founder and chairman of Meitu, a Chinese photo-touch-up app created to improve selfies.
Meitu also sells smartphones with large pixel cameras.
Cai is an angel investor in Chinese startups.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dmitry Kamenshchik owns Moscow's Domodedovo Airport, one of the largest in Eastern Europe, serving an estimated 21 million passengers in 2022.
He got into the business in 1992, when the then-philosophy student chartered a plane to fly goods from China to Moscow.
abouts: Kamenshchik got control of Domodedovo airport when he was 30.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rolly van Rappard is a cofounder and non-executive chair of the board of Luxembourg-based private equity firm CVC Capital Partners.
The firm went public on the Amsterdam stock exchange in April 2024 and van Rappard owns a 6.7% stake.
CVC was established in 1981 as the European operations of Citicorp Venture Capital, the VC arm of Citigroup.
In 1993, van Rappard and seven cofounders acquired the business and spun it out as CVC. They raised their first fund in 1996 and shifted their focus to private equity.
CVC's investments include Petco, Swiss watchmaker Breitling and Spanish soccer league La Liga.
abouts: Van Rappard has a family office in Luxembourg that invests in public and private firms in Europe.
Van Rappard co-owns a yacht, the 184-foot Blue II, with fellow CVC cofounder Steve Koltes.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Anna Maria Braun is CEO of medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
A sixth-generation family member, she owns 10% of the company and also serves as president of its Asian/Pacific operations.
Her father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
abouts: Anna Maria is a member of the board of Dr. August Oetker KG, a $9 billion (sales) conglomerate with interests in food, beverages, financial services and hotels.
Her billionaire brother Otto Philipp Braun was responsible for the company's Iberian Peninsula and Latin American regions before stepping down in February 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Johanna Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
Her father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
A sixth-generation family member, Johanna is the youngest daughter of Ludwig Georg. Her sister, Anna Maria, is CEO of B. Braun.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments
abouts: Johanna Braun is a member of the board of the B. Braun Foundation, which works in education, science and public health in the field of human medicine.
B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Karl Friedrich Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
