bios: Xiang Wenbo is vice chairman of Sany Group, a heavy equipment manufacturer.
Xiang is one of three billionaires from Sany Group, along with Liang Wengen and Mao Zhongwu.
Xiang is a graduate of Dalian University of Technology with a master's degree in molding.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sven Hagstr?mer is the founder and chairman of publicly traded investment company Creades and online broker Avanza.
Hagstr?mer co-founded HQ AB, later HQ Bank, in 1990. The bank collapsed in 2010 because of an overvalued trading portfolio.
Creades was one of the first investors in Klarna, investing as early as 2007, but sold their stake in 2014.
Hagstr?mer was, for the first three seasons, one of the sharks in the Swedish version of Shark Tank.
Hagstr?mer cofounded the Raoul Wallenberg Academy, a non-profit foundation that supports and educates young people in human rights and self-leadership.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Clelia Haji-Ioannou is the daughter of Loucas Haji-Ioannou, the late Greek Cypriot shipping magnate (d. 2008).
She is a billionaire thanks to her stake in discount airline easyJet, founded by her brother Stelios.
Clelia owns approximately $240 million worth of real estate across Europe, including properties in London, Monaco and Greece.
She also has a gallery outside of Athens featuring artwork by Picasso, Warhol and Dali.
abouts: Haji-Ioannou oversaw the publication of a biography of her father, "Loucas Haji-Ioannou: The King of the Tankers."
Born in Athens, Clelia Haji-Ioannou holds both Cypriot and British citizenship and sits on the board of the Cyprus Marine Environment Protection Association.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ken Kendrick is the managing general partner and largest shareholder of the Arizona Diamondbacks baseball team.
Kendrick was a member of the group that brought the MLB expansion team to Arizona in 1995.
He built a fortune in software and banking, founding Datatel (later renamed Ellucian) and investing in Woodforest National Bank.
In 2021, Kendrick joined a group of investors, including Larry Fitzgerald, Kevin Durant and Andy Roddick, that purchased memorabilia authenticator Collectors for $850 million.
abouts: Kendrick owns one of the world's most valuable baseball card collections, estimated to be worth nine figures; it includes a 1952 Topps Mickey Mantle card.
Kendrick is a prostate cancer survivor and endowed a research position in the space at the Cleveland Clinic.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lu Lili derives her fortune from a minority stake in East Money Information and a 8.5% stake in Wanda Film Holding.
Lu is the wife of Qi Shi, who founded and chairs East Money Information, a provider of IT and software for the financial services industry in China.
She previously worked at the company's general manager's office.
Lu bought just over 8% of Wanda Film Holding for $306 million in 2023.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Fredrik 'sterberg cofounded Evolution AB with Jens von Bahr in 2006.
Evolution sells casino solutions to online gambling operators, primarily live-streamed tables of blackjack, poker, craps and roulette.
Evolution's first casino studio was set up in Riga, Lithuania in 2006. Today the company has live-casino studios in nine countries, including the U.S.
The company went public in Stockholm in 2015 and today provides its services to over 700 customers in 21 countries. Evolution's products are available globally for end users.
Prior to Evolution, he was CEO of Sportal Nordic.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Wu Bo chairs Estun Automation, a Chinese supplier of components for artificial intelligence equipment and robots.
Nanjing Estun Automation went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015.

Wu Bo received his bachelor's degree and master's degree in mechanical engineering from Southeast Universtiy in Nanjing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chris Olah is cofounder and interpretability research lead at Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $61.5 billion in March 2025, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Olah previously worked in a similar role at OpenAI and was a researcher at Google Brain.
Olah skipped college and was named a Thiel Fellow in 2012, when he was 19. In 2020, he wrote a blog post to help others decide if they should follow a similar path.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Daniela Amodei is cofounder and president of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
She cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other former OpenAI employees, including her brother Dario Amodei, who is CEO.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $61.5 billion in March 2025, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Amodei worked at OpenAI for about three years as an engineering manager and vice president.
Amodei studied English literature at the University of California, Santa Cruz, then joined fintech unicorn Stripe in 2013 as a founding recruiter.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dario Amodei is cofounder and CEO of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other former OpenAI employees, including his sister Daniela Amodei, who is president.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $61.5 billion in March 2025, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Amodei previously served as vice president of research at OpenAI, where he co-invented reinforcement learning from human feedback.
Amodei has a PhD in biophysics from Princeton University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gwynne Shotwell is SpaceX's president and COO, and manages the operations of the commercial space exploration company founded by Elon Musk.
It's grown from a futuristic idea of enabling people to live on other planets to a company with over 13,000 employees and a valuation of $350 billion.
As of March 2024, SpaceX has transported astronauts to the International Space Station nine times on behalf of NASA and three times for private company customer Axiom Space.
Shotwell was the 11th employee of SpaceX, joining the company in 2002. Before that, she was at spacecraft developer Microcosm as its space systems director.
Shotwell owns an estimated stake in SpaceX of less than 1%.
abouts: NASA has selected SpaceX to be one of the companies that will transport astronauts to the Moon's surface as part of the Artemis program.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jack Clark is cofounder and head of policy at Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six ex-OpenAI researchers.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $61.5 billion in March 2025, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Clark previously worked as a technology journalist at Bloomberg, before leaving for OpenAI in 2016.
He writes a newsletter about AI research called Import AI. It has more than 69,000 subscribers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jared Kaplan is cofounder and chief science officer of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $61.5 billion in March 2025, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Kaplan is a theoretical physicist with a PhD from Harvard. His research has been focused on quantum gravity and machine learning.
He became a professor at Johns Hopkins University in 2012 but is currently on leave.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sam McCandlish is cofounder and chief technology officer of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $61.5 billion in March 2025, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
McCandlish previously worked for three years as a member of the technical staff at OpenAI.
He has a PhD in theoretical physics from Stanford.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Tom Brown is cofounder and chief compute officer of startup Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $61.5 billion in March 2025, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
While working at OpenAI, Brown served as lead author of the white paper that introduced the GPT-3 language model.
Brown studied computer science and cognitive science at MIT. He cofounded his first company, social club Grouper, in 2011.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Andrei Filatov made his first money selling imported goods while taking part in international chess tournaments.
In 1996 together with Konstantin Nikolaev and Nikita Mishin, he founded a transport joint venture with Alexei Mordashov. They later bought him.
The trio previously owned more than a third of Globaltrans, the biggest private rail transport operator in Russia.
In December of 2017 all three withdrew from port business, selling their stakes in Global Ports.
abouts: Filatov is the president of Russian Chess Federation.
Filatov owns wine production farm La Grace Dieu Des Prieurs in France,  founded in 1885. The vineyard produces 35,000 bottles of wine a year.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: J. Christopher Flowers runs private equity firm J.C. Flowers & Co., which focuses on the financial services sector.
Flowers studied math at Harvard and then joined Goldman Sachs in 1979, becoming a partner in 1988.
He struck out on his own a decade later and in 2000 bought a beleaguered Japanese bank, Long Term Credit Bank, which had been nationalized in 1998.
He resold the business to the public under the moniker Shinsei Bank in 2004; the partners reaped $2.3 billion.
In 2008, he helped advise Bank of America and Merrill Lynch on their merger.
abouts: Flowers joined board of directors for the Kasparov Chess Foundation, named for legendary chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov, in 2015.
During his college years, Flowers wrote for the Harvard Crimson.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liang Zhaoxian is president of Galanz Group, one of China's largest suppliers of microwave ovens, air conditioners and household appliances.
The company traces its roots to 1978 when it was founded as a feather product plant.
Privately held Galanz is headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Foshan.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yang Xuegang is the chairman and CEO of China Risun Group, a supplier of coke and chemicals.
Founded in 1995, China Risunis headquartered in Beijing.
Yang Xuegangworked at the Dongwushi Reservoir Management Center-- under a government water bureau -- earlier in his career.
Yang Xuegang holds an executive master's degree in business administration from Hebei University of Technology in Tianjin.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Chen Qingzhou chairs Hytera Communications, a manufacturer of radio communications equipment.
Early in his career, Chen worked at a mobile radio communications factory as a sales manager in Fujian Province.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Giuliana Caprotti inherited her fortune from her late husband Bernardo Caprotti, who was the founder of Italian supermarket chain Esselunga.
Bernardo left his second wife Giualiana and their daughter Marina a 67% stake in the company, and gave the remaining third to his other two children.
In 2020, Giuliana and Marina bought out the remaining stake of Esselunga for nearly 2 billion Euros.
Giuliana was named honorary chair of Esselunga in 2020.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Marina Caprotti inherited most of her wealth from her late father, Bernardo Caprotti, who was the founder of Italian supermarket chain Esselunga.
Bernardo left his second wife Giuliana and daughter Marina a 67% stake in the company, and gave the remaining third to his other two children.
In 2020, Giuliana and Marina bought out the remaining stake for nearly 2 billion Euros.
Marina was named executive chair of Esselunga in 2020.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michael Jacques Gans is a Luxembourgish-American businessman who owns commercial real estate in Dublin, London, Luxembourg and Manchester.

He used to own 25% of logistics firm Supreme Group, with the rest held by his business partner Stephen Orenstein. Supreme Group was the primary supplier of food and water to the U.S. army in Afghanistan.
The firm was founded in 1957 to supply food to U.S. military bases in Germany by Orenstein's father Alfred, a former U.S. army soldier. Gans joined the company after Orenstein took over in 1985.
In 2014, two Supreme Group companies pleaded guilty to major fraud for overcharging the U.S. army for $48 million between 2005 and 2009.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Victor Jacobsson cofounded Klarna in 2005, pioneering the buy-now, pay-later model in fintech.
He left the company in 2012 but retains a stake in the business estimated at around 9%.
Private investors valued Klarna at $6.7 billion in 2022. Forbes estimates the company is now worth nearly $14 billion.
Klarna is a fully licensed bank in Europe, where it offers checking accounts, savings accounts and debit cards.
Investors in Klarna include Sequoia Capital, Dragoneer, Silver Lake, Bestseller Group, Visa and Ant Group.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Li Haizhou is chairman of Shenzhen Zhaowei Machinery & Electronics, which he founded in 2001.
The company specializes in designing, developing and manufacturing precision transmission systems.
Its main products include components that are used in automotive, smart home devices, medical technology, robotics and telecommunications.
His wife Xie Yanling is vice chairman of the listed company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Catharina Mühleis is a fourth generation heir to the Stihl family fortune, founded in 1926 by Andreas Stihl.
Primarily known for its chainsaws, the company also manufactures power tools for forestry, agriculture and construction.
Stihl, which employs 19,805 people, has manufacturing facilities in Germany, USA, Brazil, Switzerland, Austria, China and the Philippines.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Maxim Tebar is a fourth-generation heir to the Stihl family fortune, founded by his great-grandfather Andreas Stihl in 1926.
A German maker of chainsaws, the company saw $5.8 billion in sales in 2023.
His mother Karen Tebar sits on Stihl's advisory board as vice chair.

bios: Mao Zhongwu is a director of the Sany Group, a construction equipment manufacturer.
Mao is one of three billionaires from Sany Group including Liang Wengen and Xiang Wenbo.
Mao resigned as a director at Sany International in October 2019.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jack Cogen is a director and early investor in cloud computing company CoreWeave.
CoreWeave went public in March at an approximately $23 billion valuation; Cogen owns approximately 4%.
CoreWeave was founded in 2017 as a crypto firm; it now sells computing power for AI to companies including Microsoft and OpenAI.
Cogen is a private investor in early-stage companies; before that he was founder and CEO of greenhouse gas asset manager Natsource.
He was also a director at natural gas hedge fund Hudson Ridge Asset Management, where two of CoreWeave's cofounders worked.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Former hedge fund manager and activist investor Thomas Sandell closed up shop in 2019, transforming his Sandell Asset Management into a family office.
Hit hard by the great recession, the Swedish credit market specialist has built up his fortune twice.
Sandell earned an MBA from Columbia University and landed a spot at Bear Stearns in 1988 before founding Sandell Asset Management a decade later.
Initially a risk arbitrage specialist, Sandell later shifted tactics and engaged in loud proxy battles with firms like Bob Evans Farms in 2013.
At Bear Stearns he worked with famed investment banker Ace Greenberg on such deals as Kirk Kerkorian's attempted buyout of Chrysler.
abouts: Sandell is a former badminton champion in his native Sweden.
Sandell privately invests in modern art, and owns pieces by Lichtenstein and Basquiat.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joaquin del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo inherited his stake in Spain's Ferrovial S.A., one of the country's largest builders, founded by his late father Rafael del Pino Moreno.

Ferrovial, which means railway in Spanish, was started in an attic in central Madrid and got its big break when it built the railway between the cities of Las Rozas and Chamartín, laying out 18 miles of track in 30 days.
Its business now spans airports, highways, construction and energy.
Formerly an owner of London's Heathrow Airport, Ferrovial built its third runway, two terminals and an integrated baggage system.
Del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo sat on the company's board from 2010 to 2021.
His brother Rafael chairs the company and his sister Maria is president of the family's charitable foundation; both of them are also billionaires.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michael Andlauer has spent more than three decades running Canadian logistics companies focused on healthcare. He founded Andlauer Transportation Services in 1991 and Associated Logistics Solutions in 1994.
In 2019, he merged several healthcare supply-chain businesses into Andlauer Healthcare Group. It went public on the Toronto Stock Exchange that same year.
In 2004, he took over as majority owner of the AHL's Hamilton Bulldogs and oversaw the club's 2007 Calder Cup victory.
He bought a minority stake in the Montreal Canadiens NHL team in 2009 and served as the team's alternate governor until 2023, when he sold his share of the team.
Andlauer led a group that purchased 90% of the Ottawa Senators in 2023 at a $950 million valuation.

Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group Co Ltd

bios: Sun Weijie chairs the Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group, a supplier of oil exploration equipment.
Jereh was listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014.
Sun founded Jereh in 1999.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Huwen is the chairman and a co-founder of Shanghai M&G Stationary Inc.
M&G Stationary was founded in 1996.
Chen holds an EMBA degree and has been involved in stationery manufacturing since 1997.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Prakramsinh Jadeja is chairman and managing director of CNC machine maker Jyoti CNC Automation based in Rajkot, a city in the western Indian state of Gujarat.
He co-founded Jyoti CNC in 1989 as Jyoti Enterprises.
The company has installed 130,000 machines across 60 countries to date.
Jyoti supplies its machines to the defence, aerospace, infrastructure and auto industries.
Jadeja listed the company in January 2024 at a 12% premium to the IPO price.
abouts: Jadeja is a director on the board of the Indian Machine Tools Manufacturers Association.
His company has subsidiaries in France, Germany, Canada and Turkey and a research team in France.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Li Guoqiang is a founder and the CEO of Zhongsheng Group, one of China's largest car dealers.
Zhongsheng focuses on luxury and mid-to-high-end brands such as Mercedes-Benz, Lexus, Porsche and Land Rover.
Li and Huang Yi, chairman of Zhongsheng, established Zhongsheng Group in 1998.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ingvar Kamprad, who died in 2018, transferred the bulk of his Ikea empire to foundations in the 80's, but kept enough to make his sons billionaires.
Jonas and his brothers own Ikano Group, which was created to manage Ikea's real estate and financial service businesses, but was spun out in 1988.
Today Ikano Group is a $2.1 billion (sales) company with interests in banking, real estate and Asian shopping centers.
Jonas, the middle child, studied industrial and furniture design in Switzerland and applied his skills in Ikea-run subsidiary Habitat.
He is a board member of Netherlands-based Ikea parent Stichting INGKA Foundation and Ikano Group.
abouts: Ingvar Kamprad ranked among the top 10 richest people for years before lawyers produced documents proving that he had irrevocably transferred economic control.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ingvar Kamprad, who died in 2018, transferred the bulk of his Ikea empire to foundations in the 80's, but kept enough to make his sons billionaires.
Mathias and his brothers own Ikano Group, which was created to manage Ikea's real estate and financial service businesses, but was spun out in 1988.
Today Ikano Group is a $2.1 billion (sales) company with interests in banking, real estate and Asian shopping centers.
Mathias, the youngest brother, is a board member of Inter Ikea Holding, the owner of the intellectual property assets.
He sits on the board of Ikano Group, and on the supervisory board of Interogo, a Liechtenstein-based foundation that is the ultimate owner of Ikea.
abouts: Mathias put in two years as assistant to Ikea's founder, Ingvar Kamprad, ranked among the top 10 richest people in the world for five years.
Ingvar Kamprad's net worth took a slide in 2011 after his lawyers produced documents proving that he had irrevocably transferred economic control decades earlier.

bios: Ingvar Kamprad, who died in 2018, transferred the bulk of his Ikea empire to foundations in the 80's, but kept enough to make his sons billionaires.
Peter and his brothers own Ikano Group, which was created to manage Ikea's real estate and financial service businesses, but was spun out in 1988.
Today Ikano Group is a $2.1 billion (sales) company with interests in banking, real estate and Asian shopping centers.
Peter, the eldest brother, ran Ikea's Belgian operations for 12 years; he now chairs the Ikano Group.
Early in his career, Peter worked three years at a different Swedish retail giant, fast-fashion company H&M.

bios: Tang Xiuguo is one of four founders of Sany Group, one of China's largest suppliers of construction equipment.
He has been the director and president of Sany Group since 2002.
Sany's holding company was founded in Hunan Province in 1989 as a small welding material factory.
Tang holds a bachelor degree in metallic materials from Central South University in 1983.

financialAssets.companyName: Alimentation Couche Tard Inc. Cl A

bios: Réal Plourde is a cofounder and board member of Alimentation Couche-Tard, the Canadian convenience store giant that owns the Circle K chain.
Couche-Tard does $63 billion in annual revenue across more than 14,000 stores.
The chain has made three other cofounders billionaires: former CEO Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin and Jacques D'Amours.
Couche-Tard has ballooned by snatching up competitors, including Minnesota-based Holiday Stationstores for $1.6 billion in December 2017.
Plourde held a number of roles at the business, including chief operating officer and manager of technical services. From 2011 to 2014, he was chairman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mike Danson is the CEO of GlobalData, which provides data analytics to such customers as Schweppes and Saab.
The son of two teachers, neither of whom went to university, Danson went to Oxford University and got his start in consulting.
Danson founded an earlier company, Datamonitor Financial, in his London flat in 1990, reportedly funding it with credit cards.
He took it public and reportedly pocketed more than $200 million when it was acquired in 2007. GlobalData later bought back parts of that first business.
The grandson of Wigan miners, he now owns his hometown's soccer team, Wigan Athletic FC. and rugby team Wigan Warriors as well as left-leaning publication New Statesman.
abouts: His Danson Foundation offers up to 60 paid internships in London each year to undergrads of Oxford's St Anne's College, where he graduated in 1982 with a law degree.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Inspired by geologist father, Timothy Headington founded Headington Oil in 1978. He sold his North Dakota oilfields to XTO Energy in 2008.
He found a new passion in filmmaking and helped bankroll "Hugo," "Argo," "World War Z," and the 2018 reboot of "Lara Croft: Tomb Raider."
He has invested in downtown Dallas, where he owns the Joule Hotel and department store 4510 and is partnering on a Virgin Hotel with Richard Branson.
After Oklahoma University, Headington earned graduate degrees in theology and psychology at Fuller Theological Seminary.
abouts: Headington was inducted into the Oklahoma Hall of Fame in 2014.
Headington cofounded the Headington Institute, a nonprofit organization that provides psychological support for humanitarian workers and first responders.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ankur Jain founded and runs home rental rewards startup Bilt Rewards, which raised $200 million from private investors at a $3.1 billion valuation in January 2024.
Bilt Rewards processes rent payments and enables renters to earn and redeem points with airlines, hotels, gyms and restaurants.
Jain, who is CEO, owns about 36% of Bilt Rewards, which is based in New York City.
Jain previously cofounded Humin, an app that combined contacts, calendars and more and was acquired by Tinder; he made the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2015.
Jain's father, former Microsoft executive Naveen Jain, was briefly a billionaire in 2000 when shares of InfoSpace, the search engine he founded, peaked.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wu Zhongyi is the vice chairman of Yealink Network Technology, a supplier of video conferencing solutions and Internet phones.
Yealink Chairman Chen Zhisong is also a member of the 2019 Forbes China Rich List.
Yealink is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Xiamen.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Oliver Samwer and his brothers Alexander and Marc founded Berlin-based tech incubator Rocket Internet in 2007 and took it public in October 2014.
Oliver is the middle brother and the CEO of Rocket Internet, which delisted from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in October 2020.
Together, the Samwers own around 45% of Rocket. The company was valued at more than $8 billion at the time of its IPO.
Inspired by the dot-com boom, they created a German auction site, Alando, in 1999 and sold it to eBay for $43 million after a few months.
That was followed by the creation of mobile phone content provider Jamba!, which they sold to Verisign in 2004 for $273 million.
abouts: Oliver once said in an interview that he has no time for hobbies, preferring to spend his spare time with his children.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: LeBron James is the first active NBA player to become a billionaire.
Born to a 16-year-old single mother, he lived with an assortment of family members, friends and neighbors, plus his youth football coach, before being drafted by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003.
James has since gone on to earn more than $500 million in pretax salary from stints with the Cavaliers, the Miami Heat and his current team, the Los Angeles Lakers.
He has raked in upwards of $900 million (pretax) off the court, according to Forbes estimates, from his business ventures and endorsement deals with brands including Nike.
Key to his billionaire status: James has been more than a pitchman, taking equity in brands he works with, including Beats by Dre.
His LeBron James Family Foundation opened its first elementary school in 2018 and has pledged to spend more than $40 million to send kids to college.
abouts: James has publicly dreamed about one day owning an NBA team. As an investor in Fenway Sports Group, he already owns stakes in pro baseball, soccer and hockey teams.
In 2021, James sold a minority stake in his movie and TV production business, the SpringHill Company, to a handful of investors at a $725 million valuation.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hiroshi Ishibashi is a grandson of the founder of Bridgestone, the world's second-largest tire maker by revenue.
He owns a small but valuable stake in the Tokyo-listed company but does not hold any executive position.
Hiroshi heads the Ishibashi Foundation, which operates Tokyo's Bridgestone Museum of Art.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Schuurman cofounded Elastic, a Netherlands-based software company that went public in October 2018 on the NYSE.
Elastic creates software for search, data and analytics purposes.
Schuurman, who has a nearly 10% stake in Elastic, first became a billionaire in December 2018.
He served as Elastic's CEO from 2012 to 2017, and now sits on the board of directors.
He cofounded another software company, SpringSource, which was acquired by VMware in 2009 for $420 million.
abouts: Some of Schuurman's hobbies include cooking and playing guitar.
He also founded and chairs FutureNL, a non-profit that supports digital literacy in Dutch primary and secondary schools.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Danilo Iervolino is an Italian entrepreneur who founded online university UniPegaso in 2006, one of the first to be established in Italy.
Iervolino started UniPegaso at age 28 and grew it to become the largest in Italy, serving more than 120,000 students.
He sold his company Multiversity, which includes UniPegaso, to private equity firm CVC Capital Partners for $1.3 billion in October 2021.
Since selling UniPegaso, Iervolino has purchased Italian soccer team Salernitana.
He also invests in Italian tech startups, both independently and through a startup accelerator and venture capital funds.
abouts: Iervolino was inspired to launch an online university in Italy when he traveled to the U.S. after developing online master's programs at the University of Salerno.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Martin Klenk is cofounder and CTO of enterprise software startup Celonis.
The Munich-based company was valued by private investors at $13 billion in 2022. Klenk owns a 16% stake.
The company disputes Forbes' valuation, which accounts for the downturn in private markets since the company's last funding round.
Klenk's cofounders Bastian Nominacher and Alexander Rinke are also billionaires. Nominacher and Rinke serve as co-CEOs.
Celonis' cofounders launched the company in 2011 after graduating from Technical University of Munich.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Gyorgy Gattyan made the bulk of his fortune from porn site LiveJasmin.com. He is also a cofounder of the International Teqball Federation
He founded the political party Megoldás Mozgalom (Solution Movement) prior the 2022 Hungarian Election but failed to win any seats in Parliament. 
He co-founded the Hungarian Prima Primissima Award to celebrate achievements in Hungarian Culture and supports causes related to children in need.
abouts: He is an active movie and TV producer whose work includes the last 11 episodes of the Hungarian Cult-classic animation series, Hungarian Folk Tales.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zeng Chaoyi is a director of Tianshan Aluminum Group, a Chinese supplier of aluminum products.
Tianshan's shares trade at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; it's headquartered in Xinjiang.
Shimge Pump Industry Group acquired Tianshan Aluminum Group in 2020 in a backdoor listing and changed its name to Tianshan Aluminum Group.
Brother Zeng Chaoyi's brother Zeng Chaolin is Tianshan's chairman and also a billionaire.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hideyuki Busujima is the son of Sankyo founder Kunio Busujima, who died in October 2016.
In 2023, Hideyuki stepped down as CEO of pachinko-machine maker Sankyo, but remains chairman.
Kunio transferred his shares of publicly-traded Sankyo to Hideyuki in 2014.
In 2020, Hideyuki sold 20 million shares back to the company, which cancelled them.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhao Hongfei chairs Shenzhen-listed software firm Thunder Software Technology.
Zhao holds a master's degree from the Beijing Institute of Technology.
Zhao worked for a joint venture of Japan's NEC and the Chinese Academy of Science's Institute of Software before founding Thunder in 2008.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dick Wolf is a writer and producer who created crime series Law & Order and built Wolf Entertainment into one of television's most prolific companies.
Law & Order first aired on NBC in 1990 and continues to have a near ubiquitous presence across a variety of networks and streaming platforms.
Wolf Entertainment's other programs include Law & Order: SVU, Law & Order: Organized Crime, three Chicago shows (Fire, Med, P.D.) and three F.B.I. shows. He produces 200 episodes per year.
Wolf maintains a large art collection, even after donating 200 pieces of Baroque and Renaissance art plus enough money to have two galleries named for him at New York's  Metropolitan Museum of Art.
abouts: Wolf began his career in advertising and was once a writer on 1980s TV hit Miami Vice.
Law & Order: SVU is the longest-running network drama in television history, airing continuously since 1999.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Amanda Westphal Radcliffe owns 21% of publicly traded tax solutions provider Vertex Inc.
The Pennsylvania-based company was founded in 1978 by Westphal Radcliffe's parents, Ray and Antoinette Westphal.
Westphal Radcliffe and her two siblings, Jeffrey Westphal and Stefanie Westphal Thompson, purchased the company from their parents in 2000.
Together, they took the company public in 2020. Westphal Thompson is also a billionaire.
Westphal Radcliffe sits on Vertex's board of directors.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bruce Springsteen, a.k.a. The Boss, spun his New Jersey, blue-collar upbringing into a substantial fortune from five decades of touring and recording.
Springsteen and his E Street Band met playing clubs along the Jersey Shore, most famously at Asbury Park's The Stone Pony.
He's sold over 140 million albums globally, with 21 studio albums, 10 live albums and seven EPs.
Accolades include 20 Grammys, an Oscar, two Golden Globes, a special Tony award and inductions in both the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Songwriters Hall of Fame.
In 2021, Springsteen sold his music catalog--his life's work--to longtime label home Sony for a $500 million lump sum.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Lim cofounded real estate fund manager ARA Asset Management in 2002, at age 45, with the backing of Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-shing.
In 2016, Lim, along with U.S. private equity firm Warburg Pincus and China's AVIC Trust, took ARA private from the Singapore Stock Exchange in a $1.3 billion buyout.
In 2022, Hong Kong-based real asset manager ESR Group acquired ARA for $5.2 billion in stock and cash.
Lim, who has a small stake in ESR Group, now is the chairman of his JL Family Office.
He has been the chairman of the Asia Pacific Real Assets Association since 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lim Kaling is an early investor and non-executive director of Razer, a gaming hardware maker that was set up in 2005.
The company has acquired a huge global following and sold millions of gaming laptops, mice, fitness bands and tablets. It went public in Hong Kong in 2017, raising $529 million.
Lim and Razer cofounder Min-Liang Tan took the company private in 2022 in a deal that valued it at $3.2 billion.
Lim also runs the Lim Teck Lee group, a family business with interests in real estate, manufacturing and trading.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ed Hallen is cofounder and chief product officer of Klaviyo, which sells marketing automation software.
The firm raised more than $500 million from venture capitalists and made a gross profit of $675 million in 2024.
Klaviyo was one of the first tech firms to test the IPO waters after a market downturn; it went public in 2023.
In 2017, Hallen stepped away from a full-time role at Klaviyo to start HR automation firm Team Engine, but rejoined in 2021 as chief product officer.
Before Klaviyo, he worked at a business analytics software firm. He holds a degree in systems engineering from the University of Virginia and an MBA from MIT.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Eddy Sugianto is the founder of coal mining group Mandiri and president commissioner of its Indonesia-listed Prima Andalan Mandiri.
He took Prima Andalan Mandiri public in 2021, raising $32 million.
His coal services company Mandiri Herindo Adiperkasa, also known as Mandiri Services, raised $31 million through an IPO in 2023.
Eddy's brother Handy Glivirgo is the president director of Prima Andalan Mandiri and a director of Mandiri Services.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Noubar Afeyan is the founder and CEO of Cambridge, Mass. life sciences innovation firm Flagship Pioneering.
He's also the chairman and cofounder of biotech firm Moderna, known for its Covid-19 vaccine which was authorized by the U.S. FDA in December 2020.
Afeyan has helped start more than 70 public and private healthcare and life sciences companies over the course of his career.
Born in Beirut, Lebanon, in 1962 to Armenian parents, he and his family fled the Lebanese Civil War to move to Montreal in 1975.
Beyond his stake in Moderna, he also owns shares in more than a dozen publicly traded biotech companies in the U.S.
abouts: Afeyan is a lecturer at Harvard Business School and also taught at MIT's Sloan School of Management from 2000 to 2016.
In 2014 he helped launch UWC Dilijan, an international boarding school in the town of Dilijan in the mountains of northern Armenia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Susumu Fujita founded website and online blog and TV platform CyberAgent in 1998.
He owns a minority stake in the Tokyo-listed company.
The company also has an internet and mobile phone advertising agency.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pan Shiyi and wife Zhang Xin co-founded Beijing real estate developer Soho China.
Soho China is listed in Hong Kong and is best known for developing commercial real estate in Beijing and Shanghai.
Pan and Zhang stepped down from their leadership roles as chairman and CEO "in order to focus on supporting the arts and philanthropic pursuits" in 2022 but remain on the board.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Soichiro Minami founded and runs Visional, a job search and human resources software firm.
U.S.-educated Minami, founded the firm in 2009 after working for Morgan Stanley and Japanese e-commerce giant Rakuten, founded by billionaire Hiroshi Mikitani.
In April 2021, Minami listed the firm on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's bourse for startups, Mothers.
Visional posted over $380 million in revenue in the fiscal year ended in July 2023.
abouts: Minami has a double degree in economics and international relations from Tufts University.
In 2004, he helped Rakuten set up its professional baseball team, the Rakuten Golden Eagles.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Vladimir Krupchak's fortune stems from his stake in Arkhangelsk Pulp and Paper Mill (APPM), Russia's largest producer of cardboard and one of its biggest makers of market pulp.
Prior to 2022 Krupchak controlled the Russian and Ukrainian assets of Austria's Pulp Mill Holding.
In the 2000s he was involved in a corporate battle with billionaire Oleg Deripaska for control of APPM.
Krupchak is a former member of the State Duma of Russia, the country's parliament.
abouts: His wife is a stakeholder of Titan Group, a leading company in Russia's sawn timber market.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Christian Angermayer invests in life sciences, fintech, AI, psychedelics and cryptocurrencies through his family office Apeiron Investment Group.
He made his first millions cofounding biotech firm Ribopharma with his college professors; he sold his stake when it merged with Alnylam in 2003.
His Malta-based Apeiron owns shares in several publicly traded firms and private companies in the U.S., Germany, Canada and Australia.
His holdings include psychedelics biopharma firm Atai Life Sciences and blockchain holding company Cryptology, alongside co-investor Mike Novogratz.
He owns an extensive art collection that includes ancient artifacts highlighting the role that psychedelics have played in human history.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sergey Lomakin cofounded Russian discount retailer Fix Price in 2007 together with Artem Khachatryan.
The chain has opened more than 4,000 stores in Russia, Kazakhstan, Georgia, Belarus, Latvia, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.
Lomakin serves as chairman of the company, which went public in 2021.
His cofounder, Khachatryan, is also a billionaire.
In December 2023 Lomakin bought nearly all of Khachatryan's stake in company for $990 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Christodoulou is the founder and owner of the Yianis Group, a London-based real estate firm with properties in the U.K. and Europe.
Born in Cyprus, he fled the country with his family after the Turkish invasion of the island in 1974 and resettled in the U.K.
He dropped out of school at age 16 and worked as a diamond mounter, using his early profits to buy his first property: a studio apartment in London.
The Yianis Group's portfolio includes residential, retail, office and hotel properties, including two five-star hotels in London's Canary Wharf.
The Monaco resident still maintains close ties with his birth country and his Yianis Christodoulou Foundation supports children's education in Cyprus.
abouts: John is a nickname; his full name is Yianakis Theophani Christodoulou.
He owns a 245-foot-yacht, Zeus, which features decks made of teak wood.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Nikita Mishin and partners Konstantin Nikolaev and Andrei Filatov formerly owned roughly one third of Globaltrans, Russia's biggest private rail operator.
In December of 2017 the partners sold their  stakes in Global Ports, exiting the port business.
He and his partners worked together at a railroad freight company.
Since 2024, he's held dual citizenship in the U.K., where he has resided for more than a decade.
abouts: Mishin is the founder of charity fund Dar, which helps talented children, including ones from low-income families.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wei Lidong chairs Shanghai-headquartered Weaver Network, which provides digital collaboration and workflow software to more than 70,000 clients.
Weaver went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
In 2019, the company added a regional headquarter in Singapore to expand its footprint in the Asia-Pacific region.
Wei holds a bachelor's degree from Zhejiang University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stefanie Westphal Thompson owns 21% of publicly traded tax solutions provider Vertex Inc.
The Pennsylvania-based company was founded in 1978 by Westphal Thompson's parents, Ray and Antoinette Westphal.
Westphal Thompson and her two siblings, Jeffrey Westphal and Amanda Westphal Radcliffe, purchased the company from their parents in 2000.
Together, they took the company public in July 2020. Westphal Radcliffe is also a billionaire.
Westphal Thompson sits on Vertex's board of directors.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Suresh Krishna chairs the Chennai-based Sundram Fasteners, which makes components for the auto sector.
Krishna is the oldest member of the third generation of the storied T.V. Sundaram Iyengar family from the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
Four families tied to the TVS Group restructured their cross-holdings, as per a 2020 agreement, which gave each family both ownership and control of their respective companies.
His eldest daughter Preethi has a board seat while two other daughters, Arathi and Arundathi, run the company.
abouts: Krishna founded the company in 1966 as a small industrial unit in Ambattur, a suburb of Chennai city.
He studied literature in the U.S. and Germany.
Global clients of Sundram Fasteners include General Motors and Cummins.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Konstantin Nikolaev and his partners Nikita Mishin andAndrei Filatov formerly owned a third of Globaltrans, Russia's biggest private rail transport operator.
The trio sold their stakes in Global Ports, exiting the port business in December 2017.
He and his partners worked together at Petra, a railroad freight company.
abouts: Nikolaev is one of the co-founders of Moscow management school Skolkovo, the first business school in Russia.
In 1996 the partners agreed with one of Petra's clients, Alexei Mordashov's Severstal, to start a transport company. They later bought him out.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gao Yi is the chairman of Yifeng Pharmacy Chain, which has more than 4,000 stores across China.
Yifeng employs more than 20,000.
Yifeng, headquartered in the central China city of Changsha, was founded by Gao in 2001.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xu Xudong chairs Ningbo Xusheng Auto Technology.
Xusheng is a supplier of gear boxes and battery protection shells to Tesla.
Other customers include Chrysler, Mahler and Bosch.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jan-Hendrik Goldbeck is co-CEO of the eponymous construction giant founded by his father  Ortwin Goldbeck in 1969.
Goldbeck's projects include factories, warehouses, schools, offices and residential properties.
The company, which employs 12,500 people, works on more than 500 projects annually.
Goldbeck and his brothers, Jörg-Uwe and Joachim, each own about a third of the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joachim Goldbeck derives his fortune from the eponymous construction company founded by his father, Ortwin Goldbeck, in 1969.
His two brothers are co-CEOs of the German builder, which has 12,500 employees and 100 locations worldwide.
One of its country's largest developers, Goldbeck completes more than 500 projects annually; its services include factories, warehouses, offices, schools, parking lots and residential buildings.
He and his brothers each own about a third of the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jörg-Uwe Goldbeck is co-CEO of the eponymous construction company, which his father, Ortwin Goldbeck, started in 1969 with just seven employees.
One of Germany's largest builders, Goldbeck's projects include factories, warehouses, schools, offices, parking lots and residential properties.
With more than 100 locations worldwide, the builder employs 12,500 people and manages more than 500 projects annually.
Goldbeck was one of the main developers for the Telsa factory in Germany.
He and his brothers, Jan-Hendrik (co-CEO) and Jörg-Uwe, each own about a third of the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chung Yong-jin is a grandson of Samsung group founder Lee Byung-Chull and a cousin of Samsung Electronics executive chairman Jay Y. Lee.
The bulk of his fortune comes from Samsung Electronics and discount chain E-Mart, a unit of Korea's retail conglomerate Shinsegae Group.
In 2024, Chung was promoted from vice chairman to chairman of Shinsegae, a retail conglomerate.
In 2021, Shinsegae acquired Korean baseball team SK Wyverns (now SSG Landers), winner of four championships, from the SK group for about $120 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Tianqiao is the founder, chairman and CEO of Shanda Investment Group, founded in 1999 by Chen and his family.
Chen is credited with having pioneered and built the online game industry and the online literature industry in China.
Chen stepped down as CEO of Shanda Interactive Entertainment in 2012 and then took the company private.
Chen and his wife Chrissy are active philanthropists, supporting research programs on brain science.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Tony Tan Caktiong is the founder and chairman of Jollibee Food, one of the world's fastest-growing Asian restaurant chains.
Jollibee operates over 9,500 outlets under 19 brands across the Philippines as well as in overseas markets such as Singapore, Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates.
Jollibee sells Filipino, Chinese, American and European dishes adapted to a quick-serve and affordable format.
In 2024, Jollibee acquired a majority stake in South Korean's Compose Coffee. The deal valued the coffee chain at $340 million.
With partner Edgar Sia II, Caktiong also owns a stake in the fast-growing real estate developer DoubleDragon Corporation.
abouts: Caktiong's mother thought Tony was the most difficult to bring up among his brothers because he was the pickiest in terms of taste.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Christian Herz owns 45% of the private equity firm Mayfair SE, whose investments have included the sports apparel company Puma.
He is the grandson of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz, who built a fortune based on the importation and sale of coffee.
His father, Guenter, ran Tchibo for almost 35 years. The family also built a stake in skin-care company Beiersdorf, whose brands include Nivea.
Guenter and his sister, Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel, founded Mayfair after they were bought out of the family business in 2003.
As one of Mayfair's managing directors, Christian Herz is active in the shaping investment decisions.
abouts: Italian restaurant operator Vapiano, in which Mayfair had a stake, filed for bankruptcy after all locations in several countries closed in response to the pandemic.
Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel and her children have exited Mayfair, reportedly founding Bilton Holding AG to invest primarily in real estate.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michaela Herz owns 45% of the private equity firm Mayfair SE, whose investments have included the sports apparel company Puma.
She is a granddaughter of Tchibo cofounder Max Herz, who built a fortune based on the import and sale of coffee.
Her father, Guenter, ran Tchibo for almost 35 years. The family also built a stake in skin-care company Beiersdorf, whose brands include Nivea.
Guenter and his sister, Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel, founded Mayfair after they sold their stake in the family business in 2003.
As one of Mayfair's managing directors, Michaela Herz is active in shaping investment decisions.
abouts: Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel and her children have exited Mayfair, reportedly founding Bilton Holding AG to invest primarily in real estate.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sytse 'Sid' Sijbrandij founded business software firm GitLab in 2012 and took it public in the U.S. in October 2021.
Sijbrandij, is from the Netherlands but lives in the San Francisco Bay Area.
He built out GitLab as a fully remote business, without a physical office.
In the fiscal year through January 2022, GitLab had a net loss of $155.1 million on revenues of $252.7 million.
Before founding GitLab, Sijbrandij worked as a web project manager for the Dutch Ministry of Justice and at a submarine company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Known as the father of the Russian stock market, Ruben Vardanyan cofounded investment company Troika Dialog in the early 1990s.
In 2013, Vardanyan and his managers sold Troika Dialog to state-owned Sberbank for $1.4 billion.
Vardanyan founded investment boutique Vardanyan, Broitman and partners, which serves ultra high-net-worth individuals, in 2014.
In 2021 he obtained Armenian citizenship and later renounced his Russian citizenship and moved to Armenia.
In November 2022 Vardanyan was appointed the State Minister of Artsakh (Karabakh). He transferred his business assets to the family trust. In February 2023 he dismissed as State Minister.
In September 2023 Vardanyan was arrested by the Azerbaijani State Border Service during an attempt to cross the border into Armenia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: M.R.Jaishankar is the chairman of South Indian real estate firm Brigade Enterprises, which he founded in 1986.
Brigade has projects in residential, office, retail and hospitality across the southern Indian states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Kerala.
Brigade also runs hotels with 1,500 rooms across five cities, including a Holiday Inn in Chennai.
His daughters Pavitra and Nirupa were appointed as managing director and joint managing director respectively in 2022.
abouts: He started his entrepreneurial career in 1980 with MLR Industries which made chicory for coffee. He shut it down in 1991.
Jaishankar hails from a family of coffee planters from Chikmagalur town in Karnataka state.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michele Kang founded healthcare information technology Cognosante in 2008, which she sold to Accenture in 2024.
Born in South Korea, Kang moved to the United States for college and earned a bachelor's degree in economics from The University of Chicago and a master's degree from Yale.
She owns majority stakes in the NWSL's Washington Spirit, France's OL Lyonnes and England's London City Lionesses, which recently earned promotion to the Women's Super League.
She also has a stake in John Textor's Eagle Football Holdings, which controls three other European clubs, one in Florida and one in Brazil.
In 2024, Kang launched Kynisca, the world's first multi-team global organization focused on professionalizing women's football, and proving its commercial potential and cultural impact.
abouts: Kang is the first woman of color to be the majority owner of a National Women's Soccer League team.
Kang convinced her parents to use her wedding fund to finance her first year of college in the U.S.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hisao Nagata is the founder and chairman of Trial Holdings, a discount supermarket chain with interests in retail IT and developing AI systems. His son Hiroyuki is a director.

Nagata's father, Oumi, opened a thrift store called Asahiya in 1974 in Fukuoka, which Hisao took over in 1981. Three years later, he changed the name to Trial Company and also started a software developer focusing on retail.
Trial has developed technology to decrease labor costs and increase efficiency, including self-checkout shopping carts and AI-powered cameras to gather shopper behavior data and monitor inventory.
Trial has over 300 stores in Japan and posted $4.6 billion in revenue in the fiscal year ended in June 2024.
In March 2024, Trial was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Growth bourse.
abouts: The first Trial discount store opened in 1992.
Nagata has written books on retail AI and digitization, including one in 2022 titled 'How to Win the Retail Digital Transformation.'

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Takaya Awata is president and CEO of Tokyo-listed Toridoll Holdings, Japan's largest operator of udon noodle  restaurants.
Awata opened his first yakitori grilled-chicken restaurant in 1985, after dropping out of the Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.
Toridoll has over 2,000 restaurants in Japan, China, Singapore, Europe. and the U.S.
In October 2021, the firm listed its Tam Jai International, an operator of Chinese noodle restaurants that it acquired in 2018, on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
The company posted $1.9 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through March 2025, a 16% jump from the previous year.
abouts: In February 2025, Toridoll proposed delisting Tam Jai to make it a wholly-owned subsidiary.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Fund manager Cheah Cheng Hye is co-chairman of Hong Kong-listed Value Partners Group.
He cofounded the asset-management company in 1993, and listed it in 2007.
After graduating from Penang Free School, he worked as a subeditor and writer at The Star newspaper in Malaysia.
In 1974, he traveled to Hong Kong, where he had stints in financial journalism at the Far Eastern Economic Review and the Asian Wall Street Journal.
He worked at Morgan Grenfell Group in Hong Kong before starting Value Partners.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Naresh Trehan, one of India's top cardiac surgeons, founded the Medanta hospital chain in 2007 with one hospital in Delhi.
He is chairman, managing director and chief cardiac surgeon at Medanta, which offers services across more than 30 specialties including cardiology, neurology and oncology.
Medanta has five hospitals across North India with more than 2,700 hospital beds
He listed Global Health, the parent company of Medanta, on the Indian bourses in 2022.
abouts: Trehan is a recipient of the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Shri, among India's highest civilian honours.
Medanta is building a 400-bed super specialty hospital in south Delhi.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Scott Smith is one of three cofounders of Utah-based cloud computing company Qualtrics.
He cofounded the company in Provo, Utah in 2002 with his two sons, Ryan and Jared; Ryan is the CEO.
Three days before its scheduled IPO in January 2019, Qualtrics was acquired by German software firm SAP for $8 billion in cash.
Scott owned about 14% of the company at the time of the sale.
The company sold a second time in March 2023 to Silver Lake and CPP Investments at a $12.5 billion valuation.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Aydin Dogan owns 29% of Dogan Holding, a public company active in oil distribution, electricity production, real estate, tourism and e-commerce.
He was once Turkey's biggest media boss but came into conflict with the policies of the Turkish government.
In 2018, he sold his portfolio (including TV channels Kanal D and CNN Turk, and the newspapers Hurriyet, Posta and Fanatik) for around $1.1 billion.
In 2012, he entered into a licensing deal with Donald Trump for an office tower and shopping mall project in Instanbul.
In 2019, he sold Trump Towers to publicly traded Dogan Holding for around $150 million.
abouts: In 2009, Dogan handed over management of the Dogan companies to his four daughters.
In 2019, he brought out a book titled "Aydın Sozler" ("Enlightened Words" - a pun on his name), consisting of aphorisms from his work life.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhang chairs Yonghui Superstores, an operator of hypermarkets and supermarkets.
His brother Zhang Xuanning is the vice chairman of Yonghui Superstores.
Yonghui Superstore listed on Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2010.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Zhang Tianyu chairs Fibocom Wireless, a supplier of wireless communication modules and solutions.
Fibocom Wireless went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: One of the highest paid actors in Hollywood history, Arnold Schwarzenegger has earned some $500 million (before taxes and fees) in paychecks and profit-sharing deals from his movies.
He's made even more from early bets on everything from California real estate to stakes in some of the world's most valuable brands.
One of his best bets: Buying a minority stake in fellow billionaire David Booth's Dimensional Fund Advisors when it was managing $12 billion in assets.
Founded in 1996, DFA now has $777 billion of assets under management.
Other valuable investments include a piece of Easton Town Center, the Columbus, Ohio mall created by billionaire Les Wexner, and equity in the Waldorf Astoria hotel in Los Angeles.
Today, Schwarzenegger continues to own several businesses: film and production company Oak Productions, Fitness Publications Inc and film and trademarking holding venture Pumping Iron America.
abouts: Between 1970 and 2019, Schwarzenegger churned out around 50 films that made $5.5 billion at the box office.
Schwarzenegger had a costly divorce in 2021 from Kennedy family member Maria Shriver; he could be worth nearly double his current fortune if the pair had a prenup.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Qin Long chairs Qingdao Sentury Tire, a supplier of motorsport and aircraft tires.
Qin founded Qingdao Sentury Tire in 2007.
Qingdao Sentury Tire went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Waleed bin Ibrahim Al Ibrahim is founder and chairman of MBC Group Company, an Arab TV broadcaster originally called Middle East Broadcasting Center.
MBC Group listed its shares in Saudi Arabia in late 2023; Al Ibrahim owns a 36% stake, while the Saudi Public Investment Fund owns 54%, effectively making it a state-controlled company.
MBC operates 13 satellite-broadcast channels including English-language news channel Al Arabiya, based in Dubai--a competitor to Al Jazeera.
MBC Group also launched and owns Arabic-language streaming platform Shahid, considered the largest such platform in Arabic.
According to media reports, Al Ibrahim was detained by the Saudi government in Riyadh's Ritz Carlton Hotel--along with hundreds of fellow business leaders--for 83 days starting in November 2017.
abouts: Al Ibrahim's sister was married to Saudi Arabia's late King Fahd (d. 2005); his close ties to the king reportedly helped his business flourish.
MBC Group got its start in London in 1991 with a single satellite TV channel; Al Ibrahim expanded and moved its headquarters to Dubai in 2002 and to Riyadh in 2022.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jane Goldman is America's only female billionaire running a real estate firm. She heads up Solil Management, which she owns with her three siblings.
The youngest daughter of Sol Goldman (d. 1987), once New York's biggest landlord, she oversees a portfolio that includes at least 400 properties.
Trophies include apartments on the Upper East Side and the block of land in Midtown Manhattan that includes the Olympic Tower and the Cartier Mansion.
The family also owns a 17% stake in the World Trade Center developments in lower Manhattan.
Her brother Allan is co-chair but has taken a back seat in recent years. Her sisters Amy and Diane Kemper are senior advisers.
abouts: The New York City resident paid $31 million in 2015 for a Palm Beach estate originally owned by the Kennedys; she sold it for $70 million in June 2020.
The Goldman family name is all over Yale University, from the law library named after Jane's mother, Lilian, to a $10 million endowed professorship.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Li Hongjing is chairman and general manager of Shanghai-listed automotive electronic components manufacturer Autel Intelligent Technology.
Li is also the founder and majority shareholder of drone supplier Autel Robotics.
Li holds a MBA from Carnegie Mellon University.
Li once worked at Pittsburgh National Corp. as an strategic analyst.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Trained pilot Chang Kuo-Wei is the chairman of Starlux Airlines, Taiwan's third-largest international carrier by passengers carried and cargo volume.
He is the youngest son of Chang Yung Fa, the late founder of Evergreen Marine, one of the world's largest shipping companies.
Former chairman of the family's EVA Airways, Kuo-Wei was ousted from the family businesses by his three stepbrothers following Yung Fa's death in 2016.
He struck out on his own and set up Starlux two years later, which went public on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in October 2024.
After the late patriarch's death, a family feud broke out over his will that left certain assets to Kuo-Wei. The Taiwan Supreme Court ruled in favor of Kuo-Wei in August 2024.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wayne Weaver is the chairman of shoe retailer Show Carnival.
Together Weaver and his wife Delores are the largest individual shareholders of Shoe Carnival, with a 29% stake.
He was the first owner of the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars and owned a majority of the team for 18 years
He sold his stake in the Jaguars to billionaire Shahid Khan in 2011 for $770 million
Weaver started his career as a shoe salesman and eventually became CEO of Nine West in 1978.
abouts: Weaver grew up in public housing and did odd jobs like digging ditches and delivering mail. He never attended college.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Maxim Shubarev is the founder of Setl Group, one of Russia's largest real estate developers.
Shubarev first worked as a radio equipment assembler before starting Petersburg Real Estate in the 1990s.
In 2006 the company rebranded and changed its name to Setl Group.
The company has built about 350 apartment buildings in three decades.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Anatoly Skurov's fortune stems from the sale of his stakes in coal producer Sibuglemet and  fertilizer maker Uralkali, which is traded in Moscow.
He is a former designer of Soviet machine-building factories and worked for the state-owned coal producer Rosugol, where he took part in the reform of the Russian coal industry.
In 1995, with Vladimir Melnichenko and Valentin Bukhtoyarov, both former billionaires, he founded the coal producer Sibuglemet.
In 2017 Skurov started coal mining project Uvalnaya, which produces more than 6 million tons of coal annually.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jens von Bahr cofounded publicly traded casino supplier Evolution AB with Fredrik 'sterberg in 2006.
He was CEO of Evolutions until 2016 and is now chairman of the company, which primarily sells live-streamed tables of blackjack, poker, craps and roulette to online gambling operators.
The company went public in Stockholm in 2015 and now provides its services to over 700 customers in 21 countries. Evolution's products are available globally for end users.
Evolution's first casino studio was set up in Riga, Lithuania. Today the company has live-casino studios in nine countries, including the U.S.
Before starting Evolution, von Bahr headed the Sri Lankan operations of Oriflame, a Swiss-Swedish multi-level marketing company that sells beauty products.
abouts: The land of Von Bahr's house is owned the king of Sweden; he was denied permission to build a pool on the property.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Koo Bon-neung runs Heesung Electronics, which makes display components for TVs, computers, tablets and smartphones.
He is the younger brother of Koo Bon-moo, the late chairman of the LG Group, one of the top five conglomerates in South Korea.
In 2004 his son Koo Kwang-mo was adopted by his brother who lost his own son in a car accident. Kwang-mo now helms LG as its chairman.
abouts: Koo is a former president of the Korea Baseball Organization.
He started his career in LG in 1976 as a manager for the company's branch in Chicago.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Craig Abod is the founder and owner of Carahsoft, a Virginia-based technology company that specializes in IT services for government agencies.
Abod founded Carahsoft in 2004 and has grown the business to revenue of more than $11 billion.
Carahsoft ranked No. 26 on Forbes's 2024 list of America's Largest Private Companies.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Marco Squinzi is the co-CEO and part-owner of MAPEI, a manufacturer of chemical products used in construction based in Milan, Italy.
He and his sister Veronica became co-CEOs in July 2019, three months before the death of their father Giorgio, who took over the company in 1984.
MAPEI was founded by Giorgio's father, Rodolfo, in 1937; its products have been used to restore the Coliseum in Rome and in the Panama City metro.
Marco shares ownership of MAPEI with Veronica and his cousin Simona Giorgetta, who owns the largest stake in the company.
Together with his sister and his cousin, he also owns Italian soccer team Sassuolo Calcio, which Giorgio acquired in 2003.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Veronica Squinzi is the co-CEO and part-owner of MAPEI, a manufacturer of chemical products used in construction based in Milan, Italy.
She and her brother Marco became co-CEOs in July 2019, three months before the death of their father Giorgio, who took over the company in 1984.
MAPEI was founded by Giorgio's father, Rodolfo, in 1937; its products have been used to restore the Coliseum in Rome and in the Panama City metro.
Veronica shares ownership of MAPEI with Marco and her cousin Simona Giorgetta, who owns the largest stake in the company.
Together with her brother and her cousin, she also owns Italian soccer team Sassuolo Calcio, which Giorgio acquired in 2003.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joseph Baratta has served as Blackstone's global head of private equity since 2012.
He joined the alternative asset management giant in 1998 and moved to London in 2001 to help build the firm's European private equity business.
Baratta serves on the boards of a number of Blackstone portfolio companies including Ancestry.com, Medline and Merlin Entertainments Group.
Before joining Blackstone, Baratta worked for investment firms Tinicum Incorporated and McCown De Leeuw & Company and in the M&A department of Morgan Stanley.
He graduated magna cum laude from Georgetown University and is a former member of the school's Board of Trustees.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cao Ji chairs Zhejiang Hangke Technology, a supplier to the lithium battery industry.
Hangke went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
Cao has more than a 60% stake in Hangke with his son Cao Zheng, a company director.
Hangke is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kim Taek-jin is the founder and chairman of NCSoft, South Korea's No. 2 online game company which he founded in 1997.
He took the company public in 2003, and still serves as CEO. In 2024, Byungmoo Park joined Kim as co-CEO; Park was previously CEO of South Korean private equity firm VIG Partners.
NCSoft now provides online game services to more than 60 countries.
He sold most of his NCSoft shares in 2012 and now holds just under 12% of the company.
An avid sports fan, Kim founded the Korean professional baseball team NC Dinos in 2011.
abouts: While still a student at Seoul National University's College of Engineering, he developed software that helped users practice typing in Korean.
He worked for Hyundai Electronics' R&D Center in Boston and later became head of a division of Hyundai Electronics that launched South Korea's first Internet access.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Luc Tack is managing director of weaving machine and cast iron parts manufacturer Picanol Group. He joined the Belgian company in 2009.
He's now a controlling shareholder in Picanol, owning over 90% of the company.
Tack is also CEO and executive director of plastic and chemical manufacturer Tessenderlo Group, which reported over $2 billion in revenue in 2019.
Tack requested emancipation from his parents at 18 so that he could legally start his first business, an importer of American wood products.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Andrei Kuzyaev's fortune is derived from Luch Capital, an investment firm whose portfolio includes ER-Telecom, the third-largest broadband internet provider in Russia.
In 2022 Luch Capital rebranded from its former name Perm Financial and Industrial Group (PFIG), which Kuzyaev started in the 1990s.
PFIG had a 27% stake in Lukoil-Perm, a production unit of the oil giant, which Kuzyaev sold to Lukoil in 2003.
In 2022 PFIG was domiciled from Cyprus back to Russia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hary Tanoesoedibjo got his start building a media business soon after college; he still owns 62 TV stations, 4 radio stations and a newspaper.
He stepped down as CEO of his Media Nusantara Citra (MNC), which owns four national TV stations, in 2016 to focus on politics.
His listed MNC Land in 2023 opened the Lido Music & Arts Center in Jakarta as part of the Lido City project, which will feature Trump-branded golf course and resort.
MNC Land is also building another Trump-branded golf resort in Bali.
His daughter Angela, who used to serve as Indonesia's Deputy Tourism and Creative Economy Minister, became co-CEO of MNC Group in October 2024.
abouts: Hary, who attended Donald Trump's inauguration in 2017, is building a Trump Hotel luxury resort in Bali.
Hary is now actively involved in his political party Perindo, which he founded in 2014 after a brief run to be the country's vice president.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Maky Zanganeh is co-CEO of Summit Therapeutics, a biotech firm with a promising drug candidate to treat lung cancer. She owns just under 5% of the company's stock.
Zanganeh, an immigrant from Iran, previously served as chief operating officer of drug firm Pharmacyclics, which was acquired by AbbVie for $21 million in 2015.
Zanganeh first came to the U.S. to work for robotic surgery firm Computer Motion in 2002 after running the company's European operations.
Zanganeh runs Summit Therapeutics as co-CEO with Robert (Bob) Duggan, who became a billionaire after investing in and running Pharmacyclics. She and Duggan married in 2024.
She trained as a dentist at university in Strasbourg, France and then obtained an MBA while first working at Computer Motion.
abouts: Zanganeh, who attended high school in Germany and university in France, speaks Persian, German, French and English.
Zanganeh is a cancer survivor; she was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019 and has since recovered.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Qian is co-founder and vice chairman of Yadea Group, a maker of electric scooters and bicycles.
Her husband, Yadea co-founder and vice chairman Dong Jinggui, is also a billionaire.
Yadea went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2016.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mahaveer Prasad Taparia is the managing director of Mumbai-based plastics producer Supreme Industries.
Supreme is one of India's largest plastic processors, making everything from moulded furniture to composite gas cylinders.
The Mumbai-headquartered company also makes bathroom fittings and storage products in its 28 factories across India.
His older brother Bajranglal Taparia, the company's chairman, and his nephew Shivratan Taparia Supreme's executive director, also have stakes in the company.
Taparia also has a small stake in Supreme Petrochem, which produces polystyrene, used for construction and packaging.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Philippe Benacin cofounded French fragrance company Interparfums in 1982, along with Jean Madar.
The pair started the company out of business school after learning in class about the high margins of the fragrance industry.
They took the business public on the NASDAQ in 1988 at a $4 million valuation. It is now worth more than $3 billion.
Benacin became President of the company in 1994, and has been the CEO of Interpafums' European subsidiary since 2018.
Benacin oversees the company's European operations, which account for 65% of net sales.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kalpana Parekh is the daughter of Balvant Parekh, the late founder of Pidilite Industries.
She has a minority stake in Pidilite, which is India's leading  maker of adhesives and sealants.
Pidilite's range of products includes construction chemicals, art materials and organic pigments.
Her brother Madhukar Parekh is the chairman of the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Huang Jian is a former president of Midea Group, the biggest manufacturer of home appliances  in China.
Huang Jian departed Midea in 2013 when it competed a backdoor listing on the Shenzhen stock exchange.
Huang Jian still owned more than 1% of Midea Group in 2023.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Huxiong is the vice chairman and president of Shanghai M&G Stationary Inc.
M&G Stationary was founded in 1996.
Chen's brother Chen Huwen is M&G's chairman and a fellow billionaire.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Richard Barton is the cofounder and CEO of Zillow Group, an online real estate marketplace.
He and Lloyd Frink launched the business in 2004; Zillow went public seven years later.
A serial entrepreneur, Barton founded Expedia as a group inside Microsoft in 1994, which he led after it spun out. He also cofounded Glassdoor, the company review website.
Barton served as a partner at Silicon Valley venture capital firm Benchmark from 2005 to 2018.
He also sits on the boards of Netflix and Qurate Retail Group.
abouts: Prior to founding Zillow, Barton spent a year living in Italy.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chae has served as chief financial officer of alternative asset management giant Blackstone since 2015. He was named vice chairman in January 2025.
Chae joined Blackstone in 1997 and ran its international private equity business before being tapped to oversee the firm's finances.
Chae previously worked at alternative asset manager The Caryle Group and investment bank Dillon, Read & Co.
Chae is an alum of Harvard, Yale and Cambridge. He is a director of the Harvard Management Company and founder of the Chae Initiative in Private Sector Leadership at Yale Law School.
He is also a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liu Xiucai chairs Cathay Biotech, a Shanghai-headquartered supplier of industrial chemicals.
Cathay went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Qi Xiangdong chairs Qi An Xin Technology Group, which supplies cybersecurity products and services to government and businesses.
Qi An Xin listed on China's STAR Market in July 2020.
He founded the company in 2014.
Earlier, Qi cofounded 360 Security Technology with fellow China billionaire Zhou Hongyi.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cai Jianyong chairs China nickel supplier Lygend Resources & Technology, headquartered on the coast of the East China Sea.
He founded the company in 2009, after nearly a decade in the commodities trading business.
Lygend trades and produces nickel products, essential for stainless steel and electric vehicle batteries.
Lygend went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in November 2022, raising money to expand its operations in Indonesia, home to much of the world's nickel resources.
Cai graduated from the Shanghai Institute of Building Materials Industry.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hua Xuande chairs Zhejiang ZoneBanner Jiuzhou Group, which controls Shanghai-listed pharmaceutical supplier Zhejiang Jiuzhou Pharmaceutical.
Hua's daughter, Hua Lirong, chairs Zhejiang Jiuzhou Pharmaceutical.
In September 2019, Jiuzhou Pharmaceutical acquired U.S. pharmaceutical ingredient firm PharmAgra Labs for a reported $16 million.
In 2019 Jiuzhou also took over a Chinese subsidiary of Swiss pharmaceutical maker Novartis to help expand its production.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Quek Leng Chye is managing director of Hong Leong Holdings, a property development and investment arm of diversified conglomerate Hong Leong Group.
His brother, Malaysian billionaire Quek Leng Chan, is the executive chairman of Hong Leong Co. (Malaysia), which has interests in finance, food and property.
