His cousin, Kwek Leng Beng, serves as chairman of Hong Leong Group in Singapore and is also a billionaire.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Analjit Singh is the youngest son of Bhai Mohan Singh, founder of pharma firm Ranbaxy Laboratories.
Today he controls the $4.5 billion (revenue) Max Group, with interests in healthcare, insurance and specialty packaging film.
In recent years, Singh has invested in South Africa where he owns a vineyard and two boutique resorts.
His son, Veer, runs Vana, a private wellness retreat in the northern Indian city of Dehradun.
In February 2025 he settled a three-year-long dispute with estranged wife Neelu Singh, by buying out her 24.15% stake in family holding company Max Ventures.
abouts: The Boston University grad made an early investment in India's telecom sector and made a pile when he sold his stake in that business to Li Ka-shing.
His daughter founded Antara, a senior living community in North India.
In March 2022, his wife Neelu filed a lawsuit alleging mismanagement by her husband. Singh has refuted her allegations.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Per Franzén joined publicly traded Swedish investment company EQT AB in 2007.
Franzen owns about 3% of EQT, which has roughly $83 billion (73,4 billion Euro) in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
Franzen's partners at EQT include billionaires Conni Johnson, Harry Klagsburn and Lennart Blecher, and Christian SInding.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ryan Israel is the chief investment officer of Pershing Square Capital Management, the hedge fund founded by Bill Ackman in 2004.
Pershing Square has $16 billion in assets under management and was valued at $10.5 billion when outside investors bought 10% of the firm in June 2024.
A University of Pennsylvania graduate, Israel joined Pershing Square early in his career in 2009 following two years in investment banking at Goldman Sachs.
Ackman named Israel his CIO and eventual successor in 2022.
abouts: Israel was named to Forbes' 30 Under 30 list in the finance category in 2015.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: He Zhaoxi is the chairman of Sangfor Technologies, a supplier of IT infrastructure solutions.
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2018.
He graduated from China University of Science and Technology in 1998 with a degree in automatic control and economic management.
After graduating, He worked for Huawei Technologies from 1998 to 2000.
He cofounded Sangfor Technologies in 2000.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Soegiarto Adikoesoemo founded AKR Corporindo as a chemicals trader in 1960 and listed it on the Indonesian Stock Exchange in 1994.
AKR Corporindo is now engaged in petroleum trading and distribution, logistics services, chemical manufacturing and industrial estate.
AKR Corporindo and British oil and gas firm BP's joint venture distributes aviation fuel and  operates jointly branded service stations in Indonesia.
Soegiarto is AKR's president commissioner. His son Haryanto is president director.
In September 2024, AKR's East Java industrial estate JIIPE inaugurated the world's largest single line copper smelter by capacity, run by Indonesia-U.S. joint venture Freeport Indonesia.
abouts: His son Haryanto Adikoesoemo started collecting art over 25 years ago and has accumulated 800 pieces, including works by Andy Warhol and Mark Rothko.
Haryanto opened a museum dedicated entirely to modern and contemporary art, Museum MACAN, in November 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xu Wanmao chairs the Huamao Group, whose interests include education, real estate and investment.
Huamao Group is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Ningbo, where it ranks as one of the city's largest service industry businesses.
Huamao Group's investments include the Bank of Ningbo.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Konstantin Goncharov controls Novotrans, a closely held Russian railway, port and shipping business.
Goncharov bought Novotrans in 2015, when it was operating at a loss, and built it into a fleet of 25,000 railway cars and several wagon repair plants.
Prior to purchasing Novotrans, Goncahrov ran several logistics companies in the 2000s.
Novotrans is building a Lugaport marine terminal in the Baltic Sea with a capacity of over 24 million tons per year.
abouts: Goncharov's wife is reportedly the daughter of Rashit Sharipov, who lost the fight against Victor Rashnikov for control over the MMK in the 1990s.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chang Byung-gyu is the chairman of online gaming company Krafton (formerly known as Bluehole), which he founded in 2007.
In 2018, Tencent invested more than $500 million in the company for a 10% stake, catapulting Krafton to unicorn status overnight.
Its shooter game, PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds, broke a world record in 2017 after posting $100 million in pre-release sales in just 79 days.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Plastics tycoon Shivratan Taparia gets his wealth from a stake in BSE-listed flagship Supreme Industries.
Taparia has a board seat at Supreme Industries.
Supreme is one of India's largest plastic processors, making everything from moulded furniture to composite gas cylinders.
The Mumbai-headquartered company also makes bathroom fittings and storage products in its 28 factories across India.
Taparia also has a small stake in Supreme Petrochem, which produces polystyrene, used for construction and packaging.
abouts: His uncles Bajranglal Taparia and  Mahaveer Prasad Taparia also have valuable stakes in the Supreme group of companies.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: He is the second largest shareholder of Leshan Giantstar Farming & Husbandry, a supplier of leather products.
He stepped down as the company's chairman in August 2023.
He is also a director and the majority shareholder of Shanghai-listed chemicals supplier Sichuan Hebang Biotechnology.
He worked for a city government commercial bureau in Leshan, China from 1971 to 1993 and founded Hebang's predecessor company in 1993.
The company listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange on Dec. 18, 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michael McCain is the CEO of Maple Leaf Foods, a Canadian packaged meat company that made $3.1 billion in sales in 2019.
McCain's father, Wallace McCain, cofounded frozen food company McCain Foods with his brother Harrison in 1956.
The family bought a controlling stake in Maple Leaf Foods in 1995.
In January 2020, Michael McCain grabbed headlines for his scathing tweets about then-U.S. President Donald Trump and his foreign policy.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lee Ho-jin is a former chairman of Taekwang Industrial, a manufacturer that became synonymous with Korea's textile and petrochemical prowess.
He rose to chairman after his oldest brother, Lee Sik-jin, died. He has now stepped down and is reportedly struggling against liver cancer.
In 2011, he was sentenced to 54 months in prison for embezzling $128 million from the company but has been out on bail due to his illness.
In 2019, Lee was sentenced to three years in prison on charges of embezzlement and breach of trust. He was pardoned in 2023.
abouts: Lee is credited for diversifying the group into media and entertainment.
His mother sold clothes in a Busan market and provided the seed money to start Taekwang, which began as a textile company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xiu Laigui's privately owned Xiuzheng Pharmaceuticals is one of China's largest pharmaceutical firms.
Xiu worked as a policeman in China in the early 1990s.
Xiuzheng is located in Tonghua in northeastern China's Jilin province.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Group Co.

bios: Zhang Keqiang fortune arises from a stake in Poly Real Estate Group,  one of China's largest real estate developers.
He also owns a stake in Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Group, a potash producer.
Zhang holds an MBA degree from Murdoch University in Australia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Maria Grace Uy and her husband Dennis cofounded Converge ICT Solutions, one of the Philippines' largest operators of high-speed internet.
They took the company public in 2020, raising more than $500 million in what was one of the Philippines' largest IPOs in recent years.
Maria serves as the company's president, Dennis as its CEO. The couple remains majority owners of the company.
Converge ICT's fixed broadband services now reach more than 17 million across the Philippines.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Vijay Agarwal founded construction equipment maker Action Construction Equipment in 1995.
He is chairman and managing director of the company, which makes hydraulic mobile cranes, tower cranes, loaders, tractors and agri-harvesters.
The company sells construction equipment under the brand name Ace.
His wife Mona and son Sorab work with him and have board seats.
Action's list of clients includes the Tata Group, engineering giant Larsen & Toubro and billionaire Anand Mahindra's Mahindra group.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ryuji Arai started Bic Camera, the electronics and appliances retailing giant, in 1978.
The company posted over $6 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through August 2024.
Arai also owns stakes in temporary staffing firm Hit Communications Holdings and contact lens-maker Seed.
abouts: Bic Camera owns a majority stake in listed satellite TV network Nippon BS Broadcasting.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shin Dong-joo is the eldest son of Shin Kyuk-Ho, the late founder of Lotte Group, one of South Korea's largest conglomerates.
The retail heavyweight has interests ranging from food and beverage to chemicals, construction and professional baseball.
In 2015, he was dismissed from his executive positions in the group after a bitter feud with his brother Dong-Bin.
abouts: Lotte started as a confectionery manufacturer in Japan in 1948 and expanded into South Korea in 1967.
At the start of his career, he worked for Mitsubishi in Japan in 1978.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Anton Fedun is the son of Russian billionaire Leonid Fedun, whose fortune is derived from Lukoil, Russia's second-largest oil producer.
His father became one of the controlling shareholders of the company in the 1990s, during the murky privatization of state-owned businesses.
In 2018 his father transferred part of his ownership in Lukoil to him and his sister Ekaterina, a fellow billionaire.
He also owns luxury hotels in London: The Ampersand Hotel and Vintry & Mercer.
Fedun holds dual citizenship in Russia and the U.K., and resides in London.
abouts: His wife Alina Uspenskaya was a contestant in the country's beauty pageant Miss Russian Radio.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Andrey Krivenko is the founder of VkusVill, one of Russia's fastest- growing retailers with 1,600 grocery stores.
In 2012 Krivenko launched his first four VkusVill (Taste Town) stores to sell fresh products with short shelf life.
A former CFO of Agama, the large Russian distributor of fish and seafood, he opened his first store Izbenka to sell fresh dairy products in 2009.
VkusVill was slated to go public on the Nasdaq and the Moscow Stock Exchange in 2022 but it was cancelled amid Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
According to the IPO prospectus, Krivenko planned to donate 20% of his shares in VkusVill to eight key executives.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhang Xin and her husband Pan Shiyi co-founded real estate developer Soho China.
Soho China is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and develops office towers in Shanghai and Beijing.
Prior to founding Soho China, Zhang worked on Wall Street for Goldman Sachs and Travelers Group.
In June 2021, U.S. private equity giant Blackstone said it would buy the majority of Soho China for as much as $3.05 billion; the purchase wasn't completed.
In 2022, Pan and Zhang stepped down from their leadership roles as chairman and CEO "in order to focus on supporting the arts and philanthropic pursuits" but remain on the board.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Igor Yakovlev is the founder of Kari, a Russian retailer of shoes, accessories and household products, which he founded in 2012.
Kari boasts 1,200 locations across Russia, including Moscow, St. Petersburg, Novosibirsk, Krasnoyarsk and Yekaterinburg, among other cities.
He also has stake in Sulpak, a large consumer electronics retailer in Kazakhstan; the company makes up a small part of his fortune.
In 2008 Yakovlev bought a 50% stake in FC Anzhi Makhachkala, a professional soccer club in Russia. Three years later he sold it to fellow Russian billionaire Suleiman Kerimov.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stuart Miller is executive chairman and co-CEO of homebuilder Lennar Corporation.
His father, Leonard Miller, was an early investor who took Lennar public in 1971 and helped grow it into a giant.
Lennar has built more than 1 million homes across 26 states. It did $35 billion in fiscal 2024 revenue.
Miller started working on Lennar's lawn crew at age 12. He took over as CEO in 1997.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lee Joon-ho is a cofounder of South Korea's largest internet portal, Naver.
He is the chairman of NHN, which was Naver's online-games business until the two split in 2013.
Lee sold $225 million worth of Naver shares in 2014 and another $115 million worth in 2016.
NHN's businesses now span from online gaming and digital payments to e-commerce and cloud services.
abouts: He was an associate professor at Soongsil University,  a private Christian university in Seoul.
He is credited for developing the natural language search solution for Naver.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Yanqing inherited her fortune from her husband Chen Guangwei, who died in April 2017.
Chen Guangwei founded Weihai Guangwei Group in 1987; Wang is a company director.
The group owns 38% of Weihai Guangwei Composites, which listed on the Shenzhen exchange in September 2017.
Founded in 1992, Guangwei produces advanced composites and fibre fabric.
Son Chen Liang, 48, is chairman of the group and a director of the listed company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Jiangsu Wujiang China Eastern Silk Market
Jiangsu Wujiang China Eastern Silk Market

bios: Tang Jinkui is vice chairman of Shenghong Group, headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Suzhou.
Shenghong completed a backdoor listing of its chemical fiber business in Shanghai in 2018.
It subsequently changed the listed company's name from Jiangsu Wujiang China Eastern Silk Market to Jiangsu Eastern Shenghong.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wu Yonghua is a director and CEO of Anta Sports, one of the world's largest sportswear businesses.
Wu joined Anta in 2003 and has over 20 years of experience in sales and marketing.
Anta is headquartered in southern China's Fujian Province.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cai Mingtong chairs Fujian Torch Electron Technology, a supplier of ceramic capacitors.
The predecessor of Fujian Torch Electron Technology was a collective owned electronic component factory founded in Quanzhou in 1989.
Cai taught high school teacher and worked as a factory technician before he joined the predecessor of Torch.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alexander Rinke is cofounder and co-CEO of enterprise software startup Celonis.
The Munich-based company was valued by private investors at $13 billion in 2022. Rinke owns a 15% stake.
The company disputes Forbes' valuation, which accounts for the downturn in private markets since the company's last funding round.
Rinke's cofounders Bastian Nominacher and Martin Klenk are also billionaires. Nominacher is co-CEO and Klenk is CTO.
Celonis' cofounders launched the company in 2011 after graduating from Technical University of Munich.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Veteran investment banker, Nimesh Kampani, qualified as an accountant and joined his family's stockbroking business in 1972.
He broke away to start a separate investment bank with a cousin whom he eventually bought out.
Kampani listed his flagship, JM Financial, in 1992 and got investors such as IFC and later partnered with Morgan Stanley.
After a decade, they parted ways with Kampani buying out Morgan Stanley's stake.
On turning 70 in 2016, Kampani handed over charge to his son Vishal, though he remains non-executive chairman.
abouts: He has been the confidante of several business tycoons, even those who are arch rivals.
In 2009, Kampani spent nearly a year in exile to avoid being arrested when a company from whose board he had resigned in 1999, defaulted on loans.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kostyantin Zhevago, a member of Ukraine's parliament from 1998 to 2019, stepped down as the firm's CEO in late 2019 amid an investigation by Ukraine's state prosecutor office.

Zhevago was wanted for allegedly embezzling and money-laundering linked to the disappearance of $113 million from Finance & Credit, his former bank that went bankrupt. With the case pending since 2015, he claims it is political persecution.
He was detained in December 2022 at the French ski resort Courchevel at Ukraine's request and then released on bail. A French court ruled against extradition to Ukraine.
A Ukraine court has also ordered the seizure of his sares in iron pellet producer Ferrexpo, which account for roughly $400 million of his of fortune. He is fighting the charges.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yu De-Chao, also known as Michael Yu, is the chairman and CEO of Innovent Biologics, a China-headquartered biotech company.
Innovent went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Yu holds a PhD in molecular genetics from the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Yu had a postdoc position in pharmaceutical chemistry at the University of California San Francisco in 1993-1996.
Yu had a postdoc position in pharmaceutical chemistry at the University of California, San Francisco in 1993-1996.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jerry Seinfeld is the co-creator and star of the 1990s-era sitcom, "Seinfeld", which was broadcast on NBC for nine seasons and is now airing in syndication.
Seinfeld and co-creator Larry David reportedly earn 15% of the show's syndication revenue, which includes sales to local television stations and streaming platforms.
His fortune comes form his share of the syndication revenue the show generates, as well as income from touring, films and other projects.
Seinfeld's work outside of "Seinfeld" includes Netflix comedy specials, Comedians In Cars Getting Coffee, Bee Movie and Unfrosted, a film about the Pop Tart.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Weijian Shan is the chairman of PAG, an Asia-focused private equity firm with $50 billion in assets under management.
Before founding PAG's private equity business in 2010, he worked for 12 years at TPG Capital and was the U.S. private equity giant's top China dealmaker.
At TPG, Shan spearheaded the first purchase of a state-owned Chinese bank by a foreign investor.
In 2022, Shan became an independent director of Alibaba. He also served on the boards of Wilmar International, Bank of China (Hong Kong), Baosteel and Lenovo.
abouts: The Beijing-born grew up during the Cultural Revolution and labored in northern China's Gobi Desert.
His memoir, published in 2019, is called Out of the Gobi: My Story of China and America.
He earned a Ph.D. in business administration from UC Berkeley, where U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen was one of Shan's thesis advisors.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rajesh Sharma gets his wealth from a majority stake in non-banking finance company Capri Global Capital, which he runs.
Mumbai-based Capri offers home loans, construction loans as well as customized business loans for medium and small-scale enterprises.
It has more than 900 branches across India, with a substantial presence in northern and western India.
abouts:
Capri Global started as a construction finance company in 2011.

Capri Global forayed into housing finance in 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Oleg Misevra controls East Mining Company, a Russian thermal coal enterprise.
Misevra, who served the Internal Troops of USSR and Russia, became a top manager and minority partner of the MDM Group, A WHATKT in the early 2000s.
MDM was founded by Andrey Melnichenko and Sergey Popov, who both became billionaires buying industrial plants across Russia.
In 2002, Misevra was elected as president of the Siberian Coal Energy Company (SUEK), the largest Russian thermal coal producer.
He resigned as president of SUEK in 2004 and purchased the company's assets on Sakhalin Island.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Wang Shuifu chairs equipment manufacturer Xizi Clean Energy Equipment.
Xizi Clean Energy was previously known as Hangzhou Boiler Group; Hangzhou Boiler went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2011.

Wang Shuifu started his career selling agricultural machinery in 1970.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ricardo Villela Marino is a third-generation member of the Brazilian family behind Itau Unibanco, Latin America's largest private bank by assets.
He is the grandson of Eudoro Libânio Villela, who cofounded Itau in 1945 and later merged with Unibanco in 2008.
Villela Marino sits on the board of Itausa, the parent of Itau Unibanco, and also serves as an advisor to the bank.
His mother, Maria de Lourdes Egydio Villela, a former billionaire, transferred her shares of Itausa to Ricardo and his brother Rodolfo in 2015.
He owns about 4% of Itausa shares.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rodolfo Villela Marino and his brother Ricardo, each own a nearly 4% stake in Brazil's Itau Unibanco.
His grandfather Eudoro Libânio Villela cofounded Itau in 1945 in Sao Paulo.
In 2008, Itau merged with Unibanco to create the largest private sector bank (by assets) in Latin America.
Villela Marino sits on the board of Itausa, the parent of Itau Unibanco, and has served as executive vice president since 2022.
In 2015, his mother, Maria de Lourdes Egydio Villela, a former billionaire, transferred her stake in the bank to Villela and his brother Ricardo.
abouts: Villela has a degree in business and a doctorate in management from the Getúlio Vargas Foundation (FGV) in São Paulo.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sundar Pichai is CEO of Google parent Alphabet, a position he has held since 2019, when he was tapped to replace Google cofounder Larry Page.
Pichai has worked at Google since 2004, reportedly interviewing for the job the same day Google launched Gmail. He became Google's CEO in 2015.
He holds around 0.02% of Alphabet and has sold more than $500 million worth of shares, before taxes.
Born in Chennai, India, Pichai grew up with limited access to technology but was always interested in how it can create community.
He said that in 1993, his father spent a year's salary on a plane ticket to California so Sundar could attend Stanford.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Joe Agresti sells 20,000 Mercedes-Benzes a year through Dream Motor Group, the dealership chain he owns alongside legendary football coach Nick Saban.
Agresti grew up in working-class New Jersey, studied accounting at Rutgers on a partial wrestling scholarship, then did stints at Big Six firm Arthur Andersen and auto dealer giant Asbury Automotive.
At age 31, he used his $200,000 life savings, a mortgage against his parents' house and a $500,000 loan to invest in his first car dealership, Mercedes-Benz of Baton Rouge.
He met Saban through Mercedes in 2013. They now runs nine Merecedes, Infiniti and Ferrari dealership locations in Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, Tennessee and Texas.
He splits his time traveling between homes he keeps near all his dealerships.
Agresti oversees the day-to-day operations and owns majority stakes in the dealerships, though Saban is a full minority partner. The two speak upwards of three times a day.
abouts: Agresti has worked with Senator Bernie Moreno to help shape automotive policy and says he might one day run for federal office himself.
Agresti, Saban and their third partner, former Mercedes-Benz USA CEO Steve Cannon, own a fledgling Kentucky distillery, Slow Pass Bourbon.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ekaterina Fedun is the daughter of Russian billionaire Leonid Fedun, whose fortune stems from Russia's second-largest oil company.
Her father became a controlling shareholder of Lukoil during the 1990s when state-owned companies were being privatized.
In 2018 the elder Fedun transferred part of his stake to Ekaterina and her brother Anton, a fellow billionaire.
Ekaterina is not involved in the business; Anton manages a fund that owns Lukoil.
In 2014 she married the manager of the Spartak Moscow football club, which is owned by the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chang Pyung-soon is chairman of Kyowon Group, one of the biggest educational companies in Korea, which he founded in 1985.
With education and training centers in bucolic settings throughout South Korea, Kyowon provides training programs to some 43,000 Kyowon staff members.
He has diversified and the company now has interests in educational travel programs, leisure activities, hotels and health foods.
abouts: His Kyowon Group also provides "lifestyle" products, including water purifiers and Oriental herb-based cosmetics.
Chang started out as a salesman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rao Wei chairs Shenzhen New Industries Biomedical Engineering, a supplier of clinical laboratory instruments.
In 1997, at age 33 year, Rao joined New Industries Biomedical Engineering when it was a trading company with only a dozen people.
Shenzhen New Industries went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020, raising $192 million; the funds will be used for R&D and manufacturing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Shih-Chung is the chairman of Taiwan's AirTAC International Group, a maker of pneumatic equipment for the automotive, electronics, medical and other sectors.
He worked at a factory upon graduating high school, and set up the company in 1988.
AirTAC is headquartered in Taipei with a strong foothold in mainland China, where it has two manufacturing sites.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jin Xin chairs Dajin Heavy Industry, a supplier of offshore wind power equipment.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Simone Maag de Moura Cunha owns 3.5% of Swiss dental giant Straumann Group.
Her billionaire uncle Rudolf Maag is the company's second largest shareholder after her brother-in-law Thomas Straumann.
Rudolf Maag bought out Straumann's medical device division in 1990 and later took it public as Stratec Medical.
In 1999 he merged Stratec with Swiss medical device powerhouse Synthes and built up a 15% stake, which was later sold to Johnson & Johnson.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Yuri Shefler established the SPI Group, which produced and sold alcohol under 380 brands in 170 countries.
In 2021 Shefler divided his alcohol business into two companies Stoli Group (manufacturing vodka under Stoli brand) and Amber Beverage Group (manufacturing other spirits).
Its best known brand is Stolichnaya vodka, which Shefler bought from state-owned VVO Soyuzplodoimport for $285,000 in 1997.
Russia's Supreme Court ruled the sale illegal in 2001, banning Shefler from selling the vodka inside its borders.
In 2014, the Netherlands, Luxembourg and Belgium joined Russia in banning sales of Stolichnaya.
Amber Beverage Group owns Latvijas balzams, the largest producer of alcoholic beverages in the Baltics, and Amber Production Tequila (KAH Tequila, Rooster Rojo Tequila and Cenote).

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Grupo Posadas SAB de CV Class A
Internacional de Ceramica SA Class B

bios: Alfredo Harp Helú's fortune stems from Acciones y Valores de Mexico, also known as Accival, which he cofounded.
In 1991 Accival merged with Mexican bank Banamex to form Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival (Banacci). Harp Helú then became chairman of the group.
Citigroup acquired Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival for $12 billion in stock and cash in 2001, and Harp Helú joined Citigroup's board.
He has a minority stake in publicly-traded tile producer Internacional de Ceramica.
He owns two Mexican baseball teams, Los Diablos Rojos of Mexico City and Los Guerreros of Oaxaca.
abouts: A baseball enthusiast, he published an autobiography in 2003 titled, "To Live and Die Playing Baseball."
He was kidnapped in 1994 for 106 days and released, reportedly after a payment of $30 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sheila Johnson cofounded cable TV channel Black Entertainment Network in 1979 with her then-husband Robert. Viacom bought it for $3 billion in 2001.
After her divorce in 2002, she sold her BET shares and has since invested in a portfolio of hotels known as the Salamander Collection, as well as real estate and horses.
Her Innisbrook resort in Palm Harbor, Florida, hosts an annual PGA Tour championship.
She was an executive producer of the critically-acclaimed 2013 film The Butler, which tells the story of a former slave turned White House employee.
Through her investment in Monumental Sports & Entertainment, she owns stakes in the WNBA's Washington Mystics, NBA's Wizards and the NHL's Capitals.
abouts: Johnson is the only black woman to own stakes in three professional sports teams (WNBA Mystics, NBA Wizards and NHL Capitals).
Johnson's parents enrolled her in an all-white school in early 1950s Kentucky before desegregation was federally mandated.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Koo Bon-sik runs LG affiliate Heesung Electronics with his brother Koo Bon-neung, who is also one of the richest people in South Korea.
He is the youngest of the four Koo brothers of the LG Group.
Heesung is LG's largest supplier of backlights, which are used to illuminate LCD displays.
Heesung group's affiliates include LT Precision, LT metal and LT Material.
abouts: More than 50% of his fortune comes from his stake in LG Corp.
In 1947 his grandfather, the late Koo In-hwoi, cofounded LG, then called, Lak Hui Chemical Industrial Corp., with a popular face cream.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Yuantai is secretary of the party committee at Contemporary Amperex Technology.
Contemporary Amperex Technology, also known as CATL, is a battery supplier to the EV industry.
CATL is headquartered in the southeastern China city of Ningde.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michael Dunlap is the cofounder and executive chairman of Nelnet, a loan servicing and payment processing company based in Lincoln, Nebraska
He started the company in the late 1990s with Stephen Butterfield (d. 2018). The two took the company public in 2003.
Michael's son Matthew is the chief business development officer and serves on the board.
His nephew Jason Muhleisen is the president and CEO of Lincoln's Union Bank & Trust, owned by the Dunlap family.
A graduate of the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, Dunlap serves on the board of the Raikes School of Computer Science and Management.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Michael Lee-Chin made a fortune investing in financial companies like National Commercial Bank Jamaica and AIC Limited.
The native of Jamaica acquired AIC in 1987, when it had less than $1 million in assets under management.
Under Lee-Chin, the Canada-based wealth management and mutual fund business managed more than $10 billion in assets by 2002.
But the firm was hit hard by the 2008 recession, and Lee-Chin sold AIC to Canadian financial services group Manulife in 2009 for an undisclosed price.
He managed to hold onto a valuable 60% stake in National Commercial Bank Jamaica, which now makes up much of his wealth.
abouts: As a teenager, Lee-Chin worked landscaping at a hotel, then got a gig cleaning the engine room on the Jamaica Queen cruise ship.
Lee-Chin later worked as a road engineer for the Jamaican government after studying civil engineering at Canada's McMaster University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhong Sheng Jian is the chairman of Singapore-listed Yanlord Land, one of the largest non-government-owned real estate developers in China.
Zhong, a mainland native, moved to Singapore in 1988.
Yanlord's prominent China partners include Ping An Insurance, China Merchants Property Development and Poly Real Estate Group.
His son Zhong Ming is Yanlord's executive deputy chairman; younger son Zhong Lek Ka and nephew Zhong Siliang both sit on the board.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: W. Nicholas Howley cofounded TransDigm through a 1993 leveraged buyout in which he acquired four struggling aerospace units from his employer, IMO Industries.
The Cleveland-based aerospace parts manufacturer has grown into an $8 billion (sales) company through acquisitions of small companies that are the sole makers of particular components.
Howley has twice been called to testify before Congress over allegations the company has overcharged the Pentagon for spare parts.
His family foundation has provided scholarships to hundreds of low-income students, primarily to attend Catholic high schools in Cleveland and Philadelphia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chaitanya Desai is the managing director of the $1.9 billion (revenue) Mumbai-based Apar Industries.
The 66-year-old company manufactures conductors, electric cables, speciality oils, polymers and lubricants.
His older brother Kushal is chairman and managing director of Apar Industries.
Apar was originally called Power Cables when it was set up in 1958 by his late father Dharamsinh Desai.
abouts: His mother Maithili Desai hails from the Mafatlal family, an old textile clan.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kushal Desai is chairman and managing director of  the $1.9 billion (revenue) Mumbai-based Apar Industries.
The 66-year-old company manufactures and supplies conductors, electrical cables, speciality oils, polymers and lubricants.
His younger brother Chaitanya is Apar's managing director.
Apar was originally called Power Cables when it was set up in 1958 by his late father Dharamsinh Desai.
abouts: His mother Maithili Desai hails from the Mafatlal family, an old textile clan.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Morris Kahn cofounded Amdocs, a customer-relationship management-and-billing software firm for large telecom outfits.
He sold nearly $1 billion worth of shares after Admocs went public in 1998.
A South African native, he lives on the Israeli coast and spends much of his time on a 100-foot yacht.
Through his Aurum Ventures, Morris invests in life sciences and clean-tech companies that he hopes will contribute to the wellbeing of the planet.
He currently serves as the chairman of SpaceIL, which attempted to send the first Israeli spacecraft to the moon in 2019.
abouts: An avid diver, Kahn started building aquariums after a diving accident that gave him a burst eardrum, forcing him to stay on land for months.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dora Voigt de Assis is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG had revenues of approximately $6.7 billion in 2024.
Dora does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; she graduated from university with an architecture degree in 2020.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lívia Voigt de Assis is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
At twenty years old, she is the world's second-youngest billionaire, behind nineteen-year-old German pharmaceuticals heir Johannes von Baumbach.
WEG was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG had revenues of approximately $6.7 billion in 2024.
Lívia does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; she is currently attending university.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Real estate heiress Amy Goldman Fowler is one of four siblings who equally split ownership of Solil Management, which owns 400 properties.
Amy is the second-youngest daughter of late patriarch Sol Goldman. His trademark was all-cash deals whenever possible.
She worked in the real estate office when she was younger. Now her younger sister Jane runs it.
She lives on a 200-acre farm in Rhinebeck, New York and also has a home in Memphis.
Amy has a Ph.D. in clinical psychology and has won three American Horticultural Society book awards.
abouts: Her husband Dr. Cary Fowler helped start the climate change conscious Svalbard Global Seed Vault.
She is an author; her latest book was The Melon, published in 2019, with photographs and descriptions of 125 different melon varieties.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Grigory Berezkin derives his fortune from Rusenergosbyt, a Russian energy trading company.
In 2006, Berezkin sold nearly half of Rusenergosbyt to Italy's energy conglomerate Enel for $105 million.
He got his start in the energy business in the 2000s; and controlled companies that supplied electricity to state-owned corporations Gazprom, Russian Railways and Transneft.
During the privatization of Russia in the 1990s, Berezkin purchased a mid-size oil company, which he later sold to Russian oil conglomerate Lukoil for $619 million.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hotel tycoon Michael Kum runs a hospitality empire spanning 20 hotels across Asia and Europe through his privately held M&L Hospitality.
His eldest daughter Jocelyn helps him run the hotel group, which includes brands such as Hilton and Hyatt.
The son of street hawkers, Kum got into hotels in 2009 after selling his offshore barges business to Macquarie Group.
Kum's assets include a majority stake in Singapore shipping firm, Atlantic Navigation.
abouts: He cofounded Offshore Equipment in 1976, chartering vessels and barges to the oil and gas industry.
He also has a stake in Australian vessel operator, MMA Offshore.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Paul Lee is the chairman of Yunnan Energy New Material, a supplier of film and packaging products.
Clients include Panasonic, LG Chemical and Comtemporary Amperex Technology.
Yunnan Energy, also known as SEMCORP Advanced Materials Group, is building a $916 million lithium battery separator film plant in Ohio.
His brother Li Xiaohua is the vice chairman of Yunnan Energy New Material and is also a billionaire.
Lee holds a degree from the University of Massachusetts.
abouts: Lee's brother Li Xiaohua is a Chinese citizen whereas Lee is an American.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shin Chang-Jae is the chairman of Kyobo Life Insurance, founded by his father in 1958 as Daehan Kyoyuk Insurance.
When Shin became chairman and CEO in 2000, Kyobo was reeling from investment portfolio losses in the aftermath of the Asian financial crisis.
He turned the company around, focusing on customer satisfaction and risk control.
With a network of agents and financial planners, the company now offers insurance and asset-management products to more than 5 million customers.
abouts: He has a mischievous penchant for staging stunts to make a point, such as reportedly taking part in his own fake funeral.
In 2010, he received the 19th Montblanc de la Culture Arts Patronage Award for his support of Korean literature through the Daesan Foundation.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Hangzhou Songcheng Tourism Development Co., Ltd
Hangzhou Songcheng Tourism Development Co., Ltd

bios: Huang Qiaoling, one of China's most successful theme park entrepreneurs, chairs Songcheng Performance Development.
Huang businesses operate 30 theme parks and 10 resorts.
Huang served in the army from 1975-80, and his early career was in the arts.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Edouard Carmignac founded Carmignac Gestion, one of Europe's largest asset managers, in 1989.
Carmignac owns 79% of the company, which now has over $40 billion in assets under management; employees and executives own the rest.
His daughter Maxime works at the company and is the heir apparent. His son directs Foundation Carmignac and another daughter, Lucrece, is an actress.
In 2019, Carmignac stepped back from managing Carmignac Patrimoine, which he had run since 1989. He is chairman and chief investment officer.
The Foundation Carmignac opened an exhibition space in 2018 to show nearly 300 art works on Porquerolles, an island off the South of France.
abouts: Edouard Carmignac wanted to be a rock star but settled for finance after receiving a BA in economics from the University of Paris and an MBA from Columbia.
Carmignac is a keen polo player. His team reached the semi final of the prestigious Deauville Gold Cup in 2017.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kenji Kasahara founded social networking site Mixi in 2004; it went public in 2006.
In 2013 Mixi was losing customers and investors as competitors raced ahead.
Kasahara stepped down as CEO but stayed on as chairman.
He refocused the business on mobile gaming, e-commerce, dating and apartment hunting.
Mixi's popular Monster Strike game has been downloaded tens of millions of times.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sam Tarascio owns a portfolio of real estate across Melbourne, including a business park, two distribution sites, a large shopping mall and a market.
Tarascio, who emigrated from Italy in the 1950s, also owns several inner-city apartment developments.
He started out in property development in the 1960s by building a warehouse for German pharmaceutical company Hoechst, where he had worked in sales.
That led him to establish logistics and industrial-development business Salta Properties, now run by his son Sam.
abouts: Tarascio imported an olive press in 2014 for his Taralinga Estate on the Mornington Peninsula, near Melbourne.
His Taralinga Estate olive oil has won two gold medals at the New York International World Olive Oil Competition.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ma Yunsheng chairs Chambroad Holding, a supplier of petrochemicals, fine chemicals and agribusiness products.
Ma worked as a government official before he joined Chambroad in 1982 when it was a collective.
Chambroad strives for "progress to better serve the country and contribute to society," according to the company website.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Antonio Gallardo Ballart's father founded pharmaceutical company Almirall in 1943 in Barcelona.
When their father died in 1988, Antonio and his brother Jorge took over running Almirall.
The company listed its shares in Madrid in 2007; Antonio and his brother Jorge control the company.
Antonio Gallardo Ballart served as vice president and advisor until 2014, when he retired.
Members of the third generation of the Gallardo family now work at the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Zan Shengda chairs investment company Nantong Zongyi Investment. 
Zan investments over the years have ranged include financial services, spirits, dairy and software.
Zan holds an EMBA degree from Tsinghua University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Jilei is a director of express delivery firm ZTO Express.
He has served as its vice president of infrastructure management since October 2012.
From October 2009 to March 2012, Wang was a deputy general manager of Beijing ZTO Daying Logistics, a ZTO Express network partner.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: SHENZHEN KSTAR SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.

bios: Liu Chengyu chairs Shenzhen Kstar Science and Technology, a maker of uninterruptible power supply equipment, inverters and storage for the solar power industry.
KStar went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.
Kstar is headquartered in Shenzhen, China.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alexander Evnevich cofounded Orimi, Russia's largest Russian producer of tea and roasted coffee.
Orimi was founded in 1994 as the Orimi Trade company, which ran wholesale trade of flour, sugar and tea.
The company would become a major player in the Russian tea market, eventually launching its own tea packaging production.
During the 1980s and 1990s, Evnevich worked in Vedeneev VNIIG, the largest scientific center of designing, construction and operation of hydraulic power plants in Russia.
Evnevich's family also controls Maxidom, a large Russian DIY retailer that in 2020 acquired the Russian subsidiary of Castorama, part of British company Kingfisher.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Mingwang is the co-founder of China electronics maker Sunwoda, a supplier of lithium-ion battery modules.
Wang Wei, his brother and co-founder, chairs the Shenzhen-headquartered company.
Sunwoda's customers include Apple and Huawei.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Tatiana Volodina's fortune is derived from L'Etoile, a well-known perfume and cosmetics retail chain with 1,000 locations in 250 cities across Russia.
Volodina owns L'Etoile through Alkor, a holding company in which she has a controlling stake.
Alkor also owns Podruzhka, a smaller cosmetics chain.
L'Etoile and Podruzhka ( also know as "Girlfriend") saw combined sales of over $1 billion.
After earning a degree in economic cybernetics, Volodina worked for Shiseido and Estée Lauder Companies and helped build their businesses in Russia.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zeng Chaolin chairs Shenzhen-listed Tianshan Aluminum Group, a Chinese supplier of aluminum products.
Tianshan's shares trade at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; it's headquartered in Xinjiang.
Shimge Pump Industry Group acquired Tianshan Aluminum Group in 2020 in a backdoor listing and changed its own name to Tianshan Aluminum Group.
Brother Zeng Chaolin's brother Zeng Chaoyi is a director of the listed company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: David Kabiller is cofounder of AQR, a money management firm that trades assets through a systematic, research-driven approach.
The firm focuses on factor-based investing and has $120 billion of assets under management.
Based in Greenwich, Connecticut, AQR operates globally with offices from London to Sydney and Hong Kong.
Before AQR, he was a vice president at Goldman Sachs, working with chief investment officers of large pension and endowment funds in North America.
abouts: Kabiller founded the Kabiller Prize and the Kabiller Young Investigator Award for researchers in nanoscience and nanomedicine at Northwestern University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bangladesh-born Muhammed Aziz Khan, who resides in Singapore, is the chairman of Summit Group.
Summit Group has interests in power, ports, fiber optics and real estate, all in Bangladesh.
Japan's JERA has a 22% stake in Summit Power International, which owns a portfolio of infrastructure assets in Bangladesh.
His daughter, Ayesha, runs Summit Power International.
abouts: Khan is the son of an army officer, who got into construction.
Khan started Summit as a trading firm but went on to focus on infrastructure.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: William Fung and his older brother Victor own a significant stake in Li & Fung, which operates as a middleman between global manufacturers and retailers in the U.S. and Europe.
William stepped down as chairman of Li & Fung in 2020 when Victor's son, Spencer, took the helm.
In 2020 Li & Fung was privatized through a deal worth $930 million.
In 2022, Danish shipping giant A.P. Moller-Maersk acquired the brothers' logistics business, LF Logistics, for $3.4 billion.
Their grandfather, Fung Pak-liu, founded Li & Fung with partner Li To-ming in 1906, exporting porcelain and silk.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hans Langer is the world's first 3-D printing billionaire.
Langer founded EOS, one of the earliest and most successful 3-D printing companies, more than 30 years ago.
Daughter Marie Langer took over as CEO of the largest operating business, EOS GmbH, which makes 3D printers for polymers and metals, in October 2019.
While others focused on consumers and 3-D printing, Langer always believed that the technology's true value was in industrial applications.
Venture capital firms have plowed funds into American 3D printing startups, but the Langer family has turned down investments and sales offers.
abouts: Langer's first customer was BMW, which bet on EOS before it even had a product available.
He has turned down multiple, multi-billion-dollar acquisition offers, insistent that the business stay in the family so that he can run it as he wishes.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zong Yanmin chairs SICC, a supplier of silicon-carbon semiconductor materials.
Founded in 2010, SICC is headquartered in the eastern China city of Jinan.
SICC went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2022.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Luigi Cremonini supplies hamburger meat to McDonald's and Burger King in Italy and other countries through his privately-held Inalca SpA.
Born to poor farmers in an Italian village near Modena, Cremonini got his start by opening a small butcher shop in 1963.
Beginning in the late 1970s he diversified into cured meats, distribution and catering and within a decade expanded the business internationally.
Today Cremonini Group employs more than 19,500 workers all over the globe and generated $5.6 billion in revenues in 2022.
Its catering arm Chef Express sells food on trains in Europe, Turkey and Russia, including the Eurostar service between London and Paris.
abouts: In 1994 the University of Bologna awarded Cremonini an honorary degree in Veterinary Medicine.
An art lover, Cremonini has a vast collection of paintings and contributed to the restoration of an archaeological area near the Trevi fountain in Rome.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Rui is the CEO of Bilibili, a Shanghai-headquartered online media company
Chen previously cofounded New York-listed Cheetah Mobile, a software firm.
Chen is a graduate of the Chengdu University of Information Technology.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Husnu Ozyegin's Fiba Holding comprises investments in financial services while non-finance activities are under the roof of Fina Holding.
His Credit Europe Bank has more than $5.5 billion in assets and around 915,000 retail and corporate customers in nine countries.
In Turkey, Ozyegin operates under the brand name Fibabanka. Fiba has investments in retail, real estate, health, renewable energy, ports and hotels.
In 2019, Ozyegin handed the reins of Fiba Holding to his children. Son Murat Ozyegin became chairman and daughter Aysecan Ozyegin Oktay, vice-chair.
Husnu Ozyegin became honorary chairman of the group. He also serves as chairman of Fibabanka and Credit Europe Bank (Russia) Ltd.
abouts: While studying civil engineering at Oregon State University, Ozyegin delivered newspapers and worked as a waiter, among other jobs. He received his MBA from Harvard.
He devotes considerable time to Ozyegin University, which he founded in 2007. In 2017, his life story was published as a book titled "Building a World."

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mark Miller is the chief operating officer of Canadian tech company Constellation Software.
Constellation Software, also known as CSI, acquires, manages and builds software businesses.
Trapeze, a transit software company Miller cofounded, was Constellation's first acquisition, in 1995.
Today he runs Volaris Group, an operating group within Constellation that has bought and held more than 200 tech companies in 50 countries, ranging from agri-food to rental management to utilities.
Miller owns around 1% of Constellation's stock, plus shares of spin-outs Topicus.com and Lumine Group.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chen Wenyuan chairs HYC Technology, a supplier of testing equipment for LCD, semiconductor and new energy electronics businesses.
HYC listed on China's new STAR market for innovative companies on the Shanghai Stock Exchange on July 22, 2019
His wife Zhang Qian cofounded the predecessor business of HYC in 2005.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Tang Ye chairs Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology, a supplier of laser-related software and hardware.
Friendess went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
Tang holds a master's degree in engineering management from China's prestigious Shanghai Jiaotong University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alexander Samwer and his brothers Oliver and Marc founded Berlin-based tech incubator Rocket Internet in 2007 and took it public in October 2014.
The youngest of the brothers, Alexander does not take part in day-to-day management of the company, leaving that to Oliver.
Together, the brothers own around 50% of Rocket. In October 2020, the company delisted from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and is now private.
Inspired by the dot-com boom, the brothers created a German auction site, Alando, in 1999 and sold it to eBay for $43 million after a few months
That was followed by the creation of mobile phone content provider Jamba!, which was sold to Verisign in 2004 for $273 million.
abouts: Alexander is on the board of directors of Zalando, a German e-commerce company founded by Rocket Internet and modeled after Zappos in the U.S.
He graduated from Oxford University and earned an MBA from Harvard University.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Marc Samwer and his brothers Alexander and Oliver founded Berlin-based tech incubator Rocket Internet in 2007 and took it public in October 2014.
Together, they own around 44% of Rocket. The company was valued at more than $8 billion at the time of its IPO.
Inspired by the dot-com boom, the Samwers created a German auction site, Alando, in 1999 and sold it to eBay for $43 million after a few months.
That was followed by the creation of mobile phone content provider Jamba!, which was sold to Verisign in 2004 for $273 million.
abouts: Marc studied law at the University of Cologne.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Orion Hindawi cofounded cybersecurity firm Tanium with his father David in 2007; private investors valued the firm at $9 billion in June 2020.
In February 2016, Orion took over as CEO of Tanium from his father, who serves as executive chairman.
The father-son team previously worked together on BigFix, an IT software patching system that they sold to IBM for $400 million in 2010.
Orion's father David was born in Baghdad, grew up in Israel, and went to UC Berkeley to earn a Ph.D.
Orion also ended up at UC Berkeley in 1997, but dropped out before graduating to work with his father.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Satya Nadella joined Microsoft in 1992 and rose to CEO in 2014, when his billionaire predecessor, Steve Ballmer, retired that year.
Nadella was named chairman in 2021, replacing veteran tech exec and investor John Thompson, who had assumed the role from Microsoft's billionaire cofounder Bill Gates in 2014.
As CEO, Nadella has built Microsoft Azure into a leading cloud computing platform and overseen the acquisitions of LinkedIn for $26 billion in 2016 and Activision Blizzard for $69 billion 2023.
He has also made Microsoft a major player in the AI boom, investing more than $10 billion in OpenAI since 2019 and leading the development of Microsoft's own suite of AI-powered tools called CoPilot.
He owns just 0.01% of the more than $3 trillion (market cap) company's stock, but that's just enough to make him a billionaire, when combined with his more than $600 million in (pretax) share sales.
A native of India, Nadella came to the U.S. as a student, earning a master's in computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and an MBA from the University of Chicago.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: John Liew is co-founder of AQR, a money management firm that trades through a systematic, data-driven approach.
The firm focuses on factor-based investing and has $120 billion of assets under management.
Based in Greenwich, Connecticut, AQR operates globally with offices from London to Sydney and Hong Kong.
Before cofounding AQR, Liew worked at Goldman Sachs as a portfolio manager, where he developed and managed quantitative trading strategies.
He created the Liew College Fellows Fund to finance undergraduates who have unpaid research opportunities with the University of Chicago's faculty.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Vivek Ramaswamy is a biotech entrepreneur, author and Republican politician who ran for president in 2024.
A Harvard and Yale Law graduate, Ramaswamy began his career on Wall Street trading biotech stocks for the hedge fund QVT.
In 2015, he took public a speculative Alzheimer's drug (which later failed) in a $3 billion IPO that formed the basis of Roivant Sciences, a drug discovery and investment firm.
Ramaswamy left Roivant in 2020 to write Woke, Inc., a best seller, and found Strive, an asset manager that provides anti-woke investment funds.
Ramaswamy helped Elon Musk found DOGE as its co-head, but departed after a few weeks amid reports of butting heads with Musk.
abouts: Ramaswamy graduated as valedictorian from St. Xavier High School in Cincinnati, Ohio.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Jiangxi Special Electric Motor Co. L

bios: Chen Baohua is general manager of Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceutical, a pharmaceuticals supplier.
Chen holds a degree in chemical analysis from the Zhejiang University of Technology.
After graduation, he worked at a state-run pharmaceuticals factory.
In 1989, Chen quit and cofounded the predecessor of Huahai in the eastern Chinese city of Linhaiat with less than $3,000; he was only 29 years old.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Real estate heiress Diane Kemper is one of four Goldman siblings who co-own Solil Management, which owns at least 400 properties in New York City.
Trophies include retail and office space along Madison Avenue in midtown and high-end coops on the Upper East Side.
Diane is the second-oldest child of late patriarch Sol Goldman, who started buying up foreclosed properties for bargain prices in the 1950s.
Diane headed the residential leasing department for several decades. She scaled back due to health issues several years ago.
The family also owns a 17% stake in the World Trade Center developments in lower Manhattan.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hedda im Brahm-Droege and her husband Walter Droege founded Droege Group in 1988. It is one of the world's largest advisory and investment practices.
Droege Group has a hybrid business model, providing expertise to consulting clients and making "buy-and-build" investments, which is now its focus.
By providing capital, management resources and "value-add" know-how, it follows an "Entrepreneurship-as-a-Service" principle in engaging with clients.
In 2018, Ernest-W. Droege, the couple's eldest son, joined the management board and succeeded his father as CEO.
Droege Group is active in 30 countries and generates around $12 billion in annual revenue.
abouts: Hedda owns 22% of the company and is vice-chairwoman of the supervisory board. Walter, who remains on the board of directors, owns the rest.
They're avid collectors of contemporary art and exhibit pieces by world-renowned artists like Gerhard Richter in their offices.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Junjin chairs Juneyao Group, which controls Shanghai-listed Juneyao Airlines.
Wang Junjin co-foundered Juneyao Airlines with brothers Wang Junhao and Wang Junyao; the latter died in 2004.
Wang Junjin holds an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Abigail Bennett's grandfather, Marvin Sands, founded a humble wine business in 1945 at age 21.
That small operation has mushroomed into a publicly-traded behemoth now called Constellation Brands, which generates nearly $10 billion in annual revenue.
The company is known for its relentless streak of acquisitions. Subsidiaries include Robert Mondavi wine and Svedka Vodka.
Constellation also holds the rights to Grupo Modelo's U.S. beer business, including its Modelo and Corona labels.
Bennett's uncles, Robert and Richard Sands, are former executives and current board members. Her brother, Zachary Stern, is also a billionaire.
The family received $1.5 billion (pre-tax) of cash to convert its enhanced voting shares to ordinary shares in 2022.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Diamantis Diamantides owns Greek shipping firms Delta Tankers and Marmaras Navigation.
He founded Marmaras Navigation in 1976 and started Delta Tankers in 2006. Together, the firms own 56 tankers and bulk carriers.
His son Paschalis founded his own firm, Velos, in 2019. Velos owns 12 tankers and dry cargo ships.
Diamantides also owns large land holdings in the Astir peninsula, a wealthy enclave south of Athens on the Aegean coast.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Victor Fung and his younger brother William own a significant stake in Li & Fung, which operates as a middleman between global manufacturers and retailers in the U.S. and Europe.
Victor chaired Li & Fung until William took over in 2012. Victor's son, Spencer, became executive chairman in 2020.
In 2020 Li & Fung was privatized through a deal worth $930 million.
In 2022, Danish shipping giant A.P. Moller-Maersk acquired the brothers' logistics business, LF Logistics, for $3.4 billion.
Their grandfather, Fung Pak-liu, founded Li & Fung with partner Li To-ming in 1906 by exporting porcelain and silk.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kurt Krieger purchased Hoeffner Group in 1967 and turned it into one of Germany's  leading furniture retailers.
After the fall of the Berlin wall in 1989, he seized the opportunity to tap into new markets in eastern Germany.
Besides Hoeffner Group, Krieger owns real estate in his hometown Berlin, having acquired almost 100 acres in 2010.
He's planning a development project with schools, shopping centers and, of course, a furniture store in the northern part of the city.
abouts: In his youth, Krieger wanted to become a musician. He still plays the piano today.
He flies his own helicopter and often uses this means of transportation to get to business meetings.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Chang Kuo-Cheng is the third son of shipping tycoon Chang Yung Fa, who died in 2016 at the age of 88.
In 1968 Yung Fa founded Evergreen Marine, now one of the world's largest transportation companies.
Brothers Kuo-Hua, Kuo-Ming and Kuo-Cheng also inherited stakes in EVA Airways and hotels in Taiwan, mainland China, Paris and Bangkok.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ramesh Genomal gets his wealth from a minority stake in apparel maker Page Industries.
Page is one of the biggest licensees in the world for underwear maker Jockey.
He cofounded Page Industries with his younger brother Sunder with the aim of bringing Jockey to India.
The Genomal family has been the sole licensee of Jockey in the Philippines for over 65 years.
Elder brother Nari Genomal died in August

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sunder Genomal runs Page Industries, one of the biggest licensees in the world for underwear maker Jockey.
The Bangalore-headquartered Page Industries is also the exclusive Indian licensee of swimwear brand Speedo.
Genomal set up Page Industries in 1994 with the aim of bringing Jockey to India.
His son Shamir is the company's deputy managing director.
While Sunder is a U.K. citizen, his brother  Ramesh, who is also a billionaire, is a citizen of Cyprus.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Eczacibasi Ilac Sanayi ve Finansal Yatirimlar Sanayi

bios: Faruk Eczacibasi and brother Bulent are partners in a conglomerate that has 25 production facilities in Turkey and 16 abroad.
It is a global exporter of ceramic and wall tiles, plus bathroom fixtures and accessories (brands include VitrA, Villeroy & Boch and Engers Keramik).
Faruk and Bulent's father, Dr. Nejat F. Eczacibasi, focused on pharmaceuticals before expanding into personal health care and other businesses.
Eczacibasi Holding also operate in healthcare services and the production and distribution of medical products to hospitals.
Other key sectors are consumer products, finance, IT, mining and real estate development. Eczacibasi is Turkey's leading producer of toilet paper.
abouts: Faruk has an extensive modern art collection (assembled with his wife, Fusun), loves jazz and lives in Istanbul's historic peninsula of Galata.
He is president of the Eczacibasi Sports Club, whose women's volleyball team won the Women's Club World Championship in 2015 and 2016.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shay Banon is a cofounder and the former CEO of search engine company Elastic, which is based in Mountain View, California.
In January 2022, Banon stepped down as CEO. He is now serving as Chief Technology Officer of Elastic.
Banon helped to develop the search technology that Elastic uses and became CEO of the company in 2017.
An Israeli citizen, Banon received his B.Sc. in Computer Science from Technion, Israel Institute of Technology.
His fortune derives from his nearly 8% stake in the company, which went public in October 2018.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jiang Long is vice chairman and president of Goertek Inc., a maker of electronic components; Goerek's customers include Apple.
Jiang, who joined Goertek in 2004, holds a doctorate from the University of Maryland.
Brother Jiang Bin, who founded Goertek in 2001, chairs the company.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jeffrey Soffer is one of seven children of Donald Soffer, who developed the Florida city of Aventura.
Alongside his sister Jackie, Soffer helmed the family real estate firm, Turnberry Associates, for over two decades.
In 2019, Soffer set out on his own, bringing his interests under new company Fontainebleau Development.
Soffer's real estate holdings include the historic Fontainebleau Miami Beach luxury hotel.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

person.name: Candido Pinheiro Koren de Lima & family

personsLists.personName: Candido Pinheiro Koren de Lima & family
bios: Pinheiro Koren de Lima, an oncologist, used money he saved from his medical practice to launch a hospital in the Brazilian city of Fortaleza in 1986.
Over the years, he added more hospitals, then health clinics and eventually health insurance, creating what is now known as Grupo Hapvida.
He took Hapvida public in April 2018 on the Sao Paulo stock exchange; his fortune now includes stakes held by his wife and his two sons.
He is Hapvida's chairman; his son Jorge is the statutory chief executive officer, while his other son Candido Junior is a member of the board of directors.
The company has 25 hospitals and operates in over 15 Brazilian states.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liu Ming Chung leads Nine Dragons Paper, one of Asia's largest paper producers.
Hong Kong-listed Nine Dragons started out as a supplier of packaging for exporters in China, and now also benefits from consumer demand inside China.
Liu is CEO and deputy chairman of Nine Dragons, while his wife Cheung Yan, also a billionaire, is the chairlady. They are both cofounders of the company, which was established in 1995.
Liu was born in Taiwan and grew up in Brazil. He holds a bachelor's degree in dental surgery from the University of Santo Amaro, in Brazil.
His son Ken Liu joined Nine Dragons' board of directors in 2018, after graduating from Harvard University and working as a consultant for PwC.
abouts: His wife Cheung has been dubbed by Chinese media as the country's "wastepaper queen." Liu and Cheung met in Hong Kong and married in the US.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hong Seok-joh heads BGF Retail, one of Korea's largest convenience store companies.
Operating under the brand name CU, BGF boasts more than 17,000 stores.
His sister, Hong Ra-hee, is the widow of the late Samsung Group chairman Lee Kun-hee.
Prior to his start in the business, Hong was a prosecutor.
abouts: The business got its start in 1989 via a franchise-licensing agreement between the Hong family's Bokwang Group and Japanese convenience store operator FamilyMart.
His late father was the chairman of JoongAng Ilbo, one of South Korea's largest newspapers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wu Kaiting is the chairman of Xiamen Intretech Inc., a supplier of electronics products including remote controls for home entertainment equipment.
Intretech went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Jan. 15, 2018.
Wu owns a 55% stake in Intretech.
Wu is the son of Wanlida Group founder Wu Huitian, a member of the Forbes China Rich list in 2008; Wu died in 2012.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios:
Ric Elias is the cofounder and CEO of Red Ventures, the digital media company that owns brands like CNET, Lonely Planet, Best Colleges and The Points Guy. 
He started Red Ventures with friend Dan Feldstein in 2000 and grew it by buying up specialized websites. 
It bought personal finance site Bankrate for $1.4 billion in 2017 and paid $500 million for product reviewer CNET in 2020. 
A Puerto Rico native, Elias has started multiple foundations, including Golden Door Scholars, which provides scholarships to undocumented students.
abouts: Elias was one of the 155 passenger on the infamous "Miracle on the Hudson" flight in 2009.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jean Madar cofounded French fragrance company Interparfums in 1982, along with Philippe Benacin.
The pair started the company out of business school after learning in class about the high margins of the fragrance industry.
They took the business public on the NASDAQ in 1988 at a $4 million valuation. It is now worth more than $3 billion.
Madar served as President of the company until 1993, when he became Director General of Interparfums' European subsidiary. He became CEO in 1997.
Madar oversees Interparfums' U.S. operations, which account for 35% of net sales.
abouts: Madar never wears fragrances himself, as a way to keep his smelling palate clear.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lu Hongyan chairs Shanghai-listed online games company G-bits Network Technology.
Its business benefited during the pandemic, when quarantined Chinese people turned to online gaming for fun.
Lu worked for telecom firms ZTE and Salira Optical Network Systems as a software engineer before he founded G-bits in 2004.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Antonio Luiz Seabra founded Natura Cosmeticos in 1969 as Brazil's answer to Avon and built it into Brazil's largest beauty company.
Some 1.4 million "consultants" (mainly women) sell Natura products door-to-door across Brazil, six other Latin American countries and France.
Natura Cosmeticos, which went public in 2004, bought U.K. cosmetics chain The Body Shop from L'Oréal in 2017 for over $1 billion.
Seabra is co-chairman of the board of Natura and also owns Bresco, a Brazilian property-rental operation focused on warehouses, offices and hotels.
Media-shy Seabra reportedly owns an apartment on the banks of the river Seine in Paris as well as real estate in London.
abouts: Seabra communicates directly to employees through motivational videos. He is known for quoting poetry and philosophy in business meetings.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Ke Guihua chairs Shanghai-listed Keboda Technology, a supplier of electronic components for the auto industry.
Keboda's customers include Porsche, Bentley, Lamborghini, BMW and Audi.
Ke is originally from the eastern China city of Wenzhou.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Dou Zhenggang chairs Hangzhou Jinjiang Group, a company whose businesses include environmental protection and energy.
Other Jinjiang businesses span trade, logistics and non-ferrous metals.
Dou made his early fortune in textiles, starting his first business in 1983 in Zhejiang Province.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zachary Stern's grandfather, Marvin Sands, founded a humble wine business in 1945 at age 21.
That small operation has mushroomed into a publicly-traded behemoth now called Constellation Brands, which generates nearly $10 billion in annual revenue.
The company is known for its relentless streak of acquisitions. Subsidiaries include Robert Mondavi wine and Svedka Vodka.
Constellation also holds the rights to Grupo Modelo's U.S. beer business, including its Modelo and Corona labels.
Stern's uncles, Robert and Richard Sands, are former executives and current board members. His sister, Abigail Bennett, is also a billionaire.
The family received $1.5 billion (pre-tax) of cash to convert its enhanced voting shares to ordinary shares in 2022.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Larry Silverstein is the chairman and founder of Silverstein Properties, a New York-based real estate development firm.
Silverstein Partners owns nearly 16 million square feet of office, residential and retail properties in the U.S., including 7 World Trade Center in Manhattan.
Silverstein signed a 99-year lease on the World Trade Center towers for $3.2 billion in July 2001, seven weeks before the 9/11 attacks.
Silverstein Properties and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey ultimately received a $4.55 billion insurance payout and built new towers on the site.
The firm developed the 7, 2 and 3 World Trade Center office towers. A fourth building, 5 World Trade Center, will be a residential high-rise when it's complete.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Harshil Mathur cofounded financial services firm Razorpay, which operates India's largest payment gateway by transaction volumes.
Marquee investors include private equity players Peak XV Partners ( formerly Sequoia Capital India), Tiger Global Management, and startup fund Y Combinator.
Razorpay was last valued at $7.5 billion after raising more than $700 million over multiple funding rounds.

It has acquired eight businesses to date including a payroll management outfit and a 
fraud detection platform.
It caters to the startup space serving 86 of the top 100 unicorns in India
abouts: He has a B.Tech from IIT Roorkee
While at IIT Roorkee, he co-founded SDSLabs along with Razopay cofounder Shashank Kumar to encourage innovation through coding and software development.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shashank Kumar cofounded financial services firm Razorpay, which operates India's largest payment gateway by number of transactions processed.
Privately held Razorpay was last valued at $7.5 billion after raising more than $700 million over multiple funding rounds.
Marquee investors include private equity players such as Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India) and Tiger Global Management, and startup fund Y Combinator.
Credit card giant Mastercard also holds a stake.
It caters to the startup space serving 86 of the top 100 unicorns in India.
abouts: It has acquired eight businesses to date including a payroll management outfit and a fraud detection platform.
He has a B. Tech degree from India's elite Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Cai Hongbin's fortune comes from his stake in Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine.
Jiangsu Hengrui is one of China's largest pharmaceutical companies, employing more than 20,000 people.
Fellow Chinese billionaire Sun Piaoyang is Hengrui's chairman.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bruce Mathieson operates his poker machine and pub empire Australian Liquor and Hospitality in a joint venture with supermarket giant Woolworths.
Mathieson is now a minority shareholder in the listed Endeavour Group, which holds both the Australian Liquor assets and Woolworth's extensive liquor retailing business.
In a board shakeup in 2024, Endeavour's chairman resigned as well as Mathieson's son, Bruce Mathieson Jr., who had a board seat.
He has a fondness for racehorses and part-owned a horse that ran in the Melbourne Cup.
He is battling a rare form of blood cancer.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Steve Ells helped pioneer fast-casual dining as the founder of Chipotle.
After studying at the Culinary Institute of America, Ells opened the first Chipotle in Denver, Colorado in 1993.
He hoped to use the profits to fund a fine dining restaurant, but Chipotle was so successful he ended up expanding to a second store in 1995 and a third in 1996.
Today, Chipotle sells $11.3 billion worth of burritos, bowls and salads each year across 3,700 stores around the world.
Ells stepped down as CEO in 2018 and as executive chairman in 2020.
He opened a new restaurant concept, a robot-manned "restaurant of the future" named Kernel, in New York City in 2024.
abouts: Ells sold big chunks of Chipotle to McDonald's beginning in 1998 to help the brand expand. By the time Chipotle went public in 2006, he owned less than 4%.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lim Wee Chai started Top Glove with his wife Tong Siew Bee in 1991 and took the company public in 2001.
Top Glove is one of the world's largest producers of rubber gloves. It has 48 factories with an annual capacity of 95 billion gloves.
Lim, whose parents are rubber plantation owners and traders, also holds a stake in property developer Tropicana.
In March 2022, Lim postponed plans for a Hong Kong listing amid a sharp drop in profits.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rihanna, Barbados' most famous export, is a billionaire thanks to the success of cosmetics line Fenty Beauty.
The cosmetics company, which she co-owns with French luxury retailer LVMH, doubled its revenue in 2022.
She also has an estimated 28% stake in the Savage x Fenty lingerie line, which raised $125 million in a funding round in January 2022.
The pop star headlined the Super Bowl LVII halftime show for the first time in 2023, during which she revealed she was pregnant with her second child.
Rihanna and rapper A$AP Rocky have two children together, the first born in May 2022 and the second in August 2023.
As of February 2025, she was reportedly working on her ninth album, set to be her first since Anti was released in 2016.
abouts: Fenty is Rihanna's last name.
Rihanna was discovered by Jay-Z as a teenager.
