personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Don Ahern, a construction equipment tycoon, made his fortune helping build skyscrapers in Las Vegas and other U.S. cities.
In 1978, after graduating high school, he launched Los Arcos Equipment, which began with a fleet of eight scissor lifts.
He purchased his dad's company, Ahern's Trailer and Equipment Rental, in 1990, and later merged Los Arcos into the family firm.
He sold the business in 2022 to United Rentals for $2 billion, pocketing an estimated $600 million after taxes and paying off debts.
Ahern still owns construction equipment maker Xtreme Manufacturing and a 51% stake in Snorkel, which manufactures aerial work platforms and lifts.
abouts: A diehard Republican, Ahern briefly served as finance chair for the Nevada State Republican party.
His Ahern Luxury Boutique Hotel in Las Vegas has become a go-to venue for state and national conservatives to hold events.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Bill Cummings founded commercial real estate developer Cummings Properties in 1970 in Woburn, Massachusetts.
The company manages 11 million square feet of office buildings in the suburbs of Boston; Bill has donated many of the buildings to the charitable Cummings Foundation.
He still owns office complexes in the Boston suburbs, including the Cummings Center in Beverly and TradeCenter 128 in Woburn.
Bill and his wife Joyce joined the Giving Pledge in 2011; the couple are generous donors to groups in the Boston area and in Rwanda.
In 2004, the couple's foundation agreed to operate Tuft University's Veterinary School, contributing $80 million over two decades.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Co-founder of Turkey's largest provider of mobile service, Murat Vargi has diversified into real estate and hotels, startups and renewable energy.
Although having divested most all of his Turkcell stake, he has 80% of KVK, a mobile phone distributor supplying a retail network with 1,000+ outlets.
Dost Energy, of which Vargi's owns 51%, has found success by focusing exclusively on producing power from wind.
Vargi is an active venture investor. In 2015, Gedik Yatırım and Vargi's MV Holding opened a startup hub in Istanbul, StartersHub.
Among his venture investments is a 20% stake in PayCore, focused on payment systems services and solutions, plus fraud detection and prevention.
abouts: Vargi started his career working as an export representative with Koc Holdings, founded by one of Turkey's leading business families.
Turkcell and KVK are among Turkey's most recognized brands.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lu Zhongfang retired from a pesticides factory in northern China's Jilin Province in 1993 and invested in test preparation firm Offcn in 1999.
Lu's son Liu Yongxin chairs Offcn and is also a billionaire.
Offcn Education Technology completed a backdoor listing at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2019.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Qiangxiang chairs CoCreation Grass, or CCGrass, the self-described largest synthetic turf supplier in the world.
CCGrass is used for athletic and landscape purposes.
CCGrass supplies sports organizations including FIFA, FIH, World Rugby, GAA and ITF.
CCGrass was founded by Wang Qiangxiang and his brother Wang Qiangzhong in 2004 in Nanjing.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Jiangsu Haili Wind Power Equipment Technology

bios: Xu Shijun is the founder of Jiangsu Haili Wind Power Equipment, a China supplier of wind power generation equipment.
Haili went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2021.
China leads the world in installed wind power generation capacity, according to the World Population Review.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Thor Bjorgolfsson owns stakes in such businesses as Swiss pharmaceutical company Xantis and Chilean telecom WOM.
Bjorgolfsson also has investments in cryptocurrencies and startups Zwift, Deliveroo and Stripe.
Bjorgolfsson made his first fortune in the wilds of Russia, cofounding Bravo brewery and creating the popular Botchkarov beer brand.
He sold it to Heineken in 2002 and used the proceeds to go on a buying spree in his native Iceland and Eastern Europe.
He lost nearly all of his fortune when Iceland nearly went bankrupt in 2008 and he had to find a way to pay off more than $1 billion in debt.
abouts: His great-grandfather Thor Jensen was one of Iceland's first entrepreneurs, who survived bankruptcy twice and was later one of Iceland's largest landowners.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Xie Bingkun chairs Fujian Kuncai Material Technology, a supplier of coating materials.
Fujian Kuncai Material Technology went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
Xie founded the predecessor of Kuncai in 2005.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Hunan Dakang Pasture farming Co. Ltd.
Hunan Dakang Pasture farming Co. Ltd.

bios: Jiang Zhaobai chairs Shanghai Pengxin Group, whose businesses include real estate, financial services and agribusiness.
Jiang founded Shanghai Pengxin Group in 1988.
Jiang graduated from Nanjing Institute of Architecture and Civil Engineering and the China Europe International Business School.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sergey Shnayder is the founder of Svetofor Group, a discount supermarket chain in Russia.
Svetofor Group has more than 2,000 supermarkets under the Svetofor and Mayak brands.
Shnayder got his start in the 1990s as a distributor of beer and low-alcoholic beverages.
In 2004, with partners, Shnayder started a new business, launching a chain of stores that primarily sold beer.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Liang Wenfeng is the founder of Hangzhou, China-based AI firm DeepSeek and quantitative trading firm High-Flyer Capital Management.
DeepSeek took the world by storm when it released its R1 model in January 2025, claiming to rival the performance of OpenAI's ChatGPT at a lower cost.
Liang launched DeepSeek in 2023 and funded it in part with proceeds from High-Flyer, the hedge fund he founded in 2015 with two college classmates.
Liang used math and AI techniques to build High-Flyer, and by 2019 it was one of the largest and best-performing quantitative trading firms in China.
High-Flyer reached a peak of $14 billion in assets under management in 2021. The firm's performance then declined and assets fell to around $6 billion.
abouts: Liang met with Chinese president Xi Jinping at a meeting with Chinese tech entrepreneurs in Beijing in February 2025.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Descendant of the storied Bangur clan of Kolkata, Krishna Kumar Bangur is the chairman of Graphite India, a maker of graphite electrodes.
The company was set up in 1962 in collaboration with Great Lakes Carbon, an American firm.
The company supplies leading steelmakers in India and overseas.
abouts: Bangur joined the business at the age of 16.
Graphite India has featured in Forbes Asia's list of Best Under A Billion companies.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Kenneth Tuchman is the founder and CEO of customer care outsourcing giant TTEC, a public company operating on six continents.
Tuchman's personal frustration with the way businesses approached customer service led him to found the company in 1982.
Today, Tuchman is the majority owner of the $2.4 billion (revenue) company, which handles customer inquiries via phone, messaging and social media.
Tuchman originally studied architecture at a junior college and dropped out to pursue his own business ventures.
abouts: As a teenager, Tuchman sold millions of puka shell necklaces to retailers, becoming one of the largest shell importers from the Philippines.
Most of Tuchman's international call centers are located in the Philippines.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Pedro Grendene Bartelle cofounded Grendene, one of the world's largest sandal manufacturers, with his twin brother Alexandre Grendene Bartelle.
Pedro is vice-chairman of the board of directors of Grendene SA. and owns just under 14% of Sao Paulo-listed Grendene SA.
He invests in other businesses, including footwear company Vulcabras Azaleia, a direct competitor to Grendene in which he holds a controlling stake.
abouts: Pedro is married to Tania Bulhoes, a Brazilian entrepreneur who owns Tania Bulhoes Perfumes Ltda., a well known retailer of perfumes, creams and soaps.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Takanori Nakamura is the founder and CEO of cloud software firm Rakus, which offers cloud-based solutions for small and midsized business.
Rakus was founded in 2000 and went public in 2015.
The company's flagship product is its expense management software, Rakuraku Seisan.
Nakamura has a stated ambition of making Rakus one of the top 100 listed enterprises in Japan by 2030 in terms of market capitalization.
abouts: Nakamura joined Nippon Telegraph and Telephone in 1996 and then established Digital Network Service in 1997 before founding Rakus in 2000.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Madeleine Olsson-Eriksson is a part owner of Stena Sphere, a privately held Swedish conglomerate.
Interests include cruising, shipping, offshore drilling, property and metal recycling.
Madeleine's father, Sten, founded Stena in 1939 as a trading company.
Her brother Dan took over in 1983 and now owns 51% of the company. Madeleine and her brother Stefan Olsson own 12.5% and 24.5%, respectively.
Madeleine's children, Gustav and Marie, each own 6%  and have seats on different boards in the company.
abouts: She became the first of her family to go to college, earning a degree in medicine and pursuing a career as a gynecologist.
Aside from an 12.5% stake in Stena, she is also part owner of a clinic in Gothenburg.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zhang Jianguo chairs Jovo Energy, a Chinese distributor of natural gas.
Jovo was founded in the southern Chinese city of Zhuhai in 1990.
Jovo's international partners include Petronas from Malaysia and the Skaugen Group from Norway.
Jovo went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alan Rydge is chairman and shareholder of cinema, hotel and ski-resort group Event Hospitality & Entertainment, formerly Amalgamated Holdings.
He inherited the Greater Union cinema chain after his father died in 1980.
He's also chairman and the major shareholder of investment firm Carlton Investments.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Lee Seung-gun is the founder and CEO of Viva Republica, which operates the Korean finance app Toss.
In 2021, Viva Republica raised more than $400 million in a financing round that valued the company at over $7 billion.
Viva Republica's investors include PayPal, Singapore sovereign-wealth fund GIC and venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins.
Before starting Viva Republica in 2013, Lee was a dentist at a hospital affiliated with the Samsung Group.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Son of a rickshaw driver, Lim Chap Huat set up a small construction outfit with two partners in 1976 at age 22.
He expanded Soilbuild Group into property development and set up an REIT, eventually buying out his partners. His wife Leo Jee Lin and sons, Lim Han Feng and Lim Han Qin, work with him.
Soilbuild expanded into Myanmar in 2012 where it has multiple contracts, and into Vietnam in 2017.
In 2021, Lim, together with Blackstone Real Estate, privatized Soilbuild Business Space REIT, delisting it from the Singapore stock exchange.
In Auguest 2024, Lim and Blackstone sold their office and industrial properties in Singapore to New York-based private equity firm Warburg Pincus and Australian developer Lendlease for $1.2 billion.
abouts: Lim taught part-time to pay fees for engineering school.
He is a firm believer in his school motto "Nothing Without Labour."

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires

financialAssets.companyName: Muyuan Foodstuff Co., Ltd. Class A
Muyuan Foodstuff Co., Ltd. Class A

bios: Qian is a co-founder and director of Shenzhen-listed pig breeder Muyuan Foods, one of the world's largest pig breeders.
She is married to Muyuan chairman Qin Yinglin, with whom she co-founded the company in 1992 at age 26.
The couple started out with 22 pigs.
Qian is a graduate of the Henan University of Animal Husbandry Economy.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Hotelier Jasminder Singh's Edwardian Hotels London group owns 12 high-end hotels in London and Manchester, including The May Fair Hotel.
Singh purchased his first hotel, The Edwardian, in 1975 for about $750,000.
In 1993 he partnered with Radisson; 11 of the group's hotels are now branded Radisson Blu Edwardian.
The group's $400 million luxury development at Leicester Square, The Londoner hotel, opened in the fall of 2021.
Singh's wife, Amrit, son, Inderneel, and daughters, Siraj and Krishma, all hold senior positions with Edwardian Hotels London.
abouts: Singh grew up in Tanzania and Kenya before moving to the UK and qualifying as an accountant.
Singh's father took him to court in 2012 claiming part of his son's fortune under Sikh culture of sharing wealth among generations. The court ruled for Jasminder.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: One of Wall Street's macro-trading legends, Louis Bacon cut his teeth as a commodities and currencies trader, earning big profits in the 1987 crash.
He created hedge fund Moore Capital in 1989 using trading profits and a small inheritance.
Bacon announced he was closing his hedge fund and returning outside investors' money in November 2019, citing years of "disappointing results."
Moore Capital still manages internal money and scored 70% returns in 2020 for Bacon and his employees.
abouts: Bacon's environmental preservation-focused Moore Charitable Trust was defrauded out of $25 million by jailed banker Andy Caspersen.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Neerja Sethi cofounded IT consulting and outsourcing firm Syntel with her husband Bharat Desai in 1980 and took it public in 1997.
French IT firm Atos SE bought Syntel for $3.4 billion in 2018. Sethi got an estimated $510 million for her stake.
Sethi served as an executive at Syntel from its founding until its sale in 2018.
Her husband Bharat Desai is also a billionaire; they met in the U.S. while working for IT firm Tata Consultancy Services.
The couple started Syntel in their apartment in Troy, Michigan with an initial investment of just $2,000.
abouts: Sethi holds an undergraduate degree in mathematics and a masters degree in computer science.
She and her husband joined the Giving Pledge, a commitment to give at least half their fortune to charitable causes, in May 2025.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gennady Kozovoy owns about 6% of publicly traded steel and mining company Evraz.
Kozovoy got Evraz shares when he and his partners sold control of coal miner Raspadskaya to Evraz in 2012.
The London Stock Exchange-listed, $9.8 billion (revenues) company is one of the world's largest steel producers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Itamar Locks is the son-in-law of Brazilian billionaire Lucia Maggi, who cofounded Andre Maggi Group with her husband, Andre Maggi.
Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest producers of soybeans and other commodities.
Lucia Maggi cofounded the business with her husband in 1977 and took over as majority shareholder after he died in 2001.
After Andre Maggi died in 2001, his son Blairo Maggi took over as the chief executive of the company.
Locks is one of the controlling shareholders of Amaggi, along with Lucia Maggi, Blairo Maggi, and Hugo de C. Ribeiro.
abouts: Locks previously served as the president of the agricultural division of Amaggi.
Amaggi produces approximately 1.2 million tons of soy, corn, and cotton in Brazil each year.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Blairo Maggi is the son of Andre Maggi and Lucia Maggi, cofounders of Brazil's Andre Maggi Group.
Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest producers of soybeans and other commodities.
He took over as the chief executive of Amaggi after his father's death in 2001. Although he no longer holds the position, he remains a controlling shareholder.
Maggi has previously served as Brazil's minister of agriculture and the governor of the state of Mato Grasso.
abouts: Maggi was referred to as the "King of Soy" by Brazilian media during his time leading the business.
Amaggi produces approximately 1.2 million tons of soy, corn, and cotton in Brazil each year.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Nigel Austin is the founder and majority owner of the Cotton On clothing and stationery group. Its brands include Cotton On, Supre, Factorie and Typo.
His company has close to 1,300 stores in 17 countries with 2024 revenue of around $1.4 billion.
About half of these stores are in Australia, while the other half are spread across countries such as Singapore, South Africa and the U.S.
Founded in 1991, Austin started selling acid-washed denim jackets from the trunk of his car in his hometown southwest of Melbourne.
Now it sells inexpensive fashion basics, including T-shirts, leggings, sweatpants, shoes and underwear, as well as quirky stationery.
abouts: Austin's late father, Grant Austin, ran a publicly traded clothing wholesale and import business called the Austin Group, where Austin would spend school holidays working.
In 1991 Austin set up his first store in a small space behind a butcher shop run by his grandfather and sourced merchandise from his father.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Wang Miaotong is the chairman of Zhejiang Century Huatong Group, a supplier of auto parts that has diversified into the mobile gaming business.
His son Wang Yifeng is vice chairman of Zhejiang Century Huatong Group.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Zach McLeroy founded the chicken chain Zaxby's with Tony Townley, his best friend since the seventh grade.
Townley and McLeroy each put up $8,000 to open the first Zaxby's restaurant in Statesboro, Georgia in 1990.
In 2020, McLeroy sold 20% of his stake to Goldman Sachs for an estimated $400 million; he still owns 30% of the business.
Townley sold his entire stake in the business to Goldman Sachs at the same time.
McLeroy served as CEO of Zaxby's until 2022; he remains chairman of the board of directors.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Song Chi-hyung is cofounder and chairman of Dunamu, which operates Upbit, South Korea's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volume.
In 2021, Hybe, the agency behind K-pop powerhouse BTS, bought a 2.5% stake in Dunamu in a deal that valued it at $17 billion.
Its investors include Kakao Ventures and Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm Altos Ventures.
Before starting Dunamu, Song worked at local mobile payment company Danal.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Mao Lixiang is the founder of Fotile, one of China's largest kitchen appliance brands.
Son Mao Zhongchun currently chairs the business from its headquarters in the eastern Chinese city of Ningbo.
Fotile's top sellers include kitchen range hoods.
Fotile's rivals include Robam Appliances, led by fellow billionaire Ren Jiahua.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Real estate billionaire Axel Stawski founded Stawski Partners in 1973.
The company owns six office buildings and three condos in Manhattan.
He sold a residential tower project in Queens? Long Island City for $200 million in March 2022.
Stawski was born in post-war Germany to Jewish parents who both survived the Holocaust.
He immigrated to the U.S. in 1971 to attend New York University.
abouts: Stawski is a board member of the American Society for Yad Vashem, which supports the Yad Vashem World Holocaust Remembrance Center in Jerusalem.
Before emigrating to the U.S. with his family in 1971, Stawski's father was a real estate developer in West Germany, focusing on shopping centers.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Alexander Klyachin owns one of the biggest Russian hotel chains, Azimut, which boasts more than 4,300 rooms altogether.
Klyachin earned his fortune largely in Moscow's commercial real estate market and from buying land from collective farmers.
Another Klyachin company, KR Properties, turns factories and plants into business centers and loft projects while keeping their old age exterior.
abouts: Klyachin owns the Metropol hotel, which served as the headquarters of the opposition to the Bolsheviks in 1917.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: David Hindawi cofounded cybersecurity firm Tanium with his son Orion in 2007.
Tanium has raised $800 million from investors who valued it at $6.5 billion in October 2018.
In February 2016, Orion took over as CEO from his father. David is executive chairman.
David, now a U.S. citizen, was born in Baghdad, grew up in Israel, and went to UC Berkeley for a  Ph.D. in operations research.
He previously founded BigFix,an IT software patching system, with help from his son. They sold the company to IBM for $400 million in 2010.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Richard Kurtz is the founder, CEO and controlling shareholder of The Kamson Corporation, a privately held real estate management company.
The Englewood, New Jersey-headquartered Kamson controls 75 multifamily apartment buildings properties, across New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Connecticut and South Dakota.
Kurtz founded Kamson in 1976 after selling his New Jersey-based pizza chain, which had 39 stores. His first property was a 62-unit apartment building in Trenton.
In 2006, Kurtz bought the historic estate of industrialist Henry Clay Frick for $58 million in Alpine, New Jersey, an upscale neighborhood.
Kurtz donated over $230,000 in support of Mehmet Oz's campaign for U.S. Senate in the state of Pennsylvania.
abouts: Kurtz lives in Palm Beach, Florida, just three miles from a home owned by Mehmet Oz and his wife, Lisa Oz.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Stephen Ketchum is founder and CEO of Sound Point Capital Management, a credit asset manager specializing in CLOs that manages $46 billion in assets.
He founded Sound Point in 2008 with backing from Stone Point Capital, a $55 billion private equity firm.
Ketchum previously served as global head of media & telecom investment and corporate banking at Banc of America Securities.
From 1990 to 2000, he was a Managing Director at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
He earned a B.A. from New England College and an M.B.A. from Harvard Business School.
abouts: Ketchum played division III basketball in college.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Jason Murray is the cofounder, chairman and CEO of Utah-based PACS Group, a publicly traded firm that operates skilled nursing facilities.
He cofounded PACS Group with fellow billionaire Mark Hancock in 2013 and the pair took the company public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2024.
PACS Group started with two skilled nursing facilities and has since expanded to 315 facilities in 17 states in the U.S.
Murray and Hancock each owned 50% of PACS Group before the IPO; Murray now owns nearly 35% of the company's shares.
Before starting PACS, Murray worked as a healthcare executive and licensed nursing home administrator.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Shashishekar Pandit is cofounder and chairman of Pune software company KPIT Technologies, which provides software development services to automotive clients.
Apart from India, it has engineering centers in Europe, the U.S., Japan, China and Thailand.
He started KPIT with fellow accountant Kishor Patil in 1990.
abouts: In 2019, Penguin published a book that he co-authored called "Leap frogging to Pole Vaulting: Creating the magic of radical yet sustainable transformation."
He has a masters degree from MIT's Sloan School of Management.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Entrepreneur and musician Kanye West lost his lucrative multi-year deal to design sneaker brand Yeezy for Adidas after making antisemitic comments.
Other brands and companies that cut ties to West, who formally changed his name to Ye, include Gap and Balenciaga.
Forbes had valued the Adidas deal at $1.5 billion. Without it, West's fortune drops to roughly $400 million.
His current fortune includes cash, real estate, the value of his music catalog and a 5% stake in his ex-wife Kim Kardashian's shapewear brand Skims.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Elizabeth Holmes dropped out of Stanford University and founded blood testing startup Theranos in 2003, with the aim of using just a few drops of blood.
Theranos raised more than $700 million from investors (including from billionaires Rupert Murdoch and Larry Ellison), who valued the company at $9 billion.
Forbes named Holmes the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire--worth $4.5 billion--in 2014, when she was 30 years old.
Starting in 2015, Theranos' technology came into question; reporting by The Wall Street Journal revealed that Theranos was using other companies' machines.
Forbes revised our net worth estimate for Holmes to $0 in June 2016 amid new information and as the company faced a slew of investigations from federal agencies.
On January 3, 2022, Holmes was found guilty of four out of 11 charges of fraud; she was acquitted on four charges; the jury failed to reach a verdict on 3 counts.
Holmes reported to a low-security women's prison in Texas in late May 2023 to begin serving a sentence of more than 11 years.
abouts: In 2018, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission charged Holmes and with fraud; Holmes settled charges, paid a $500,000 fine and gave up her shares in Theranos.
Other wealthy investors in Theranos included New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft, members of Walmart's Walton family and the DeVos family, heirs to Amway.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Gary Wang was a cryptocurrency billionaire until the empire he built with Sam Bankman-Fried imploded in November 2022.
Wang cofounded crypto exchange FTX and helped grow it into a leading marketplace for buying and selling crypto derivatives.
Wang pled guilty to two counts of wire fraud, one count of securities fraud, and one count of commodities fraud in Dec. 2022
An MIT grad, Wang worked at Google, building systems to aggregate prices across millions of flights, before linking up with Bankman-Fried to launch trading firm Alameda Research and FTX.
Wang, who first met SBF at math camp during high school, is expected to cooperate with prosecutors against his friend.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Rene Benko is the founder of Signa Holding, once one of Europe's largest real estate and retail firms until a 2023 credit crunch wiped much of Signa's equity.
Benko fell from the billionaire ranking in December 2023 after his main holdings - Signa Prime, Signa Development and Signa Holding - declared insolvency.
Benko's personal assets - including a yacht, art and property - were not part of the 2023 insolvency proceedings. They are not included in the net worth estimate.
Benko worked for a real estate developer in high school, racking up so many absences that he couldn't graduate. He began his investment career at 22.
In 2018, Benko jumped into the media industry and the following year purchased a stake in New York City's Chrysler Building.
abouts: Former Formula One world champion Niki Lauda, who died in 2019, was a significant shareholder of Signa.
In 2018, Signa created its own venture capital firm, Signa Innovation, which invests in startups.

personsLists.name: Real-Time Billionaires
bios: Sam Bankman-Fried was one of the richest people in crypto, thanks to his FTX exchange and Alameda Research trading firm, before his empire came crashing down in November 2022.
After users began withdrawing their investments from FTX at a rapid pace, Bankman-Fried filed for bankruptcy for FTX, FTX's U.S. operations and Alameda Research.
On Dec. 13, 2022, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York charged Bankman-Fried in an eight-count indictment with fraud, money laundering, and campaign finance offenses.
Prosecutors added a charge in March for Bankman-Fried's alleged $40 million bribe paid to a Chinese official. His trial is set to begin in October 2023.
The son of two Stanford law professors, he graduated with a degree in physics from MIT in 2014 before starting his career at Wall Street trading firm Jane Street Capital.
Bankman-Fried's wealth peaked in early 2022 at an estimated $26.5 billion, most of which was tied up in his ownership of FTX and a share of its FTT tokens.
abouts: Bankman-Fried poured hundreds of millions into mainstream marketing, including the naming rights to leading esports league TSM and the Miami Heat's arena.
Bankman-Fried was the second largest billionaire donor to Democratic causes in the 2022 midterm election, giving nearly $40 million.
